name: Nobodywho
description: Nobodywho runs AI on your own devices and servers. Its open-source inference engine ships SDKs for Rust, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, React Native and Godot, so you can run models locally with no per-token costs, no data leaving the machine and no dependency on an internet connection.
description_en: Nobodywho runs AI on your own devices and servers. Its open-source inference engine ships SDKs for Rust, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, React Native and Godot, so you can run models locally with no per-token costs, no data leaving the machine and no dependency on an internet connection.

use_cases.title: Ship inference inside an app
use_cases.detail: Embed local model calls in desktop, mobile or game builds through a language SDK.

use_cases.title: Keep sensitive data in house
use_cases.detail: Run models on-premises for data that is not allowed to leave your network.

use_cases.title: Build offline features
use_cases.detail: Offer AI features that keep working with no internet connection.

pros: No per-token costs and no vendor lock-in
Auditable engine released under an open source licence
Broad SDK coverage across languages and platforms
cons: You are responsible for model choice, hardware and updates
Enterprise support is a separate commercial offering

name: Ollaya
description: Ollaya downloads and serves open decision models on your own machine. You ask typed questions about any text or JSON, the model scores the options you define and returns the top answer with calibrated scores in milliseconds, privately and on your own hardware.
description_en: Ollaya downloads and serves open decision models on your own machine. You ask typed questions about any text or JSON, the model scores the options you define and returns the top answer with calibrated scores in milliseconds, privately and on your own hardware.

use_cases.title: Classify support mail
use_cases.detail: Score incoming messages for intent, urgency and tone without sending them anywhere.

use_cases.title: Get typed answers
use_cases.detail: Ask structured questions with fixed options instead of parsing free-form text.

use_cases.title: Run it in a pipeline
use_cases.detail: Call the CLI from shell scripts and batch jobs as a scoring step.

pros: Typed, calibrated output instead of prose you have to parse
Runs locally with no network dependency
Open source and independent of the vendors it borrows ideas from
cons: Limited to the decision models in its catalogue
Local inference speed depends on your hardware

name: Cloudflare cf CLI
description: cf is Cloudflare agentic CLI for the whole Cloudflare API. Commands are discoverable through built-in search and steering so an agent can find the command it needs, JSON is the default interface, pretty printed for humans and condensed for agents to save context, and cloudflare.config.ts becomes the single configuration format for the platform.
description_en: cf is Cloudflare agentic CLI for the whole Cloudflare API. Commands are discoverable through built-in search and steering so an agent can find the command it needs, JSON is the default interface, pretty printed for humans and condensed for agents to save context, and cloudflare.config.ts becomes the single configuration format for the platform.

use_cases.title: Let an agent drive your account
use_cases.detail: Expose the whole Cloudflare API to an agent through commands it can discover itself.

use_cases.title: Save context on output
use_cases.detail: Get condensed JSON for agents and readable output for humans from the same commands.

use_cases.title: Unify configuration
use_cases.detail: Move to a single cloudflare.config.ts instead of scattered per-service config.

pros: Built for agents first, with search and steering baked in
JSON-native interface reduces parsing glue code
Official Cloudflare project covering the full API
cons: Only useful if you already run on Cloudflare
Replaces habits built around the older Wrangler workflow

name: Imp
description: Imp is a full port of DSPy to the BEAM. You describe what each language-model step takes and returns, choose how it thinks, and let an optimizer improve the program against examples of what good looks like, giving you signatures, modules, optimizers, agent loops and retrieval with the concurrency and reliability of OTP.
description_en: Imp is a full port of DSPy to the BEAM. You describe what each language-model step takes and returns, choose how it thinks, and let an optimizer improve the program against examples of what good looks like, giving you signatures, modules, optimizers, agent loops and retrieval with the concurrency and reliability of OTP.

use_cases.title: Write declarative LM programs
use_cases.detail: Describe inputs and outputs per step rather than hand-writing prompts.

use_cases.title: Optimize against examples
use_cases.detail: Let an optimizer tune the program using examples of good output.

use_cases.title: Run it on OTP
use_cases.detail: Get agent loops and retrieval supervised by the BEAM runtime.

pros: Brings the DSPy programming model to Elixir and Erlang teams
Concurrency and supervision come from OTP rather than bolted-on plumbing
Optimizers mean less manual prompt tuning
cons: Requires Elixir and willingness to think in signatures
Smaller ecosystem than the Python original

name: Konnect
description: Konnect brings AI-assisted PCB design to KiCad 10. It is a native KiCad plugin, a single Rust binary, that exposes hundreds of schematic, layout, routing, placement, design-review and manufacturing tools to Claude or the model of your choice over the Model Context Protocol, grouped into on-demand toolsets.
description_en: Konnect brings AI-assisted PCB design to KiCad 10. It is a native KiCad plugin, a single Rust binary, that exposes hundreds of schematic, layout, routing, placement, design-review and manufacturing tools to Claude or the model of your choice over the Model Context Protocol, grouped into on-demand toolsets.

use_cases.title: Capture a schematic by asking
use_cases.detail: Have an assistant place parts and wire a schematic from a description.

use_cases.title: Audit before fabrication
use_cases.detail: Run ERC, DRC and design-review checks through the same conversational interface.

use_cases.title: Search parts in context
use_cases.detail: Look up distributor parts and reference circuits without leaving KiCad.

pros: Deep KiCad coverage rather than a thin wrapper
Toolsets load on demand so the model context stays manageable
Model-agnostic over MCP
cons: Beta release tied to KiCad 10
Hardware work still needs a human to sanity-check the result

name: JetBrains Air
description: JetBrains Air is one system for building software with agents. It works with the agents you already use, Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot, OpenCode and anything you can connect over ACP, and gives you tasks, automations and projects you can drive from JetBrains IDEs, the web, the CLI or a phone.
description_en: JetBrains Air is one system for building software with agents. It works with the agents you already use, Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot, OpenCode and anything you can connect over ACP, and gives you tasks, automations and projects you can drive from JetBrains IDEs, the web, the CLI or a phone.

use_cases.title: Keep your existing agent
use_cases.detail: Bring Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot or OpenCode into one task system.

use_cases.title: Automate the chores
use_cases.detail: Set up automations such as rebasing a branch or updating agent instructions on merge.

use_cases.title: Work from anywhere
use_cases.detail: Drive the same projects from an IDE, a browser, a terminal or mobile.

pros: Agent-agnostic through the ACP protocol
Spans IDE, web, CLI and mobile rather than one surface
Tasks, automations and projects share one model
cons: Commercial product with a credit-based pricing model
Most valuable if you already live in JetBrains tooling

name: PatchWave
description: PatchWave is a GitHub app that automatically analyzes, fixes and merges your Dependabot pull requests. Its agent checks each dependency update against your code and repairs what breaks, so dependency bumps stop piling up in the review queue.
description_en: PatchWave is a GitHub app that automatically analyzes, fixes and merges your Dependabot pull requests. Its agent checks each dependency update against your code and repairs what breaks, so dependency bumps stop piling up in the review queue.

use_cases.title: Clear the PR backlog
use_cases.detail: Let an agent work the queue of dependency bumps instead of a human.

use_cases.title: Fix what the bump broke
use_cases.detail: Check the update against your code and repair the fallout before merging.

use_cases.title: Keep the audit trail
use_cases.detail: Every merge arrives as a normal pull request with its analysis attached.

pros: Attacks a queue almost every team has given up on
Free tier covers a monthly allowance of merged PRs
Installs as a GitHub app with no pipeline rewrite
cons: Merging automatically needs trust in the analysis
Focused on Dependabot rather than other update sources

name: MirrorMD
description: MirrorMD is a facial analysis built by a cosmetic surgeon. It measures your face the way a consultation does and tells you which treatments may suit you, which would waste your money and which could harm you, before you spend anything on them.
description_en: MirrorMD is a facial analysis built by a cosmetic surgeon. It measures your face the way a consultation does and tells you which treatments may suit you, which would waste your money and which could harm you, before you spend anything on them.

use_cases.title: Screen the treatment first
use_cases.detail: Get an opinion on whether a procedure suits your face before booking it.

use_cases.title: Avoid the wasted spend
use_cases.detail: Find out which popular treatments would do nothing for you.

use_cases.title: Hear the risks
use_cases.detail: Learn which options carry harm rather than benefit in your case.

pros: Written by a practising cosmetic surgeon rather than a generic beauty quiz
Explicitly willing to say a treatment is a bad idea
Positioned before you spend money, not after
cons: Paid analysis, not a free checker
Advice from a tool is not a substitute for an in-person examination

name: Worklicant
description: Worklicant is a tech hiring platform where AI reads every resume and ranks your applicants. You share one apply link, it scores each applicant against the job, hides spam and fake resumes, and auto-rejects people who fail your deal-breaker, while candidates book their own interviews.
description_en: Worklicant is a tech hiring platform where AI reads every resume and ranks your applicants. You share one apply link, it scores each applicant against the job, hides spam and fake resumes, and auto-rejects people who fail your deal-breaker, while candidates book their own interviews.

use_cases.title: Post once, share everywhere
use_cases.detail: Put a single apply link on LinkedIn, job boards and your careers page.

use_cases.title: Rank by fit
use_cases.detail: See applicants sorted by a score against the role instead of arrival order.

use_cases.title: Filter the noise
use_cases.detail: Hide spam, fake resumes and anyone who fails a deal-breaker you set.

pros: Pay per vacancy rather than a monthly seat subscription
Unlimited team members on a posting
Candidates self-schedule interviews
cons: Newest entrant in a crowded applicant-tracking field
Automated rejection needs care to avoid filtering out good candidates

name: Tori
description: Tori is an AI support agent for customer success teams, built on TalkJS messaging infrastructure. It learns your product from the help docs, product pages and company knowledge you already have, then answers even complex customer questions through a UI you can customize, handing off to a human with full context when a customer needs one.
description_en: Tori is an AI support agent for customer success teams, built on TalkJS messaging infrastructure. It learns your product from the help docs, product pages and company knowledge you already have, then answers even complex customer questions through a UI you can customize, handing off to a human with full context when a customer needs one.

use_cases.title: Answer from what you published
use_cases.detail: Point it at your URL and let it answer from your own documentation.

use_cases.title: Keep your branding
use_cases.detail: Customize the support UI instead of embedding someone else widget.

use_cases.title: Escalate cleanly
use_cases.detail: Hand a conversation to a human with the history attached.

pros: Built on production messaging infrastructure with real delivery and history
Setup starts from a URL rather than a data migration
Customizable front end
cons: Best for teams whose answers already exist in documentation
Pricing is not published up front

name: Invofox
description: Invofox turns invoices, payslips, contracts and other documents into structured JSON through one API. You pay only for pages it extracts correctly, and the extraction keeps learning from corrections you make.
description_en: Invofox turns invoices, payslips, contracts and other documents into structured JSON through one API. You pay only for pages it extracts correctly, and the extraction keeps learning from corrections you make.

use_cases.title: Replace the template zoo
use_cases.detail: Extract fields from any document layout through one endpoint.

use_cases.title: Pay for correct pages
use_cases.detail: Get billed only on pages the extraction got right.

use_cases.title: Improve over time
use_cases.detail: Feed corrections back so recurring layouts get cleaner.

pros: Single API across invoices, payslips and contracts
Billing tied to correct extractions rather than raw volume
Continuous learning from corrections
cons: Commercial API, so documents leave your infrastructure
Correct-page billing model is unusual and worth reading carefully

name: Layout
description: Layout lets you order food from any restaurant using AI. It connects Claude and ChatGPT to real ordering, so your assistant can place the order end to end, and it exposes a developer console and merchant dashboard for building on top of the same rails.
description_en: Layout lets you order food from any restaurant using AI. It connects Claude and ChatGPT to real ordering, so your assistant can place the order end to end, and it exposes a developer console and merchant dashboard for building on top of the same rails.

use_cases.title: Order through your assistant
use_cases.detail: Ask Claude or ChatGPT to place a real food order rather than just find a restaurant.

use_cases.title: Connect a platform
use_cases.detail: Add a connector so an agent can transact on an existing delivery service.

use_cases.title: Build on the rails
use_cases.detail: Use the developer console to integrate ordering into your own product.

pros: One of the first attempts at real agent-side commerce rather than recommendations
Has both developer and merchant sides from the start
Explicit model of delegated spending authority
cons: Availability depends on participating merchants
Handing spending authority to an agent needs trust in the limits you set

name: Jurl
description: Jurl is curl for pages you want read rather than fetched. You tell it what you want from a URL and it scrapes with intent, returning only what you asked for word for word, and following links when the answer sits several pages away.
description_en: Jurl is curl for pages you want read rather than fetched. You tell it what you want from a URL and it scrapes with intent, returning only what you asked for word for word, and following links when the answer sits several pages away.

use_cases.title: Ask instead of grep
use_cases.detail: Describe the value you want and get it back rather than a document to parse.

use_cases.title: Follow the trail
use_cases.detail: Let it walk links when the fact you need is not on the first page.

use_cases.title: Keep it scriptable
use_cases.detail: Use it as a command line step in shell pipelines and agent tools.

pros: Returns the answer, not the page
Follows links when the target is pages away
Fits naturally into a terminal workflow
cons: Depends on a model call per query
Accuracy on long trails still needs a human eye

name: AgentSocialX
description: AgentSocialX is a Second Brain Network. You start your second brain from LinkedIn and X, then use the network to get answers and opinions from other peoples second brains and to set up one-on-ones. The pitch is that your AI keeps learning from the network while your own thinking gets found by the right mind.
description_en: AgentSocialX is a Second Brain Network. You start your second brain from LinkedIn and X, then use the network to get answers and opinions from other peoples second brains and to set up one-on-ones. The pitch is that your AI keeps learning from the network while your own thinking gets found by the right mind.

use_cases.title: Seed it from your profiles
use_cases.detail: Build a second brain starting from what you already posted on LinkedIn and X.

use_cases.title: Ask people, not feeds
use_cases.detail: Get answers and opinions from other members second brains.

use_cases.title: Turn matches into calls
use_cases.detail: Move from a shared interest to a one-on-one conversation.

pros: Focuses on connecting people through their notes rather than follower counts
Imports from profiles you already have
Public counters make network activity visible
cons: Value depends on who else joins
Handing your notes to a network means thinking about what you publish there

name: Plannotator
description: Plannotator is free, open-source review tooling for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi and Droid. You review an agent plan before it executes, annotate agent-written code in a full diff viewer, and send structured feedback straight back to the agent, all running locally. Its Inbox collects your agents questions, plans and reviews in one window.
description_en: Plannotator is free, open-source review tooling for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi and Droid. You review an agent plan before it executes, annotate agent-written code in a full diff viewer, and send structured feedback straight back to the agent, all running locally. Its Inbox collects your agents questions, plans and reviews in one window.

use_cases.title: Read the plan first
use_cases.detail: Inspect and edit what an agent intends to do before it touches the repository.

use_cases.title: Annotate the diff
use_cases.detail: Comment on agent-written code in a viewer rather than in a chat log.

use_cases.title: Answer from one window
use_cases.detail: Use the Inbox to handle questions, plans and reviews from several agents.

pros: Free and open source, running locally rather than as a hosted service
Works across several agent CLIs instead of one
Feedback goes back to the agent in structured form
cons: Adds a deliberate pause to agent workflows
Local-only means no shared review with a team by default

name: Daydream Studio
description: Daydream Studio is a hybrid recording studio in the browser for crafting and producing music. You generate or record a part, add live session-player tracks over it, and reshape the parts as they play. The page also exposes a scriptable interface so agents can drive the studio directly.
description_en: Daydream Studio is a hybrid recording studio in the browser for crafting and producing music. You generate or record a part, add live session-player tracks over it, and reshape the parts as they play. The page also exposes a scriptable interface so agents can drive the studio directly.

use_cases.title: Build a track in the browser
use_cases.detail: Generate or record a part without installing a DAW.

use_cases.title: Add real players
use_cases.detail: Layer live session-player tracks over what you generated.

use_cases.title: Let an agent drive it
use_cases.detail: Script the studio through its exposed interface for agent-driven sessions.

pros: Combines generated parts with human session playing
Runs in a browser tab with no install
Scriptable surface makes it usable by agents
cons: Best on a desktop rather than a phone
Output quality still depends on your own ear and editing

name: Reduck
description: Reduck is an MCP server that lets your agent create and run reusable automation scripts for the web. Instead of reasoning through every click, the agent writes or reuses a script that returns the same structured output each time, runs in your own Chrome, and burns no tokens while it executes.
description_en: Reduck is an MCP server that lets your agent create and run reusable automation scripts for the web. Instead of reasoning through every click, the agent writes or reuses a script that returns the same structured output each time, runs in your own Chrome, and burns no tokens while it executes.

use_cases.title: Make the web deterministic
use_cases.detail: Turn a flaky click-by-click task into a script with a clear contract.

use_cases.title: Stop paying per step
use_cases.detail: Run scripts that cost no tokens and do not grow the context window.

use_cases.title: Reuse across sites
use_cases.detail: Keep a library of scripts the agent can call on any website.

pros: Scripts return consistent structured output instead of varying per run
Runs in your own Chrome with your own logged-in sessions
Ships ready-made scripts for common sites
cons: Someone still has to write or fix the script when a site changes
Hosted MCP service rather than a local-only tool

name: Datastory
description: Datastory is a no-code platform for data storytellers. You upload your own data or search a curated catalog of open datasets, then build interactive charts, websites and reports with its Studio, CMS and AI features.
description_en: Datastory is a no-code platform for data storytellers. You upload your own data or search a curated catalog of open datasets, then build interactive charts, websites and reports with its Studio, CMS and AI features.

use_cases.title: Start from your own file
use_cases.detail: Upload a spreadsheet and turn it into an interactive chart or report.

use_cases.title: Or start from open data
use_cases.detail: Search a catalog of curated open datasets instead of sourcing your own.

use_cases.title: Publish the result
use_cases.detail: Use the CMS to turn charts into a website rather than a static image.

pros: No-code path from raw data to a published story
Bundles a catalog of open datasets to start from
Studio, CMS and AI features in one product
cons: Aimed at storytellers rather than analysts needing deep statistics
Commercial platform with tiered plans

name: Privatemode
description: Privatemode is a confidential AI service that protects your data end to end. Using confidential computing, it encrypts your data before it leaves your device and keeps it protected even while the model is processing it, including inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
description_en: Privatemode is a confidential AI service that protects your data end to end. Using confidential computing, it encrypts your data before it leaves your device and keeps it protected even while the model is processing it, including inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint.

use_cases.title: Use AI on sensitive files
use_cases.detail: Work with documents that are not allowed to be exposed to a model provider.

use_cases.title: Keep Office in the loop
use_cases.detail: Get AI help inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint with the same protection.

use_cases.title: Prove it technically
use_cases.detail: Rely on confidential computing isolation rather than a contractual promise.

pros: Encryption holds during processing, not only in transit
Extends to the Office tools people actually work in
Aimed at regulated and security-conscious teams
cons: Commercial service you have to evaluate and trust
Protection depends on the attestation model behind it

name: Feyn
description: Feyn is a platform for training custom models on your own data. It keeps learning in production, serves faster and cheaper inference, and lets you own the weights. Its open-source releases include MultiMatte and FeyNoBg, models for promptable image background removal.
description_en: Feyn is a platform for training custom models on your own data. It keeps learning in production, serves faster and cheaper inference, and lets you own the weights. Its open-source releases include MultiMatte and FeyNoBg, models for promptable image background removal.

use_cases.title: Train on your own examples
use_cases.detail: Build a model around your data instead of prompting a general one.

use_cases.title: Keep improving after launch
use_cases.detail: Let the model keep learning once it is in production.

use_cases.title: Cut the background
use_cases.detail: Use its open matting models for promptable image background removal.

pros: You own the weights rather than renting a behaviour
Production learning loop rather than a one-off fine-tune
Open source model releases alongside the platform
cons: Platform is commercially oriented; pricing is not published
Training and serving your own models needs ML ops maturity

name: LayerFS
description: LayerFS is a filesystem built for AI coding agents. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so ephemeral workspaces still leave durable results. It is designed for massive parallelism and multi-agent coordination across branches.
description_en: LayerFS is a filesystem built for AI coding agents. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so ephemeral workspaces still leave durable results. It is designed for massive parallelism and multi-agent coordination across branches.

use_cases.title: Give every command its own workspace
use_cases.detail: Each Bash tool call mounts an ephemeral workspace, then commits, so an agent cannot leave a half-finished tree behind.

use_cases.title: Share history without a database
use_cases.detail: Agents on different computers commit to one serverless store, with no DB server in the middle.

use_cases.title: Run many agents on one project
use_cases.detail: Every tool call becomes a commit on a branch, so conflicts on the same file are recorded and traceable.

pros: Durable shared history even though each workspace is ephemeral
No database server needed for agents to share state
Per-call commits make multi-agent conflicts traceable
cons: A new storage layer to learn and operate under your agent stack
Conflicts on the same file still need to be resolved by someone

name: Alter
description: Alter is privileged access management for AI agents. It keeps OAuth tokens and managed API keys in a credential vault, applies a default-deny policy engine down to the individual parameter, gives every agent its own identity with delegation and IdP integration, and holds sensitive calls until a named person approves them.
description_en: Alter is privileged access management for AI agents. It keeps OAuth tokens and managed API keys in a credential vault, applies a default-deny policy engine down to the individual parameter, gives every agent its own identity with delegation and IdP integration, and holds sensitive calls until a named person approves them.

use_cases.title: Control what an agent can do per call
use_cases.detail: Policy is evaluated on the actual request, including identity, scope and rate limit, before it is approved.

use_cases.title: Keep provider credentials away from the model
use_cases.detail: Tokens live in the vault and are refreshed there, so the agent never holds the raw secret.

use_cases.title: Make a human approve the risky calls
use_cases.detail: Sensitive calls wait for a named person instead of firing the moment the agent asks.

pros: Default-deny policy down to the parameter level
Tamper-evident audit record with evidence on demand
Per-agent identity, delegation and IdP integration
cons: Sits in the request path, so it adds a hop to every agent call
Getting value out of it means wiring up each provider you use

name: Omnara
description: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform and a self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API. You describe an agent in an agent.yaml file with its instruction, model provider and machine pool, then the API runs it on any model and any machine with tools, secrets, permissions and streaming built in.
description_en: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform and a self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API. You describe an agent in an agent.yaml file with its instruction, model provider and machine pool, then the API runs it on any model and any machine with tools, secrets, permissions and streaming built in.

use_cases.title: Run agents on any model and any machine
use_cases.detail: One API drives agents across model providers and the machine pools you point it at.

use_cases.title: Self-host the whole platform
use_cases.detail: Apache 2.0 means you can run it yourself for free instead of depending on a hosted agents API.

use_cases.title: Stream agent output into your own UI
use_cases.detail: Streaming, tools, secrets and permissions are part of the platform rather than things you bolt on.

pros: Apache 2.0 and explicitly built to be self-hosted
Provider-agnostic across models and machines
Secrets and permissions handled by the platform
cons: Young project, so the API surface can still move
Running your own machine pools is real infrastructure work

name: Linkit
description: Linkit is a desktop bookmark manager built for knowledge workers. AI summaries, semantic search and a knowledge graph turn saved links into something you can actually use, collections group ideas across categories, and link health checks plus duplicate detection keep the library clean. Storage is local-first with optional cloud sync.
description_en: Linkit is a desktop bookmark manager built for knowledge workers. AI summaries, semantic search and a knowledge graph turn saved links into something you can actually use, collections group ideas across categories, and link health checks plus duplicate detection keep the library clean. Storage is local-first with optional cloud sync.

use_cases.title: Import the bookmarks you already have
use_cases.detail: One-click import from Chrome, Firefox, Raindrop and more gets a full library in seconds.

use_cases.title: Search by meaning, not by keyword
use_cases.detail: Semantic search finds a saved page even when you cannot remember its title.

use_cases.title: Run the AI features on your own model
use_cases.detail: Point it at any OpenAI-compatible API or a local model such as Ollama for the full feature set.

pros: Completely free with no paywalls, local or cloud
Local-first storage that keeps your data yours
Works with local models through an OpenAI-compatible API
cons: Desktop only, and macOS builds ship without Apple notarization
Full AI features need you to bring an API key or a local model

name: IronBee Express
description: IronBee Express is a browser agent that checks whether your app really did what the page says, and finds the root cause when it did not. It drives real flows such as logging in, adding to cart and checking out, escalating to deeper reasoning only when a step needs it. It is written in TypeScript and licensed under Elastic-2.0.
description_en: IronBee Express is a browser agent that checks whether your app really did what the page says, and finds the root cause when it did not. It drives real flows such as logging in, adding to cart and checking out, escalating to deeper reasoning only when a step needs it. It is written in TypeScript and licensed under Elastic-2.0.

use_cases.title: Verify a flow actually completed
use_cases.detail: It checks the outcome at runtime instead of trusting whatever the page happens to display.

use_cases.title: Get a root cause when a step fails
use_cases.detail: When the app did not do what the page claims, it works out why rather than just failing.

use_cases.title: Keep the evidence from every run
use_cases.detail: Connect IronBee and each run is kept with its video, plus backend traces and logs behind the verdict.

pros: Checks runtime behaviour rather than trusting the page text
Deep reasoning is spent only where it matters
Open source under Elastic-2.0
cons: Hosted runs are behind a waitlist
Needs Node.js 22 or newer

name: Answer Me With HTML
description: Answer Me With HTML is an agent skill that answers hard questions with a single readable HTML page instead of a wall of terminal text. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and DeepSeek Harness, and the model writes roughly an eighth of the tokens it would need to hand-write the same HTML.
description_en: Answer Me With HTML is an agent skill that answers hard questions with a single readable HTML page instead of a wall of terminal text. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and DeepSeek Harness, and the model writes roughly an eighth of the tokens it would need to hand-write the same HTML.

use_cases.title: Explain something you keep re-reading
use_cases.detail: Ask for a protocol or a system and get one page with diagrams rather than dense prose.

use_cases.title: Map a repository you just joined
use_cases.detail: Ask how the modules in the repo fit together and get a page you can scan.

use_cases.title: Keep the answer as one file
use_cases.detail: The page is a single self-contained file you can open offline or send to someone.

pros: Turns dense terminal output into a page you can actually read
Cuts the tokens needed for a formatted answer by a large factor
Installs into several different coding agents
cons: Produces a page rather than text you can paste into a terminal
Output quality still depends on the underlying model

name: Refuseless
description: Refuseless is a hosted, OpenAI-compatible inference API for abliterated open-weight models. It serves Z AI's GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash with the refusal direction removed from the weights, charges per million tokens, and does not retain prompts after the response.
description_en: Refuseless is a hosted, OpenAI-compatible inference API for abliterated open-weight models. It serves Z AI's GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash with the refusal direction removed from the weights, charges per million tokens, and does not retain prompts after the response.

use_cases.title: Swap it into an existing SDK
use_cases.detail: Point any OpenAI SDK at its endpoint and set the model to an abliterated GLM checkpoint.

use_cases.title: Run a coding agent against it
use_cases.detail: Config snippets are published for agents such as OpenCode and Pi.

use_cases.title: Automate cyber tasks
use_cases.detail: It is positioned at security teams and professionals rather than general chat use.

pros: Drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint
No prompt retention after the response
Both a frontier model and a cheaper flash model
cons: Pay per million tokens, with no free tier mentioned
Serving models with refusals removed raises obvious responsible-use questions

name: Jaynshare
description: Jaynshare is a self-hosted proxy that lets Claude Code, Codex and Claude Desktop draw from a pool of subscriptions. You replace claude with jaynshare claude and each prompt is routed to an account that still has quota. It is written in Rust, released under MIT, and ships a Linux server with macOS and Windows clients.
description_en: Jaynshare is a self-hosted proxy that lets Claude Code, Codex and Claude Desktop draw from a pool of subscriptions. You replace claude with jaynshare claude and each prompt is routed to an account that still has quota. It is written in Rust, released under MIT, and ships a Linux server with macOS and Windows clients.

use_cases.title: Keep working through a rate limit
use_cases.detail: Requests are routed away from accounts that have run out of quota.

use_cases.title: Pool accounts you own
use_cases.detail: It works just as well for several accounts of your own as for a shared pool.

use_cases.title: Route Codex the same way
use_cases.detail: The same wrapper covers codex and claude desktop, not just the claude CLI.

pros: Self-hosted and MIT licensed
Adoption is one word in front of your usual command
Detailed risk, security and privacy docs included
cons: Pooling Claude subscriptions conflicts with Anthropic's terms and can get every account suspended
You run and secure the proxy server yourself

name: BonBook
description: BonBook is an AI travel agent you reach by email. You send one message, it replies with flight options, and once you pick one it books and then keeps watching the trip, checking you in, catching delays and rebooking you automatically. It advertises zero fees and zero commissions.
description_en: BonBook is an AI travel agent you reach by email. You send one message, it replies with flight options, and once you pick one it books and then keeps watching the trip, checking you in, catching delays and rebooking you automatically. It advertises zero fees and zero commissions.

use_cases.title: Book a flight by replying to an email
use_cases.detail: One message gets you options, and picking one finishes the booking.

use_cases.title: Get rebooked when a flight cancels
use_cases.detail: It monitors the trip and rebooks without you having to notice first.

use_cases.title: Recover money when the fare drops
use_cases.detail: It watches fares after purchase and pursues refunds and rebooking.

pros: Works entirely over email, where you already are
Monitors the trip and acts instead of only notifying you
Keeps your card points, loyalty miles and seat upgrades
cons: Flights only and currently labelled beta
Its savings and inventory claims are the company's own

name: Costura
description: Costura is open-source, self-hosted AI spend attribution. You connect read-only billing keys for Anthropic, Claude.ai, OpenAI, Codex, OpenRouter, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and it folds them into one daily ledger rolled up to the person who spent it, explaining anomalies in one sentence and flagging keys with no owner or no limit.
description_en: Costura is open-source, self-hosted AI spend attribution. You connect read-only billing keys for Anthropic, Claude.ai, OpenAI, Codex, OpenRouter, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and it folds them into one daily ledger rolled up to the person who spent it, explaining anomalies in one sentence and flagging keys with no owner or no limit.

use_cases.title: Find out why spend moved
use_cases.detail: Anomalies come back as a sentence naming the key and the model that caused them.

use_cases.title: Find keys nobody owns
use_cases.detail: Owner, limit, creation date and last use are shown for every key and seat.

use_cases.title: Tie out against the provider
use_cases.detail: The ledger is checked against each provider's own report over matched date ranges.

pros: Read-only by design, and self-hosted so provider keys never leave your infrastructure
Covers API keys and seats in one ledger
Explains changes rather than only charting them
cons: The site still marks the product as coming soon
GitHub Copilot support is listed as experimental

name: Pi Subagents Lite
description: Pi Subagents Lite adds sub-agents to the pi coding agent, schema-first and with minimal token overhead. It exposes four tools, Agent, StopAgent, MessageAgent and AgentStatus, and supports foreground and background agents with their own tools, extensions and model, plus a live widget, a conversation viewer with cost tracking and a watchdog for stuck agents.
description_en: Pi Subagents Lite adds sub-agents to the pi coding agent, schema-first and with minimal token overhead. It exposes four tools, Agent, StopAgent, MessageAgent and AgentStatus, and supports foreground and background agents with their own tools, extensions and model, plus a live widget, a conversation viewer with cost tracking and a watchdog for stuck agents.

use_cases.title: Keep the system prompt clean
use_cases.detail: Work goes into isolated sessions instead of piling up in your main context.

use_cases.title: Run agents in the background
use_cases.detail: Background agents acknowledge immediately and auto-deliver when they finish.

use_cases.title: Watch what each agent costs
use_cases.detail: A live widget and conversation viewer show tokens and cost per agent.

pros: Deliberately tiny tool schema to limit token overhead
Background agents with concurrency, steering and continuation
Cost tracking and a watchdog for stuck agents
cons: Requires pi 0.99.0 or newer and Node.js 22.19 or newer
Only useful if you already run pi

name: Claude Migrate
description: Claude Migrate is an unofficial CLI that moves Claude Desktop Code sessions to another account on the same Mac, pins included. It copies the session records from the old account's sidebar store to the new one, keeps their IDs so pins survive, and clears the links that belong to the old account. It dry-runs first and is undoable.
description_en: Claude Migrate is an unofficial CLI that moves Claude Desktop Code sessions to another account on the same Mac, pins included. It copies the session records from the old account's sidebar store to the new one, keeps their IDs so pins survive, and clears the links that belong to the old account. It dry-runs first and is undoable.

use_cases.title: Get your Code sidebar back
use_cases.detail: Moving from a personal to a Team account otherwise leaves the Code tab empty.

use_cases.title: Preview before you commit
use_cases.detail: A dry run shows exactly what would move before anything is written.

use_cases.title: Back out if it was wrong
use_cases.detail: The migration is undoable, and it never touches transcripts or existing files.

pros: Dry-run first and undoable
Session IDs are preserved so pins carry over
Never touches transcripts or existing files
cons: macOS only, unofficial and not endorsed by Anthropic
Relies on undocumented Claude Desktop storage that can change

name: MCP Census
description: The MCP Census checks the public evidence for an MCP server and returns PASS, REVIEW, BLOCK or UNKNOWN before you install it. It tracks tens of thousands of servers, GitHub repositories, issues and remote endpoints, serves the same facts over HTTP and MCP, and lets an agent audit a whole .mcp.json config with a single call.
description_en: The MCP Census checks the public evidence for an MCP server and returns PASS, REVIEW, BLOCK or UNKNOWN before you install it. It tracks tens of thousands of servers, GitHub repositories, issues and remote endpoints, serves the same facts over HTTP and MCP, and lets an agent audit a whole .mcp.json config with a single call.

use_cases.title: Check a server before installing
use_cases.detail: It asks whether it is the vendor's own server or a lookalike, and whether it is still maintained.

use_cases.title: Audit a whole config at once
use_cases.detail: One API call audits every server in an .mcp.json before the agent uses any of them.

use_cases.title: See what changed since last time
use_cases.detail: A cursor tells an agent what moved in the registry since its previous check.

pros: Says plainly that it is a first gate, not a malware scan
Unmetered stats endpoint that needs no account
Same facts served over MCP for agents to call
cons: Verdict can be UNKNOWN when the public evidence is thin
Daily lookup limits, with paid tiers for heavier use

name: Gauge CLI
description: Gauge CLI is an open-source command line tool for hillclimbing agent experience. It runs real coding agents against your Skills, CLI, SDK, MCP server, API or docs, captures where they get stuck, and lets your own coding agent test fixes before you publish them. The whole loop runs locally in Docker with the agent subscriptions or API keys you already have.
description_en: Gauge CLI is an open-source command line tool for hillclimbing agent experience. It runs real coding agents against your Skills, CLI, SDK, MCP server, API or docs, captures where they get stuck, and lets your own coding agent test fixes before you publish them. The whole loop runs locally in Docker with the agent subscriptions or API keys you already have.

use_cases.title: Find what blocks an agent
use_cases.detail: It catches interactive commands that hang, deprecated patterns agents reach for, and workflows they cannot work out.

use_cases.title: Notice a Skill nobody triggers
use_cases.detail: Gauge reports when a Skill goes unused even though the task should have triggered it.

use_cases.title: Validate a fix before release
use_cases.detail: Your own agent can test a proposed change to help text, code or docs before you publish it.

pros: Runs locally with no Gauge account required
Tests the real product against real agents rather than a synthetic checker
MIT licensed
cons: Needs Docker running Linux containers plus credentials for the agents you test with
Findings still need a human to decide what the right fix is

name: Standard Topic
description: Standard Topic is a news platform that ranks the latest reporting on every topic by relevance and adds AI summaries that show their sources. It covers world, politics, business, technology and AI, and also publishes a twice-daily news podcast.
description_en: Standard Topic is a news platform that ranks the latest reporting on every topic by relevance and adds AI summaries that show their sources. It covers world, politics, business, technology and AI, and also publishes a twice-daily news podcast.

use_cases.title: Read a topic with its sources attached
use_cases.detail: Summaries link back to the reporting they came from instead of replacing it.

use_cases.title: Follow a running story
use_cases.detail: Topics are ranked by relevance, so a developing story stays near the top.

use_cases.title: Listen instead of reading
use_cases.detail: A twice-daily podcast covers the same ground as the written summaries.

pros: Summaries show their sources rather than standing in for them
Ranked by relevance across a wide set of topics
Includes a podcast feed alongside the writing
cons: No pricing or API details published on the site
Coverage and ranking are the operator's own editorial judgement

name: Okaeri
description: Okaeri is a calm localhost homepage that gathers the latest papers, blogs, forums and news in science and tech into tabs you set up yourself. A small embedding model runs on your own machine to rank stories, your clicks and hides feed the ranking, and your reading history never leaves the device.
description_en: Okaeri is a calm localhost homepage that gathers the latest papers, blogs, forums and news in science and tech into tabs you set up yourself. A small embedding model runs on your own machine to rank stories, your clicks and hides feed the ranking, and your reading history never leaves the device.

use_cases.title: Make it your browser homepage
use_cases.detail: Pick your sources once and it fetches them in the background and opens on localhost.

use_cases.title: Get recommendations without a server
use_cases.detail: A small embedding model on your machine ranks the feed for recommended stories.

use_cases.title: Tune the ranking yourself
use_cases.detail: The recommendation algorithm is yours to change, from the UI or in the code.

pros: Everything including the embedding model runs locally
The recommendation algorithm is yours to tune
Reading history never leaves the device
cons: Needs about 500 MB of disk and downloads a model on first run
The background ranking process uses CPU and memory and can cost laptop battery

name: UI Design Editor
description: UI Design Editor is a free shared design canvas that people and AI assistants can read and edit together. It exposes WebMCP site tools so an assistant can read a design and then add, move, resize, restyle, hide or remove text, shapes, icons and pictures in the same project, while keeping your own undo history intact.
description_en: UI Design Editor is a free shared design canvas that people and AI assistants can read and edit together. It exposes WebMCP site tools so an assistant can read a design and then add, move, resize, restyle, hide or remove text, shapes, icons and pictures in the same project, while keeping your own undo history intact.

use_cases.title: Let an agent edit the mockup in place
use_cases.detail: Send a project link and the assistant reads it before changing anything.

use_cases.title: Generate a whole design into a new project
use_cases.detail: A full design can be created as a named project rather than patching an existing one.

use_cases.title: Share one canvas across browsers
use_cases.detail: Anyone with the Space link can read and edit, and changes save to the server.

pros: Free, and works through standard browser site tools
Keeps the normal undo history and your own edits
HTML exports carry their own copy of the design
cons: Needs a browser with WebMCP site tools enabled
Anyone holding the Space link can read and edit

name: Anima
description: Anima is a Claude Code skill that turns a biology request into an interactive, sourced, isometric figure. Each figure has real structures, a mechanism you can toggle and a citation for every number on screen, and it says so out loud when the human evidence behind a claim is weak. It is MIT licensed.
description_en: Anima is a Claude Code skill that turns a biology request into an interactive, sourced, isometric figure. Each figure has real structures, a mechanism you can toggle and a citation for every number on screen, and it says so out loud when the human evidence behind a claim is weak. It is MIT licensed.

use_cases.title: Compare two mechanisms side by side
use_cases.detail: Ask for a figure contrasting two drugs at the transporter and get one you can toggle.

use_cases.title: Watch a signal change
use_cases.detail: Figures model the mechanism live, so you can block a receptor and see what happens.

use_cases.title: Share a figure as a link
use_cases.detail: Live figures open in a browser, so you can send one to someone instead of a static image.

pros: Every number on screen carries a citation
Figures are interactive rather than static images
Free and open source under MIT
cons: Scope is biology only
Some figures use models the project itself labels as not peer reviewed

name: Twain
description: Twain is a diff viewer for people who like Meld but wanted it slightly different. It shows every file from a Git diff in one sequential view with a fast file tree, scrolling minimaps, tree-sitter highlighting and search across all modified files, and it lets you comment on sets of changes and lines that an AI agent can read and add to from a CLI.
description_en: Twain is a diff viewer for people who like Meld but wanted it slightly different. It shows every file from a Git diff in one sequential view with a fast file tree, scrolling minimaps, tree-sitter highlighting and search across all modified files, and it lets you comment on sets of changes and lines that an AI agent can read and add to from a CLI.

use_cases.title: Read everything an agent changed
use_cases.detail: All files from a diff appear in one view, in order, instead of one tab at a time.

use_cases.title: Reveal context around a hunk
use_cases.detail: Switch between changed parts only and full files, revealing unchanged parts granularly.

use_cases.title: Comment where the agent can see it
use_cases.detail: Comments on lines and change sets can be read and extended by an agent from the command line.

pros: Every file from a diff in one sequential view
Comments are machine-readable so agents can take part in the review
Tree-sitter highlighting across languages
cons: No merge, no three-way compare and no direct editing of files
GTK 4 desktop build, with Windows listed as new and not well tested

name: Skillsync
description: Skillsync is a macOS app that searches all your past agent sessions before each prompt and hands your agent what you already figured out. It installs plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Amp, pi, Grok, Antigravity and Hermes, reads the sessions those agents already keep, and returns a short recollection with sources in under a second.
description_en: Skillsync is a macOS app that searches all your past agent sessions before each prompt and hands your agent what you already figured out. It installs plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Amp, pi, Grok, Antigravity and Hermes, reads the sessions those agents already keep, and returns a short recollection with sources in under a second.

use_cases.title: Stop re-explaining a recurring problem
use_cases.detail: A prompt is checked against every past session and matches come back as a recollection.

use_cases.title: Search every session from anywhere
use_cases.detail: A shortcut opens search over any app, so you can find and reopen a session without leaving your work.

use_cases.title: Hand over a decision with its sources
use_cases.detail: Recollections arrive with sources, so the agent builds on them instead of starting over.

pros: Nothing to index and nothing to configure up front
Works on the sessions your agents already write to disk
Recollections come back with sources attached
cons: macOS only
Pricing is not stated on the page you land on first

name: Doozy
description: Doozy is an AI coworker that lives in your Slack and does the work in your own tools. You ask it in a channel, it pulls the data from the systems your team already uses, writes the result back as a file, and reports what it did along with the sources it used.
description_en: Doozy is an AI coworker that lives in your Slack and does the work in your own tools. You ask it in a channel, it pulls the data from the systems your team already uses, writes the result back as a file, and reports what it did along with the sources it used.

use_cases.title: Ask a question, get a spreadsheet
use_cases.detail: It can pull a churn list from one system and the reason for each row from another, then write the file.

use_cases.title: Delegate a report and come back to it done
use_cases.detail: Work is carried out in your own tools rather than in a separate assistant UI.

use_cases.title: Let the whole team use one hire
use_cases.detail: It is priced per team rather than per seat, so anyone in the workspace can ask.

pros: Priced for a whole team rather than per person
Shows the tools and steps behind each answer
Learns how the team works as it goes
cons: Only works inside Slack, so teams on other chat tools are out
It acts in your production systems, so permissions need thinking about

name: Server Noonien
description: Server Noonien is shared, serverless, conflict-free memory for AI agents, built as a drop-in replacement for the official MCP memory knowledge graph. It keeps the same entities, observations and relations but converges across machines through peer-to-peer sync, with no central server, no database and no merge conflicts.
description_en: Server Noonien is shared, serverless, conflict-free memory for AI agents, built as a drop-in replacement for the official MCP memory knowledge graph. It keeps the same entities, observations and relations but converges across machines through peer-to-peer sync, with no central server, no database and no merge conflicts.

use_cases.title: Share one memory across machines
use_cases.detail: The daemon replicates each node's shard directly to the others, so several machines share one memory with no shared folder.

use_cases.title: Replace the reference memory server
use_cases.detail: Same entities, observations and relations, so existing MCP clients keep working.

use_cases.title: Fall back to a shared area
use_cases.detail: When peers cannot reach each other, file and S3 backends cover the same ground.

pros: Peer-to-peer sync with no server or database to run
Drop-in compatibility with the reference MCP memory graph
Conflict-free by construction rather than by merge rules
cons: Peers need IP reachability, so a VPN or LAN is assumed
MPL-2.0 carries obligations if you modify and distribute it

name: Ramet
description: Ramet gives AI agents persistent, forkable workspaces. Each session or attempt gets an isolated writable workspace over a shared immutable base, changes become persistent when your harness captures a snapshot, and you can fork isolated attempts, reset to a clean starting point and choose exactly what survives between sessions.
description_en: Ramet gives AI agents persistent, forkable workspaces. Each session or attempt gets an isolated writable workspace over a shared immutable base, changes become persistent when your harness captures a snapshot, and you can fork isolated attempts, reset to a clean starting point and choose exactly what survives between sessions.

use_cases.title: Keep agent files when a sandbox dies
use_cases.detail: Workspace files and local Git state save and restore across sessions and sandbox replacements.

use_cases.title: Run parallel attempts on one base
use_cases.detail: Independent forks and selective persistence suit best-of-N coding agents.

use_cases.title: Reset environments between rollouts
use_cases.detail: Clean filesystem resets are verified before reuse, to catch contamination in agentic RL.

pros: Bring your own agent framework and sandbox
Git-aware snapshots with verified resets
Documented integrations for LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen and SkyRL
cons: Infrastructure that sits between your framework and your sandbox
A custom harness still needs Go, Python or HTTP integration work

name: Chai UI
description: Chai UI is an open-source design system for building AI apps. It ships React and Vue components for model routing, prompt optimization, media analysis and image editing alongside design tokens, so designers, developers and AI agents work from the same interface.
description_en: Chai UI is an open-source design system for building AI apps. It ships React and Vue components for model routing, prompt optimization, media analysis and image editing alongside design tokens, so designers, developers and AI agents work from the same interface.

use_cases.title: Drop in a prompt bar
use_cases.detail: A composer component handles the prompt state and hands you everything it tracks on submit.

use_cases.title: Give agents the same components you use
use_cases.detail: Designers, developers and agents build from one set of components.

use_cases.title: Keep model controls consistent
use_cases.detail: Model routing and prompt optimization get shared, themed controls rather than one-off widgets.

pros: MIT licensed and available for both React and Vue
Components target AI-specific UI rather than generic widgets
Design tokens ship as their own package
cons: Marked as in active development, with only a handful of components so far
A 0.x version means the API can still move

name: Agent Workflow Skills
description: Agent Workflow Skills is a library of Claude Code skills, subagents and hooks for an agent that proves its work. A supervisor sends each step to the cheapest model that can do it and escalates after two failures, gates pass on exit code, bug fixes ship with a test shown to fail without the fix, and every session ends with a handoff note the next one picks up.
description_en: Agent Workflow Skills is a library of Claude Code skills, subagents and hooks for an agent that proves its work. A supervisor sends each step to the cheapest model that can do it and escalates after two failures, gates pass on exit code, bug fixes ship with a test shown to fail without the fix, and every session ends with a handoff note the next one picks up.

use_cases.title: Make a fix prove itself
use_cases.detail: The new test is run against the code from before the fix and shown to fail, then pass with it.

use_cases.title: Keep sessions continuous
use_cases.detail: A session ends with a handoff note that the next session picks up automatically.

use_cases.title: Spend less on easy steps
use_cases.detail: A supervisor routes each step to the cheapest model and moves up a tier after two failures.

pros: Regression proof is demonstrated on a real fix inside the repository
The library checks its own frontmatter, links, scripts and hooks in CI
Installable as a plugin or through the skills CLI
cons: Built specifically for Claude Code
The model-tier supervisor only pays off on larger workflows

name: Glider
description: Glider is a single-node vector database that treats S3-compatible object storage as the source of truth. Every acknowledged write is durable in object storage before the server answers, local RAM and SSD only speed up reads, and it serves nearest-neighbour search with metadata filters over an HTTP and JSON API, with a Python client and an MCP memory server.
description_en: Glider is a single-node vector database that treats S3-compatible object storage as the source of truth. Every acknowledged write is durable in object storage before the server answers, local RAM and SSD only speed up reads, and it serves nearest-neighbour search with metadata filters over an HTTP and JSON API, with a Python client and an MCP memory server.

use_cases.title: Run vector search with S3 as the only durable state
use_cases.detail: Acknowledged writes land in object storage before the client gets a response.

use_cases.title: Query with metadata filters over HTTP
use_cases.detail: Collections, upserts and filtered nearest-neighbour queries are all plain HTTP and JSON.

use_cases.title: Back an agent's memory with it
use_cases.detail: An MCP memory server is included alongside the Python client.

pros: Crash-safe writes acknowledged only after object storage durability
No separate database cluster to operate
Dual licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0
cons: Single node, so it is not a distributed store
Real durability needs S3 or MinIO credentials and configuration

name: Shipback
description: Shipback is an SFTP deploy tool built so every deploy can be taken back. It uploads a folder to cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin or a plain VPS with a backup of each replaced file taken before the upload starts, swaps files in whole so a dropped connection leaves the old one, and restores byte for byte with one command. It runs standalone, from a script, or as an MCP server.
description_en: Shipback is an SFTP deploy tool built so every deploy can be taken back. It uploads a folder to cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin or a plain VPS with a backup of each replaced file taken before the upload starts, swaps files in whole so a dropped connection leaves the old one, and restores byte for byte with one command. It runs standalone, from a script, or as an MCP server.

use_cases.title: Let an agent deploy and still be able to undo
use_cases.detail: One command puts the site back byte for byte, even after a deploy cut off halfway.

use_cases.title: Refuse a stale deploy
use_cases.detail: A deploy only runs the exact plan the agent previewed, and refuses if a file changed in between.

use_cases.title: See what drifted on the server
use_cases.detail: A dry-run pull shows what changed on the host since your last deploy.

pros: One-command undo that never overwrites a live edit
Files are swapped in whole, so a dropped connection leaves the old file
The MCP server has no switch to delete files or skip the backup
cons: Covers SFTP hosts only, not container or serverless targets
A young project whose guarantees rest on its own published promise

name: CoolDock
description: CoolDock is a second Dock for macOS that holds live widgets for music, todos, events, weather, search, stats, quick actions, clipboard and screenshots beside your original Dock. It is local-first and privacy-first, and it also runs an MCP server so an assistant can reach the same widgets.
description_en: CoolDock is a second Dock for macOS that holds live widgets for music, todos, events, weather, search, stats, quick actions, clipboard and screenshots beside your original Dock. It is local-first and privacy-first, and it also runs an MCP server so an assistant can reach the same widgets.

use_cases.title: Keep the day one Dock away
use_cases.detail: Todos, reminders, calendar events and meetings sit beside your apps.

use_cases.title: Act without switching apps
use_cases.detail: Quick actions, clipboard history and search run straight from the Dock.

use_cases.title: Let an assistant read your widgets
use_cases.detail: The MCP server exposes the same widgets to tools such as Claude.

pros: One-time purchase rather than a subscription
Local-first and privacy-first
Broad widget set including clipboard and screenshots
cons: macOS Sonoma 14.0 or later only
The MCP server means deciding how much of your desktop an assistant can see

name: Fuel Gauge
description: Fuel Gauge is an unofficial Claude Code plugin that gives Claude a sense of its own limits. It reads the five-hour window, the weekly window and the context fill straight from the responses your session already receives, shows them next to your prompt, and pulls a hard stop at 95% so work ends at a clean point instead of mid-edit.
description_en: Fuel Gauge is an unofficial Claude Code plugin that gives Claude a sense of its own limits. It reads the five-hour window, the weekly window and the context fill straight from the responses your session already receives, shows them next to your prompt, and pulls a hard stop at 95% so work ends at a clean point instead of mid-edit.

use_cases.title: Stop a long task dying at 100%
use_cases.detail: A hard stop at 95% ends work at a clean point rather than mid-refactor.

use_cases.title: Let Claude pace heavy work
use_cases.detail: Every message carries one line with the window, the reset time and the context fill.

use_cases.title: Check resets without guessing
use_cases.detail: A gauge sits above the input, with a details panel showing reset times.

pros: Zero extra API calls, it reads what the session already receives
Hard stop at 95% instead of a surprise cut-off
MIT licensed with Windows and macOS builds
cons: Unofficial and tied to Claude's undocumented usage headers
A hard stop can interrupt a task you wanted to keep going

name: SuperLocalMemory
description: SuperLocalMemory is an open-source, local-first memory control plane for AI agents and teams. One memory serves every agent you use, from Claude Code and Cursor to web bots that speak MCP, recalling decisions, documents, screenshots and PDFs under governance that treats them like company data, and answering honestly when something is not in there.
description_en: SuperLocalMemory is an open-source, local-first memory control plane for AI agents and teams. One memory serves every agent you use, from Claude Code and Cursor to web bots that speak MCP, recalling decisions, documents, screenshots and PDFs under governance that treats them like company data, and answering honestly when something is not in there.

use_cases.title: Share one memory across harnesses
use_cases.detail: Local agents and web bots talk to each other through a mesh over one memory.

use_cases.title: Recall a decision or a screenshot
use_cases.detail: Decisions, documents, screenshots and PDFs are recalled the way you ask for them.

use_cases.title: Get an honest miss
use_cases.detail: When the answer is not there, the agent hears that it is not there rather than a confident guess.

pros: Local-first, with a mesh between local agents and web bots
Governance modelled on how company data is handled
Refuses to bluff when the answer is not in memory
cons: AGPL-3.0, which is restrictive for proprietary products
A control plane means setup work before it pays off

name: ColdIVF
description: ColdIVF is a read-optimized vector index in Rust, built for cold reads. It builds an index over float vectors of 128 to 4,080 dimensions, lets you prepare it while the query embedding is being computed so its tables load in parallel, and searches with an nprobe and rerank budget, with a writer that can insert, delete, sync and compact in the background.
description_en: ColdIVF is a read-optimized vector index in Rust, built for cold reads. It builds an index over float vectors of 128 to 4,080 dimensions, lets you prepare it while the query embedding is being computed so its tables load in parallel, and searches with an nprobe and rerank budget, with a writer that can insert, delete, sync and compact in the background.

use_cases.title: Serve a first query on a cold index
use_cases.detail: Prepare loads the index tables while the query embedding runs, rather than after.

use_cases.title: Write while searches continue
use_cases.detail: A writer inserts, replaces and deletes with changes visible to searches in the same process.

use_cases.title: Compact without stopping reads
use_cases.detail: Compaction can be handed to another thread so searches keep going while it writes.

pros: Purpose-built for the first query on a cold index
Python bindings through maturin plus a Rust crate
Background compaction while searches keep running
cons: Narrow feature set next to a full vector database
The benchmark numbers are the author's own

name: Autograph
description: Autograph is a music notation app for iPad and Mac that reads handwriting on the staff and engraves it properly. On the Mac, Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any assistant that speaks MCP can read the open score and edit it while you watch, with each request one undoable step. It exports PDF, MusicXML and MEI.
description_en: Autograph is a music notation app for iPad and Mac that reads handwriting on the staff and engraves it properly. On the Mac, Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any assistant that speaks MCP can read the open score and edit it while you watch, with each request one undoable step. It exports PDF, MusicXML and MEI.

use_cases.title: Write a phrase by hand
use_cases.detail: The stroke is read and set properly, so the handwriting disappears and the music stays.

use_cases.title: Ask an assistant to edit the open score
use_cases.detail: Claude can add a bass line, transpose a passage or add a dynamic as one undoable step.

use_cases.title: Take the score somewhere else
use_cases.detail: Export PDF for print, MusicXML for Sibelius, Finale, Dorico or MuseScore, and MEI for scholarly work.

pros: Handwriting recognition aimed at the moment before a piece is finished
MCP edits are one undoable step each
Exports to the interchange formats that actually matter
cons: iPad and Mac only, and the assistant connection is Mac-only
Not meant for typesetting a full symphony

name: Bifrost
description: Bifrost is an open-source, high-performance AI gateway that works as an LLM gateway, an MCP gateway and an agent gateway. It puts 23 or more providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API with automatic failover, load balancing, semantic caching, virtual keys, budgets and MCP code mode, and reports under 200 microseconds of overhead at 5k RPS.
description_en: Bifrost is an open-source, high-performance AI gateway that works as an LLM gateway, an MCP gateway and an agent gateway. It puts 23 or more providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API with automatic failover, load balancing, semantic caching, virtual keys, budgets and MCP code mode, and reports under 200 microseconds of overhead at 5k RPS.

use_cases.title: Front several providers with one endpoint
use_cases.detail: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex and more sit behind a single API your SDKs already speak.

use_cases.title: Survive a provider going down
use_cases.detail: Automatic failover and load balancing are part of the gateway rather than your application code.

use_cases.title: Put budgets on keys
use_cases.detail: Virtual keys, budgets and semantic caching let you govern spend per team.

pros: One OpenAI-compatible API across many providers
Failover, load balancing and semantic caching built in
Single Go binary with a claimed sub-200 microsecond overhead
cons: Another service to deploy, monitor and keep available
Its performance figures are the project's own measurements

name: Opposable
description: Opposable gives an AI assistant control of a real phone. It connects the iPhone or Android phone you already use to Claude over MCP, so the assistant opens apps, reads the screen, taps and types while signed in as you, and it also works as a connector from the Claude or ChatGPT app.
description_en: Opposable gives an AI assistant control of a real phone. It connects the iPhone or Android phone you already use to Claude over MCP, so the assistant opens apps, reads the screen, taps and types while signed in as you, and it also works as a connector from the Claude or ChatGPT app.

use_cases.title: Hand off the phone chores
use_cases.detail: Ask Claude to clear duplicate photos and old screenshots, find what is filling storage and free it up.

use_cases.title: Test on a real device
use_cases.detail: Claude Code and Codex can open the app you are building, walk through it and report what broke.

use_cases.title: Move a code between apps
use_cases.detail: It can read a sign-in code from Messages and use it in the app that needs it.

pros: Works on the phone you use every day, signed in as you
Free to download and usable from any MCP client
Offers its own on-device model alongside hosted ones
cons: iPhone support needs a Mac running the bridge
Granting an assistant an Accessibility service on your phone is a large amount of trust

name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is NVIDIA's open-source runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Written in Rust and licensed under Apache 2.0, it gives agents a sandboxed place to execute with isolation primitives and an extension surface, so a team can let agents act on real systems without handing over the host. It installs from PyPI as the openshell package and ships published documentation and a 0.1.x upgrade guide.
description_en: OpenShell is NVIDIA's open-source runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Written in Rust and licensed under Apache 2.0, it gives agents a sandboxed place to execute with isolation primitives and an extension surface, so a team can let agents act on real systems without handing over the host. It installs from PyPI as the openshell package and ships published documentation and a 0.1.x upgrade guide.

use_cases.title: Run agents against real systems
use_cases.detail: Agents execute inside an isolated runtime instead of directly on the developer machine.

use_cases.title: Scale past a single session
use_cases.detail: The runtime is built for fleets of agents rather than one long-running conversation.

use_cases.title: Extend the runtime safely
use_cases.detail: Version 0.1.x adds new isolation primitives and an expanded extension surface with a documented upgrade path.

pros: Apache 2.0 and installable from PyPI
Isolation primitives designed specifically for autonomous agents
Published documentation and a stated release cadence
cons: Early 0.1.x line, so interfaces are still moving
Rust and container tooling make this a developer-facing install

name: MIKE
description: MIKE (Integrated Kanban Environment) is an open-source LLM harness for software development work. It pairs a Kanban board with strong sandbox isolation through gVisor, supports custom extensions in sandboxed iframes or WebAssembly through wazero, ships a Progressive Web App optimized for spotty networks, and runs against llama.cpp or any provider that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API.
description_en: MIKE (Integrated Kanban Environment) is an open-source LLM harness for software development work. It pairs a Kanban board with strong sandbox isolation through gVisor, supports custom extensions in sandboxed iframes or WebAssembly through wazero, ships a Progressive Web App optimized for spotty networks, and runs against llama.cpp or any provider that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API.

use_cases.title: Give an agent a walled garden
use_cases.detail: Units of work run under gVisor isolation rather than straight on your machine.

use_cases.title: Work from a weak connection
use_cases.detail: The Progressive Web App is built to stay usable on spotty networks.

use_cases.title: Bring your own inference
use_cases.detail: Point it at local llama.cpp or at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

pros: gVisor sandboxing is part of the design, not an add-on
Works with local llama.cpp or OpenAI-compatible providers
Extensions run sandboxed through iframes and wazero
cons: Needs Docker or Podman plus a generated encryption key to start
The API and extension interfaces are explicitly unstable before 1.0

name: Corgi
description: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer for humans and agents. It keeps watch over every agent you have running, shows which ones need you, tracks where your tokens went, replays every file an agent touched and organizes workspaces into worktrees, while processes keep running in the background the way they do in tmux. It installs with a curl one-liner and supports macOS, Linux and WSL.
description_en: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer for humans and agents. It keeps watch over every agent you have running, shows which ones need you, tracks where your tokens went, replays every file an agent touched and organizes workspaces into worktrees, while processes keep running in the background the way they do in tmux. It installs with a curl one-liner and supports macOS, Linux and WSL.

use_cases.title: Watch several agents at once
use_cases.detail: A status line marks each agent as working, needing you, finished or idle, with F1 to catch up.

use_cases.title: See where tokens went
use_cases.detail: Per-agent activity tracking shows what each one did, with detail on hover.

use_cases.title: Review what an agent changed
use_cases.detail: Replay lists every file the agent touched in one scroll, and worktrees keep tasks apart.

pros: Agents and dev servers keep running in the background like tmux
Reuses your existing Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode accounts
Workspace-aware, with worktree organization and per-workspace resource usage
cons: macOS, Linux and WSL only
Installs by piping a shell script from the site

name: Craig CLI
description: Craig is a keyboard-driven terminal workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in parallel, each task in its own Git worktree, and keeps tasks, changes, pull requests and checks together in one place. It installs from npm, needs Node 22 or newer, is MIT licensed and requires no Craig account.
description_en: Craig is a keyboard-driven terminal workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in parallel, each task in its own Git worktree, and keeps tasks, changes, pull requests and checks together in one place. It installs from npm, needs Node 22 or newer, is MIT licensed and requires no Craig account.

use_cases.title: Split a bug and a feature
use_cases.detail: Give one agent the bug and another the feature; Craig creates a branch and worktree for each.

use_cases.title: Watch checks without leaving the terminal
use_cases.detail: Pull requests and CI checks sit next to the agent that produced them.

use_cases.title: Go from task to merged PR on the keyboard
use_cases.detail: The whole loop from starting a task to merging runs inside one TUI.

pros: MIT licensed and no vendor account required
Agnostic across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
One worktree per task keeps parallel agents from colliding
cons: Requires Node 22 or newer
Terminal only, with no graphical interface

name: Twine
description: Twine is a native macOS workspace for coordinating coding agents, described by its authors as an Agentic Development Environment.
