Written in Rust and released under the MIT license, it runs on macOS 26 or later and keeps several agents, their workspaces and their output inside one native app instead of scattered terminal tabs.
description_en: Twine is a native macOS workspace for coordinating coding agents, described by its authors as an Agentic Development Environment. Written in Rust and released under the MIT license, it runs on macOS 26 or later and keeps several agents, their workspaces and their output inside one native app instead of scattered terminal tabs.

use_cases.title: Coordinate several agents at once
use_cases.detail: Agents run side by side in a native macOS app instead of separate terminal windows.

use_cases.title: Keep agent work where you can see it
use_cases.detail: Workspace state and agent output stay in one place you can return to.

use_cases.title: Install without building a toolchain
use_cases.detail: CI publishes release assets you can download directly.

pros: Native macOS app under the MIT license
Written in Rust with CI on every push
Purpose-built for coordinating agents rather than generic terminal multiplexing
cons: Requires macOS 26 or later
Young project with a narrow platform target

name: Halv
description: Halv is an open-source desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM side by side on the subscriptions you already pay for. Its local savings engine filters command output and compresses context on your own machine, and a Crux code index answers caller, reference and blast-radius questions from an index instead of reading files. Halv Cloud adds a router that sends each task to the model it needs, a savings dashboard and automatic account rotation, for 10 dollars a month.
description_en: Halv is an open-source desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM side by side on the subscriptions you already pay for. Its local savings engine filters command output and compresses context on your own machine, and a Crux code index answers caller, reference and blast-radius questions from an index instead of reading files. Halv Cloud adds a router that sends each task to the model it needs, a savings dashboard and automatic account rotation, for 10 dollars a month.

use_cases.title: Run four agents in one window
use_cases.detail: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM each use their own subscription.

use_cases.title: Cut context and output cost locally
use_cases.detail: Command output filtering and context compression both run on your device.

use_cases.title: Let a router pick the model
use_cases.detail: Halv Cloud routes each task and can move work to another account when one plan hits its usage ceiling.

pros: Apache 2.0, free forever for the desktop workspace and every local savings layer
Crux code index answers structural questions without reading every file
Live savings meter shows what each conversation saved as you work
cons: The Cloud router is a separate 10 dollar a month subscription
Published savings percentages come from the project own SWE-rebench paired runs, not from your codebase

name: EditMD
description: EditMD is a small native macOS editor for markdown files that lets you edit the rendered document in place and saves plain markdown back. It uses Y.js to merge edits made by coding agents in real time, so you can keep writing while an agent changes the same file instead of one side clobbering the other or hitting a file-changed-on-disk dialog.
description_en: EditMD is a small native macOS editor for markdown files that lets you edit the rendered document in place and saves plain markdown back. It uses Y.js to merge edits made by coding agents in real time, so you can keep writing while an agent changes the same file instead of one side clobbering the other or hitting a file-changed-on-disk dialog.

use_cases.title: Write while an agent edits
use_cases.detail: Y.js merges your edits and the agent edits in real time, like a shared document.

use_cases.title: Edit rendered markdown
use_cases.detail: Work on the rendered document and still get plain markdown on disk.

use_cases.title: Send an agent for references
use_cases.detail: Have an agent add links or fill in quotes while you keep writing in the same file.

pros: MIT licensed and deliberately small
Real-time merge removes clobbering and reload dialogs
Files stay plain markdown
cons: macOS only
Early release at version 0.1.0

name: Keen Code
description: Keen Code is a context-aware terminal-based coding agent written in Go. It supports multiple providers, MCP servers, subagents and agent skills, and adds controllable tool output retention, hashline edits, compaction, a permission system, session management, multi-agent orchestration and a task classifier that routes work using decision models.
description_en: Keen Code is a context-aware terminal-based coding agent written in Go. It supports multiple providers, MCP servers, subagents and agent skills, and adds controllable tool output retention, hashline edits, compaction, a permission system, session management, multi-agent orchestration and a task classifier that routes work using decision models.

use_cases.title: Swap providers without swapping tools
use_cases.detail: Several AI providers sit behind the same CLI.

use_cases.title: Control what stays in context
use_cases.detail: Tool output retention is configurable and compaction trims long sessions.

use_cases.title: Route tasks by classification
use_cases.detail: A decision-model classifier decides how a request is handled, with documented fail-open behaviour.

pros: Single Go binary driving a terminal agent
Documented subsystems for permissions, memory, subagents and MCP
Skills system and queuing built in
cons: Documentation is still being filled out alongside the code
Terminal-first, so there is no editor UI

name: TenseMem
description: TenseMem is embedded, deterministic state memory for AI agents, described as memory that knows its tenses. One SQLite file with no server: the model proposes typed facts and the engine decides what is current, keeping one current value per slot, reporting whether a read is fresh and refusing to learn from its own output. Installed with pip, it works with a rule-based extractor or with OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LiteLLM or Gemini.
description_en: TenseMem is embedded, deterministic state memory for AI agents, described as memory that knows its tenses. One SQLite file with no server: the model proposes typed facts and the engine decides what is current, keeping one current value per slot, reporting whether a read is fresh and refusing to learn from its own output. Installed with pip, it works with a rule-based extractor or with OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LiteLLM or Gemini.

use_cases.title: Replace stale duplicate facts
use_cases.detail: Similarity search returns both an old address and a new one; TenseMem keeps one current value per slot.

use_cases.title: Run without an API key
use_cases.detail: The bundled FakeExtractor is rule-based, so the same API works offline.

use_cases.title: Check freshness before acting
use_cases.detail: A read returns whether the value is current, not just the nearest match.

pros: Single SQLite file with no server to operate
Deterministic: the engine, not the model, decides what is current
Refuses to learn from its own output
cons: Python package, so Python agents get the smoothest path today
Opinionated memory model that replaces rather than augments vector search

name: Inillucent
description: Inillucent is an embedded SQL database written in Rust and built as an agentic database. It implements the SQLite dialect with a Postgres dialect listed as upcoming, adds vector embeddings for semantic search and keyword search, and ships with a command line, a shell and an MCP server so an agent can query structured and semantic data through one database.
description_en: Inillucent is an embedded SQL database written in Rust and built as an agentic database. It implements the SQLite dialect with a Postgres dialect listed as upcoming, adds vector embeddings for semantic search and keyword search, and ships with a command line, a shell and an MCP server so an agent can query structured and semantic data through one database.

use_cases.title: Give an agent one database
use_cases.detail: Relational SQL and vector search live in the same embedded file.

use_cases.title: Wire it into MCP
use_cases.detail: The bundled MCP toolset lets an agent query data without custom glue code.

use_cases.title: Keep the dialect you know
use_cases.detail: The SQLite dialect is implemented, so existing queries carry over.

pros: Ships a CLI, a shell and an MCP server
Vector and keyword search built into the database itself
Embedded, so there is no separate server to operate
cons: Speed comparisons come from the vendor own benchmark workloads
The Postgres dialect is still listed as upcoming

name: Lumabri
description: Lumabri runs a private inference service across your own computers and servers, powered by Colibri and written in pure C. You choose the models, select which computers may help and approve how their memory is used. A worker loads only the weights for its assigned layers rather than a complete copy of the model, and you chat from the terminal or the bundled web page.
description_en: Lumabri runs a private inference service across your own computers and servers, powered by Colibri and written in pure C. You choose the models, select which computers may help and approve how their memory is used. A worker loads only the weights for its assigned layers rather than a complete copy of the model, and you chat from the terminal or the bundled web page.

use_cases.title: Run a model that does not fit one machine
use_cases.detail: Workers share the work, each loading only the layers it is assigned.

use_cases.title: Keep several models resident
use_cases.detail: Approved models stay loaded within explicit memory budgets.

use_cases.title: Watch the cluster from one place
use_cases.detail: Computers, allocations and measured workloads show up in one local workspace.

pros: A worker does not need its own complete copy of the model
Controller, terminal interface and inference integration are pure C
Conversation state stays with the nodes that execute those layers
cons: Adding computers adds memory and capacity but does not guarantee more tokens per second
Only worth the setup if you have several machines on one network

name: Skillstore
description: Skillstore is a searchable skills library for Claude Code and Codex. You connect through MCP to find expert instructions for whatever you are building, publish your own team methods so teammates and coding agents follow the same standards, and improve skills with feedback. The public library needs no Skillstore account, so you keep using your existing AI account.
description_en: Skillstore is a searchable skills library for Claude Code and Codex. You connect through MCP to find expert instructions for whatever you are building, publish your own team methods so teammates and coding agents follow the same standards, and improve skills with feedback. The public library needs no Skillstore account, so you keep using your existing AI account.

use_cases.title: Find instructions for the job
use_cases.detail: Search the library for a skill covering the specific task at hand.

use_cases.title: Share house style with agents
use_cases.detail: Publish team methods so every agent applies the same standards.

use_cases.title: Harden code before review
use_cases.detail: Sample skills cover checking access to each resource, validating untrusted input at the boundary and writing an abuse case.

pros: No account needed to try the public library
Works through MCP with the agents you already run
Skills can be improved with feedback over time
cons: Aimed at Claude Code and Codex rather than every agent
Value depends on the skills the community publishes

name: Ego Lite
description: Ego Lite is a browser built for AI agents to run browser automation in parallel while you keep browsing yourself. Each agent gets its own fully isolated Space so background work never collides with your tabs, agents write JavaScript functions directly instead of looping through CLI commands, and the project is MIT licensed and free to download for macOS.
description_en: Ego Lite is a browser built for AI agents to run browser automation in parallel while you keep browsing yourself. Each agent gets its own fully isolated Space so background work never collides with your tabs, agents write JavaScript functions directly instead of looping through CLI commands, and the project is MIT licensed and free to download for macOS.

use_cases.title: Let agents work while you browse
use_cases.detail: Agents run in their own Spaces in the background without touching your tabs.

use_cases.title: Run several agents at once
use_cases.detail: One agent can enrich leads while another scrapes competitor sites.

use_cases.title: Avoid command-loop dead ends
use_cases.detail: Agents write JavaScript functions against the page instead of chained CLI calls.

pros: MIT licensed, zero cost and zero configuration
A dedicated isolated Space for every agent
Code-based automation rather than CLI-based
cons: macOS build today, with Windows and Linux listed as coming soon
Speed comparisons come from the project own benchmarks

name: RigCheck
description: RigCheck answers whether your GPU or Mac can run a given local AI model. You pick your graphics card or Mac plus the amount of RAM, and each model own checker answers from the requirements and benchmarks published by the model developers, covering language, image and video model routes, complete workflow files and sourced memory limits.
description_en: RigCheck answers whether your GPU or Mac can run a given local AI model. You pick your graphics card or Mac plus the amount of RAM, and each model own checker answers from the requirements and benchmarks published by the model developers, covering language, image and video model routes, complete workflow files and sourced memory limits.

use_cases.title: Check a card before downloading
use_cases.detail: Pick a specific card and RAM and see which model sizes fit with every layer in GPU memory.

use_cases.title: Compare quantizations
use_cases.detail: File choices such as Q5_K_M or IQ4_XS are compared per model rather than collapsed into one verdict.

use_cases.title: Get a workflow, not just a verdict
use_cases.detail: Model routes come with complete workflow files and sourced memory limits.

pros: Answers come from developer-published requirements and benchmarks
Covers language, image and video model routes
Shows which quantization actually fits instead of a single yes or no
cons: Figures are capacity estimates for llama.cpp at a 32K context, not measured runs
Only covers models the site has on file

name: Agent Usage Guard
description: Agent Usage Guard is a Claude Code mod that holds subagent fan-out, heavy-context prompts and retry loops before they spend your usage window. It runs inside Claude Code, reads your plan live usage, counts agents across every session and asks for confirmation in Claude Code own dialog rather than after the budget is already gone.
description_en: Agent Usage Guard is a Claude Code mod that holds subagent fan-out, heavy-context prompts and retry loops before they spend your usage window. It runs inside Claude Code, reads your plan live usage, counts agents across every session and asks for confirmation in Claude Code own dialog rather than after the budget is already gone.

use_cases.title: Stop runaway subagents
use_cases.detail: It holds subagent fan-out before it multiplies across sessions.

use_cases.title: Catch context churn
use_cases.detail: Heavy-context churn and retry loops are held before they burn the window.

use_cases.title: Decide in the moment
use_cases.detail: The prompt appears in Claude Code own dialog, backed by the live usage numbers.

pros: Runs inside Claude Code as a mod, with no separate service
Reads live plan usage and counts agents across every session
Asks before spend happens rather than reporting afterwards
cons: Only works with Claude Code
As a mod it depends on Claude Code plugin surface staying stable

name: XTrace
description: XTrace is an open-source macOS app that shows where your coding time and money go. It reads the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor history already on your Mac and reports agent activity, estimated human time and API-equivalent spend, tracks Claude and Codex account usage and pace in the sidebar, and lets you tune the numbers with customizable scoring skills.
description_en: XTrace is an open-source macOS app that shows where your coding time and money go. It reads the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor history already on your Mac and reports agent activity, estimated human time and API-equivalent spend, tracks Claude and Codex account usage and pace in the sidebar, and lets you tune the numbers with customizable scoring skills.

use_cases.title: Compare agent time to human time
use_cases.detail: Estimated human time sits next to the agent time for the same work.

use_cases.title: Watch your usage window
use_cases.detail: Claude and Codex account usage and pace show in the sidebar.

use_cases.title: Score work your way
use_cases.detail: Scoring skills are customizable so the ranking matches your own definition of useful.

pros: Apache 2.0 and works from history already on your Mac
Covers Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in one dashboard
Customizable scoring skills
cons: macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon only
Human-time and spend figures are estimates, not billing data

name: Consumer Agent Testing Tool
description: CATT (Consumer Agent Testing Tool) tests how an assistant uses your service. You run a scripted or model-driven agent against an MCP server, an MCP app, a website or an HTTP API, check what the service actually did on its side, inspect sealed evidence and compare results across builds. Muse and Instinct are supported as surrogate emulation targets.
description_en: CATT (Consumer Agent Testing Tool) tests how an assistant uses your service. You run a scripted or model-driven agent against an MCP server, an MCP app, a website or an HTTP API, check what the service actually did on its side, inspect sealed evidence and compare results across builds. Muse and Instinct are supported as surrogate emulation targets.

use_cases.title: Test an MCP server before shipping
use_cases.detail: Drive an agent at the server and assert on service-side outcomes.

use_cases.title: Compare builds over time
use_cases.detail: Results are kept as sealed evidence so runs can be diffed across builds.

use_cases.title: Cover more than one assistant
use_cases.detail: Muse and Instinct emulation targets share one connector testing contract.

pros: Tests service-side outcomes rather than only the agent transcript
Works against MCP servers, MCP apps, websites and HTTP APIs
MIT licensed, with sealed evidence for each run
cons: It is a surrogate: a passing test approximates a host and does not certify compatibility with a real assistant
The model driving a trial is separate from the assistant being emulated, which adds configuration

name: Jahan
description: Jahan simulates how a population reacts to a product. It builds a population of LLM personas, each grounded in a real survey respondent drawn from a one-million-row dataset rather than invented by a prompt, places them on a social network, and lets them meet a product on an X-like feed, a Reddit-like forum and through word of mouth before answering survey waves about whether they would buy it.
description_en: Jahan simulates how a population reacts to a product. It builds a population of LLM personas, each grounded in a real survey respondent drawn from a one-million-row dataset rather than invented by a prompt, places them on a social network, and lets them meet a product on an X-like feed, a Reddit-like forum and through word of mouth before answering survey waves about whether they would buy it.

use_cases.title: Test a launch message
use_cases.detail: Personas see the product on a feed and a forum and change their minds out loud.

use_cases.title: Audit any number
use_cases.detail: Every turn is written to an append-only trace, so any run can be replayed, resumed or audited.

use_cases.title: Measure intent in words
use_cases.detail: Personas answer in their own words and answers are scored by semantic similarity instead of being asked for as a number.

pros: Personas are sampled from a real survey dataset rather than generated from a prompt
Append-only trace makes every run replayable and auditable
Prompts are rebuilt from the record and hash-checked rather than stored
cons: Simulation output is a signal, not a substitute for real customers
Large populations mean real inference spend

name: Firmenza
description: Firmenza is an AI assistant for SAM.gov and federal contracting. It monitors your registration, finds relevant opportunities, explains what a government section asks and checks the format of what you type, emails you before your registration expires and prepares renewal answers in a worksheet. A free health check shows what SAM.gov lists publicly for your UEI or legal name.
description_en: Firmenza is an AI assistant for SAM.gov and federal contracting. It monitors your registration, finds relevant opportunities, explains what a government section asks and checks the format of what you type, emails you before your registration expires and prepares renewal answers in a worksheet. A free health check shows what SAM.gov lists publicly for your UEI or legal name.

use_cases.title: Check your public record
use_cases.detail: Enter a UEI or legal name and see what SAM.gov lists publicly.

use_cases.title: Do not miss a renewal
use_cases.detail: An email arrives before the registration expires and a worksheet walks the renewal questions.

use_cases.title: Match opportunities
use_cases.detail: Relevant contract opportunities are surfaced against your registration.

pros: Free health check with no signup barrier
Explains what a section asks and checks the format of your answers
Spanish-language version of the site
cons: Not a lawyer and not part of the government, only software
New registrations and renewals at scale sit behind paid packages

name: ORION Catalyst Calendar
description: ORION is a biotech catalyst calendar that shows the sentence behind every date. Each readout or FDA date links to the SEC filing it came from, both versions are kept when a company changes its wording, and there are no forecasts. It is free with no signup and covers readouts, FDA dates and company-stated windows by ticker, company or program.
description_en: ORION is a biotech catalyst calendar that shows the sentence behind every date. Each readout or FDA date links to the SEC filing it came from, both versions are kept when a company changes its wording, and there are no forecasts. It is free with no signup and covers readouts, FDA dates and company-stated windows by ticker, company or program.

use_cases.title: See the source of a date
use_cases.detail: Every date links back to the SEC sentence that produced it.

use_cases.title: Track wording changes
use_cases.detail: When a company moves from one phrasing to another, both versions are kept.

use_cases.title: Watch a window close
use_cases.detail: Company-stated windows show a countdown to the day they end.

pros: Every date is sourced to a filing rather than estimated
Free and no signup
Revision history of company wording is preserved
cons: Only covers companies with published timing records
Email alerts are listed as temporarily unavailable

name: this+that
description: this+that is a company brain for teams. It keeps operational knowledge in one place, turns the requests arriving in your messages into tasks with an owner through DoBox, assembles a contacts list from your own channels, and exposes the same knowledge to agents through an MCP server and an assistant you can delegate to.
description_en: this+that is a company brain for teams. It keeps operational knowledge in one place, turns the requests arriving in your messages into tasks with an owner through DoBox, assembles a contacts list from your own channels, and exposes the same knowledge to agents through an MCP server and an assistant you can delegate to.

use_cases.title: Stop maintaining the wiki by hand
use_cases.detail: Updates arrive as proposals a person approves instead of manual edits.

use_cases.title: Turn requests into owned tasks
use_cases.detail: DoBox converts what arrives in your messages into tasks with an owner.

use_cases.title: Give agents company context
use_cases.detail: An MCP server exposes the brain to assistants you already use.

pros: Knowledge updates arrive as proposals a human approves
DoBox works from the messages you already receive
MCP server for connecting your own assistants
cons: Aimed at teams, so it is heavy for one person
Pricing is not published on the site

name: A2O LITE AI
description: A2O LITE AI is a dance video generator built around one fixed template. You upload two photos: photo 1 maps to the foreground dancer with white sunglasses in the opening shot and photo 2 to the dancer standing behind at the start, and the tool returns a NEON-style dance duo video. Credit cost is shown before you render, and a short 480p preview costs far less than the full video.
description_en: A2O LITE AI is a dance video generator built around one fixed template. You upload two photos: photo 1 maps to the foreground dancer with white sunglasses in the opening shot and photo 2 to the dancer standing behind at the start, and the tool returns a NEON-style dance duo video. Credit cost is shown before you render, and a short 480p preview costs far less than the full video.

use_cases.title: Make a duo clip from two photos
use_cases.detail: Two photos in, a NEON-style dance duo out, with no timeline to learn.

use_cases.title: Preview before paying
use_cases.detail: A 480p four-second preview costs far fewer credits than the full render.

use_cases.title: Ship a social-ready clip
use_cases.detail: The generator targets one fixed template rather than acting as a general video editor.

pros: No editing skills, choreography or timeline work required
Credit cost is shown before you render
Fixed template makes results predictable
cons: Only does the one NEON duo template
Credit pricing is not shown in a currency on the page

name: OraStage
description: OraStage is a Hotel Lobby AI video generator. You upload two photos or one duo photo and it places your performers in the orange booth beneath a hanging microphone as a rap duo, at 9:16 or 16:9 MP4, in 480p or 720p, at 5, 10 or 15 seconds. The beat is generated rather than licensed, the first video is free with 10 credits, and failed renders are refunded.
description_en: OraStage is a Hotel Lobby AI video generator. You upload two photos or one duo photo and it places your performers in the orange booth beneath a hanging microphone as a rap duo, at 9:16 or 16:9 MP4, in 480p or 720p, at 5, 10 or 15 seconds. The beat is generated rather than licensed, the first video is free with 10 credits, and failed renders are refunded.

use_cases.title: Make a Hotel Lobby clip
use_cases.detail: Two photos become a stage video built for that one scene.

use_cases.title: Pick your format
use_cases.detail: Portrait 9:16 for social or landscape 16:9, at three lengths.

use_cases.title: Try it before paying
use_cases.detail: The first video is free and failed generations are refunded.

pros: First video free and failed renders refunded
Original AI-generated beat, so no licensed track is used
Built for one scene instead of a general tool stretched to fit
cons: Purpose-built for the Hotel Lobby format only
The free tier is limited to starting credits

name: BeatsFlow
description: BeatsFlow is an AI beat maker and four-track stem studio. You generate instrumental beats from a text prompt or from reference audio, isolate four stems (drums, bass, melody and FX), and clone a reference style, with output aimed at finishing in FL Studio, Ableton or Logic Pro. Sign-up is instant with Google and 15 free studio credits need no credit card.
description_en: BeatsFlow is an AI beat maker and four-track stem studio. You generate instrumental beats from a text prompt or from reference audio, isolate four stems (drums, bass, melody and FX), and clone a reference style, with output aimed at finishing in FL Studio, Ableton or Logic Pro. Sign-up is instant with Google and 15 free studio credits need no credit card.

use_cases.title: Start from a prompt
use_cases.detail: Describe the track and audition the synthesized instrumental in the browser.

use_cases.title: Work the stems
use_cases.detail: Split drums, bass, melody and FX for arrangement in your own DAW.

use_cases.title: Match a reference
use_cases.detail: Clone the style of a reference track instead of writing the prompt from scratch.

pros: Four isolated stems ready for real DAW work
15 free studio credits with no credit card required
Reference-audio cloning alongside text prompts
cons: Credit-based, so heavy use becomes a subscription
Showcase leans toward trap, boom bap, lofi and Afrobeats styles

name: Enzyme
description: Enzyme is a local-first compile step for knowledge bases. It reads how your Markdown notes are already organised (folders, tags, links and dates) and builds a local index, so coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex can query your wiki instead of re-reading it. The project claims roughly 350x lower cost and 1000x faster retrieval than handing the same notes to a frontier model.
description_en: Enzyme is a local-first compile step for knowledge bases. It reads how your Markdown notes are already organised (folders, tags, links and dates) and builds a local index, so coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex can query your wiki instead of re-reading it. The project claims roughly 350x lower cost and 1000x faster retrieval than handing the same notes to a frontier model.
best_for: Pointing coding agents at a Markdown wiki
Cutting repeated note reads out of agent runs

use_cases.title: Orient an agent to a wiki
use_cases.detail: Let a coding agent read the structure of your notes rather than pasting them into a chat.

use_cases.title: Search notes locally
use_cases.detail: Query folders, tags, links and dates from an index that stays on your machine.

use_cases.title: Cut retrieval spend
use_cases.detail: Replace repeated full-note reads with indexed lookups during long agent sessions.

pros: Reads the organisation your notes already have instead of forcing a new schema
Index and retrieval stay local
Targets Claude Code and Codex directly
cons: Aimed at Markdown wikis, so other note formats are not covered
Cost and speed figures are the project's own claims

name: Xet Server
description: Xet Server is a Go server that is wire-compatible with Hugging Face's Xet storage protocol, the content-defined-chunking, dedup-first storage layer that replaces Git LFS for large model files on the Hub. You can point the real hf CLI (huggingface_hub plus hf_xet) at it and use hf upload and hf download, with byte-identical round-trips, real BLAKE3 hashing, real xorb and shard binary formats, and real LZ4 and byte-grouping compression.
description_en: Xet Server is a Go server that is wire-compatible with Hugging Face's Xet storage protocol, the content-defined-chunking, dedup-first storage layer that replaces Git LFS for large model files on the Hub. You can point the real hf CLI (huggingface_hub plus hf_xet) at it and use hf upload and hf download, with byte-identical round-trips, real BLAKE3 hashing, real xorb and shard binary formats, and real LZ4 and byte-grouping compression.
best_for: Teams that need S3-compatible dedup for large files

use_cases.title: Run a private model mirror
use_cases.detail: Serve large model files from your own infrastructure with the standard Xet protocol.

use_cases.title: Keep working offline
use_cases.detail: Use the real hf CLI against a local server when the Hub is unreachable.

use_cases.title: Study the protocol
use_cases.detail: Read a from-scratch, spec-driven reimplementation verified end-to-end against a live Hub.

pros: Wire-compatible with the real hf CLI, not a simplified approximation
Content-defined chunking and deduplication built in
Written in Go with an explicit protocol specification
cons: Deeply infrastructure-focused, with a steep setup curve
Depends on matching Hugging Face's evolving wire format

name: Task View
description: Task View turns a coding agent's change into a map instead of a flat diff. It renders a graph of what changed, the flows step by step, and each piece's code next to the reason the agent gave for changing it, checked against Git. The output is a single offline HTML page and works with any language.
description_en: Task View turns a coding agent's change into a map instead of a flat diff. It renders a graph of what changed, the flows step by step, and each piece's code next to the reason the agent gave for changing it, checked against Git. The output is a single offline HTML page and works with any language.
best_for: Teams that review Claude Code or Codex output

use_cases.title: Review a fourteen-file change
use_cases.detail: See how the changed pieces fit together without opening each file in an IDE.

use_cases.title: Follow a request path
use_cases.detail: Read the flows view to see which route a request now takes through the change.

use_cases.title: Check the agent's reason
use_cases.detail: Put each piece's code next to the stated reason and the diff that backs it.

pros: Graph, flows and reasons on one page instead of a linear diff
Offline HTML output with no hosted service required
Language-agnostic
cons: Focused on review, so it does not approve or reject anything
Value depends on the agent recording a reason for each change

name: Argus Agent
description: Argus Agent turns DeepSeek Harness (dsh) into a self-hosted autonomous agent system for running AI agents over days and weeks. It enforces a budget on every run, asks before risky actions and recovers after a crash. You run and watch it from a web interface or from Telegram, with projects that carry their own folder, model, instructions, memory and budget, plus one-off tasks and cron schedules that fire exactly once even across restarts.
description_en: Argus Agent turns DeepSeek Harness (dsh) into a self-hosted autonomous agent system for running AI agents over days and weeks. It enforces a budget on every run, asks before risky actions and recovers after a crash. You run and watch it from a web interface or from Telegram, with projects that carry their own folder, model, instructions, memory and budget, plus one-off tasks and cron schedules that fire exactly once even across restarts.
best_for: Self-hosters who want a budget ceiling per run
Teams that want to supervise agents from Telegram

use_cases.title: Run a weeks-long project
use_cases.detail: Give a research or devops project its own memory, model and budget and let it run.

use_cases.title: Cap the spend
use_cases.detail: Set a budget per run so an autonomous agent cannot run away with costs.

use_cases.title: Schedule recurring work
use_cases.detail: Use cron schedules that fire exactly once even across restarts, delivered to your chat.

pros: Budget enforcement on every run
Web and Telegram control surfaces
Crash recovery and approval gates for risky actions
cons: Built around DeepSeek Harness rather than being harness-agnostic
Self-hosting means you operate the infrastructure yourself

name: Vericto Proxy
description: Vericto Proxy stops destructive SQL before it reaches your PostgreSQL or MySQL database. It is a transparent wire-protocol proxy, so AI agents, scripts and people all keep running SQL with real credentials and no code changes. The project is source-available under FSL-1.1-ALv2 and becomes Apache-2.0 after two years.
description_en: Vericto Proxy stops destructive SQL before it reaches your PostgreSQL or MySQL database. It is a transparent wire-protocol proxy, so AI agents, scripts and people all keep running SQL with real credentials and no code changes. The project is source-available under FSL-1.1-ALv2 and becomes Apache-2.0 after two years.
best_for: Putting a firewall in front of agent database access
Protecting production databases from destructive statements
Teams that cannot modify every script that touches the DB

use_cases.title: Guard agent SQL
use_cases.detail: Sit between an AI agent and production so destructive statements never land.

use_cases.title: Cover scripts and people too
use_cases.detail: Apply one policy to every client, not only to the agent you are worried about.

use_cases.title: Deploy as a container
use_cases.detail: Run the published Docker image as a drop-in wire-protocol proxy.

pros: No code changes in the applications that issue SQL
Covers PostgreSQL and MySQL
Works for agents, scripts and humans alike
cons: Source-available licence is not OSI open source for the first two years
Adds a network hop in front of the database

name: Caudra
description: Caudra is a terminal coding agent shipped as one native binary, with steerable subagents, built-in token savings, a workbench and a history you can revert. The parts are designed together rather than assembled from separate tools, and you can open a running subagent's chat and type guidance that it reads at its next turn while the main agent keeps working.
description_en: Caudra is a terminal coding agent shipped as one native binary, with steerable subagents, built-in token savings, a workbench and a history you can revert. The parts are designed together rather than assembled from separate tools, and you can open a running subagent's chat and type guidance that it reads at its next turn while the main agent keeps working.
best_for: Developers who want one self-contained coding agent binary
Reverting agent history after a bad turn

use_cases.title: Guide a running subagent
use_cases.detail: Open a background task's chat and type; the guidance is queued for its next turn.

use_cases.title: Keep token spend down
use_cases.detail: Rely on built-in token savings rather than bolting on a separate compressor.

use_cases.title: Roll back
use_cases.detail: Revert history when a run goes somewhere you did not want.

pros: Single native binary with no runtime to install
Subagents you can steer while they run
Revertible history
cons: New project, so the ecosystem around it is small
Terminal-first, with no graphical IDE surface

name: Mnemolith
description: Mnemolith is shared local memory for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that stays true to your code. Memories go stale when the code they describe changes, so an edit to a file such as docker-compose.yml flags the memory that described it and lets you record what is true now. The project was formerly called Aether Cache and existing memories carry over.
description_en: Mnemolith is shared local memory for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that stays true to your code. Memories go stale when the code they describe changes, so an edit to a file such as docker-compose.yml flags the memory that described it and lets you record what is true now. The project was formerly called Aether Cache and existing memories carry over.
best_for: Sharing one memory across several coding agents
Keeping agent memory honest as code drifts
Developers who switch between Claude Code, Cursor and Codex

use_cases.title: Share memory across tools
use_cases.detail: Let Claude Code, Cursor and Codex read the same memory instead of three separate ones.

use_cases.title: Catch stale memories
use_cases.detail: See a memory flagged when the file it describes has changed underneath it.

use_cases.title: Migrate from Aether Cache
use_cases.detail: Move an existing aether-cache install over with your memories intact.

pros: Explicit staleness detection tied to real file changes
One memory shared across multiple coding tools
Python package with a published website and PyPI release
cons: Python-based, so it adds an install step to each environment
Staleness handling still depends on you recording what is true now

name: Pith
description: Pith cuts LLM output-token spend without losing information. It watches a route, replays a sample under cheaper output profiles, has a judge compare every answer with the baseline, and pins a profile only when it is as good as the baseline is with itself. When it is not, Pith says so and changes nothing.
description_en: Pith cuts LLM output-token spend without losing information. It watches a route, replays a sample under cheaper output profiles, has a judge compare every answer with the baseline, and pins a profile only when it is as good as the baseline is with itself. When it is not, Pith says so and changes nothing.
best_for: Cutting output-token costs on a live route
Teams that need evidence before changing a prompt
Anyone wary of silent quality regressions from compression

use_cases.title: Tune a route
use_cases.detail: Replay real traffic under cheaper output profiles and compare answers.

use_cases.title: Judge before pinning
use_cases.detail: Let a judge compare every candidate answer against the baseline before anything changes.

use_cases.title: Fail safe
use_cases.detail: Receive a refusal instead of a silent degradation when savings would drop content.

pros: Refuses to change anything when the saving costs information
Judged replays rather than heuristic trimming
Installable from PyPI as pith-optimizer
cons: Needs real sample traffic to judge against
Focused on output tokens, not on prompt or context size

name: Aw1 Circuit Breaker
description: Aw1 Circuit Breaker is a deterministic AST security circuit breaker for autonomous AI agents, tool dispatch pipelines and MCP servers, with the project quoting sub-0.2ms evaluation. Rather than asking a model to judge whether an action is safe, it inspects the syntax tree of the action and blocks it before dispatch.
description_en: Aw1 Circuit Breaker is a deterministic AST security circuit breaker for autonomous AI agents, tool dispatch pipelines and MCP servers, with the project quoting sub-0.2ms evaluation. Rather than asking a model to judge whether an action is safe, it inspects the syntax tree of the action and blocks it before dispatch.
best_for: Teams that do not trust model-based safety judgement

use_cases.title: Break the circuit
use_cases.detail: Stop a dangerous action at dispatch time instead of after the tool runs.

use_cases.title: Guard tool pipelines
use_cases.detail: Insert the breaker into a tool dispatch pipeline without a model in the loop.

use_cases.title: Keep latency flat
use_cases.detail: Rely on sub-millisecond AST evaluation rather than an extra model call.

pros: Deterministic rules, so the same input always gets the same verdict
No model call in the decision path
Published on PyPI for Python 3.10 through 3.13
cons: Covers what the AST rules encode, not every possible unsafe behaviour
Python-focused despite the low-level positioning

name: Forked
description: Forked is Git for agent state: it lets AI agents fork, rewind and replay their structured state (messages, memory, plans and tool results) with a side-effect log that keeps emails, payments and API calls effectively-once across retries and rewinds. Recorded idempotency keys replay their stored result instead of re-running the action, and there is a Rust core you can self-host or run in the cloud.
description_en: Forked is Git for agent state: it lets AI agents fork, rewind and replay their structured state (messages, memory, plans and tool results) with a side-effect log that keeps emails, payments and API calls effectively-once across retries and rewinds. Recorded idempotency keys replay their stored result instead of re-running the action, and there is a Rust core you can self-host or run in the cloud.
best_for: Agents that take real-world side effects
Replaying a failed run from an earlier step
Teams worried about double-charging on retry

use_cases.title: Retry without double charging
use_cases.detail: Replay a stored payment result instead of re-running the charge after a crash.

use_cases.title: Explore an alternative
use_cases.detail: Fork a session to try another approach while the original head stays anchored.

use_cases.title: Rewind state
use_cases.detail: Roll messages, memory and plans back to an earlier point.

pros: Effectively-once side effects across retries and rewinds
Rust core with self-host or cloud options
Structured state, not just a transcript
cons: Strict guarantees assume a single writer at a time
Requires instrumenting your agent's side effects

name: Flint
description: Flint gives AI agents tools to use fewer tokens and keep more useful context: reversible compression for code, JSON and text, persistent memory for decisions, focused reads and version-aware edits. It works at the agent-tool layer, so you connect the CLI or JSON interface to your workflow independently of your model or provider. Python 3.11 or newer, Linux or WSL, standard library core, no model or server required.
description_en: Flint gives AI agents tools to use fewer tokens and keep more useful context: reversible compression for code, JSON and text, persistent memory for decisions, focused reads and version-aware edits. It works at the agent-tool layer, so you connect the CLI or JSON interface to your workflow independently of your model or provider. Python 3.11 or newer, Linux or WSL, standard library core, no model or server required.
best_for: Compressing context without losing the original
Agents that re-read the same large files

use_cases.title: Compress a payload
use_cases.detail: Shrink code, JSON or text and restore the original when the agent needs it.

use_cases.title: Read narrowly
use_cases.detail: Use focused reads so the agent pulls only the part of a file it needs.

use_cases.title: Edit against a version
use_cases.detail: Tie edits to file versions so a stale context cannot overwrite newer content.

pros: Reversible compression, so nothing is thrown away permanently
No model, server or provider dependency
Standard library core keeps installation light
cons: Linux and WSL only, with no Windows or macOS support
You have to wire the CLI or JSON interface into your own workflow

name: Unterm
description: Unterm is a terminal that AI agents can drive, plus the cockpit to run them from. It exposes 151 MCP methods, an agent Inbox, git-worktree fleets, diff review and rollback, and one-click updates. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, is local-first and free, and is released under MIT. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Aider can all control it over MCP.
description_en: Unterm is a terminal that AI agents can drive, plus the cockpit to run them from. It exposes 151 MCP methods, an agent Inbox, git-worktree fleets, diff review and rollback, and one-click updates. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, is local-first and free, and is released under MIT. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Aider can all control it over MCP.
best_for: Running several coding agents at once
Giving an agent real terminal control
Reviewing and rolling back agent terminal work

use_cases.title: Watch a fleet
use_cases.detail: Run agents in separate git worktrees and let the Inbox surface the one that needs you.

use_cases.title: Drive the terminal
use_cases.detail: Let any MCP-capable agent control the terminal over 151 methods.

use_cases.title: Review and revert
use_cases.detail: Inspect diffs from agent runs and roll back the ones you do not want.

pros: Broad MCP surface covering 151 methods
Cross-platform and local-first
Agent Inbox for triaging several running agents
cons: Replacing your terminal is a bigger commitment than adding a plugin
151 methods is a large surface to learn

name: Mnestiq
description: Mnestiq is a flight recorder for AI agents: signed, tamper-evident records of what an agent saw, decided and did, covering model calls, tool calls and network connections. It is built for incident response rather than dashboards, so it can show which run and step acted, that an instruction came from a web page rather than the user, and that a policy waved it through, and prove none of it was edited afterwards.
description_en: Mnestiq is a flight recorder for AI agents: signed, tamper-evident records of what an agent saw, decided and did, covering model calls, tool calls and network connections. It is built for incident response rather than dashboards, so it can show which run and step acted, that an instruction came from a web page rather than the user, and that a policy waved it through, and prove none of it was edited afterwards.
best_for: Incident response after an agent misbehaves
Proving what an agent did after the fact
Teams with compliance or audit obligations

use_cases.title: Investigate an exfiltration
use_cases.detail: Identify the exact run and step that sent data, and what authorised it.

use_cases.title: Trace untrusted input
use_cases.detail: Show that a instruction entered the run from a fetched web page earlier in the session.

use_cases.title: Prove the log is intact
use_cases.detail: Rely on signed records that cannot be quietly rewritten.

pros: Signed and tamper-evident rather than best-effort logging
Built around incident questions, not vanity metrics
Records network connections alongside model and tool calls
cons: Aimed at forensics, so it is not a live monitoring dashboard
Python package that needs instrumenting into your agent

name: QAmcp CLI
description: QAmcp tests any MCP server in one command, covering tools, safety labels, hidden instructions, bad inputs, leaked secrets, OAuth login setup, resources and prompts. Every result is a hard fact such as pass or fail, milliseconds and exact matches: no AI judges anything, and nothing is sent anywhere except to the server you test. It ships as a CLI and a GitHub Action.
description_en: QAmcp tests any MCP server in one command, covering tools, safety labels, hidden instructions, bad inputs, leaked secrets, OAuth login setup, resources and prompts. Every result is a hard fact such as pass or fail, milliseconds and exact matches: no AI judges anything, and nothing is sent anywhere except to the server you test. It ships as a CLI and a GitHub Action.
best_for: Catching hidden instructions in third-party servers

use_cases.title: Test a server
use_cases.detail: Run one command against a server URL and get a plain-language report.

use_cases.title: Gate every change
use_cases.detail: Run the GitHub Action so a broken tool definition fails the build.

use_cases.title: Audit a third party
use_cases.detail: Look for hidden instructions, leaked secrets and missing safety labels before you install.

pros: Deterministic results with no model in the judgement loop
CLI plus GitHub Action for continuous testing
Nothing leaves your machine except the calls to the server under test
cons: Requires Node.js 20 or newer
Covers protocol-level correctness, not whether the tool is useful

name: mcpspan
description: mcpspan is open-source, self-hosted analytics for MCP servers. You add one line to your MCP server and run the dashboard with docker compose up, then see which tools, resources and prompts get used, by which client, how fast they answer and why they fail. Nothing leaves your machine.
description_en: mcpspan is open-source, self-hosted analytics for MCP servers. You add one line to your MCP server and run the dashboard with docker compose up, then see which tools, resources and prompts get used, by which client, how fast they answer and why they fail. Nothing leaves your machine.
best_for: MCP server authors who want usage data
Self-hosters who will not ship telemetry offsite
Comparing versions of a server after a release

use_cases.title: See real usage
use_cases.detail: Find out which tools clients actually call and which ones never fire.

use_cases.title: Track failures
use_cases.detail: Read why calls fail and how latency moves between releases.

use_cases.title: Compare versions
use_cases.detail: Put release markers on the timeline and compare versions side by side.

pros: One-line integration and a docker compose dashboard
Fully self-hosted, with no data leaving the machine
Per-client attribution across Claude, Claude Code and Cursor
cons: You operate the dashboard yourself
Analytics only, with no alerting described

name: Murmur
description: Murmur is a free, open-source macOS menu bar dictation app: hold a key, speak, let go, and your words appear at the cursor in any app. It uses your own OpenAI API key for speech-to-text and is positioned as an alternative to Wispr Flow and Superwhisper. It is built with Swift and SwiftUI, requires macOS 14 or later and is released under MIT.
description_en: Murmur is a free, open-source macOS menu bar dictation app: hold a key, speak, let go, and your words appear at the cursor in any app. It uses your own OpenAI API key for speech-to-text and is positioned as an alternative to Wispr Flow and Superwhisper. It is built with Swift and SwiftUI, requires macOS 14 or later and is released under MIT.
best_for: Developers who already hold an OpenAI API key
Anyone replacing a paid dictation subscription

use_cases.title: Dictate anywhere
use_cases.detail: Push to talk and drop text into whatever app you are typing in.

use_cases.title: Bring your own key
use_cases.detail: Point Murmur at your own OpenAI API key instead of paying a per-seat fee.

use_cases.title: Keep it in the menu bar
use_cases.detail: Run dictation as a lightweight native macOS app rather than a browser tool.

pros: Free and MIT-licensed
Bring-your-own-key means no subscription to the app vendor
Native Swift and SwiftUI macOS app
cons: macOS only, version 14 or later
You need your own OpenAI API key and pay for transcription usage

name: SentinelMCP
description: SentinelMCP is a stateless enterprise policy firewall and token-cost proxy for the Model Context Protocol. You drop it in front of any MCP server and every tool call is checked for identity, policy and budget before it reaches your infrastructure. There is no database and no sticky sessions, so there is nothing new to operate at 3am, and a demo image runs with a single docker command.
description_en: SentinelMCP is a stateless enterprise policy firewall and token-cost proxy for the Model Context Protocol. You drop it in front of any MCP server and every tool call is checked for identity, policy and budget before it reaches your infrastructure. There is no database and no sticky sessions, so there is nothing new to operate at 3am, and a demo image runs with a single docker command.
best_for: Putting policy in front of MCP servers
Enforcing a token budget per tool call
Teams that refuse to operate another stateful service

use_cases.title: Check every call
use_cases.detail: Validate identity, policy and budget on each tool call before it is forwarded.

use_cases.title: Cap token spend
use_cases.detail: Use the proxy as a cost gate as well as a policy gate.

use_cases.title: Try it quickly
use_cases.detail: Run the published demo container with one docker command.

pros: Stateless design, with no database to run
Combines policy and token-cost enforcement
One-command demo container
cons: Enterprise framing means the policy model takes effort to configure
Adds a proxy hop in front of each MCP server

name: Rubi
description: Rubi is a knowledge graph and context manager for AI coding agents, working with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and local models. It builds a code map with PageRank, keeps a temporal knowledge graph, offers hybrid search, and does early compaction with handoffs so sessions get shorter and projects stay organised.
description_en: Rubi is a knowledge graph and context manager for AI coding agents, working with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and local models. It builds a code map with PageRank, keeps a temporal knowledge graph, offers hybrid search, and does early compaction with handoffs so sessions get shorter and projects stay organised.
best_for: Large codebases where agents re-read too much
Local-model users who need context discipline

use_cases.title: Map the code
use_cases.detail: Build a code map ranked by PageRank so the agent knows what matters first.

use_cases.title: Search hybrid
use_cases.detail: Combine graph and vector style retrieval over the project.

use_cases.title: Compact early
use_cases.detail: Hand off a compacted context instead of letting a session grow unbounded.

pros: Works with hosted and local models alike
Temporal knowledge graph, not a static index
Claude Code plugin plus a live demo
cons: Adds a graph layer you have to maintain alongside the repo
Benefit grows with codebase size, so small projects see less

name: Secret Guard
description: Secret Guard is a lightweight local LLM gateway that protects your secrets. Outbound requests have secrets replaced with equal-length realistic mocks, and responses are restored back to real values on the way in, so the LLM never touches a real secret while your agent's tools keep working. It is written in Rust and supports multiple protocols.
description_en: Secret Guard is a lightweight local LLM gateway that protects your secrets. Outbound requests have secrets replaced with equal-length realistic mocks, and responses are restored back to real values on the way in, so the LLM never touches a real secret while your agent's tools keep working. It is written in Rust and supports multiple protocols.
best_for: Using hosted models without exposing keys
Agents that handle credentials in their context
Teams with a policy against sending secrets to providers

use_cases.title: Redact on the way out
use_cases.detail: Swap real credentials for equal-length mocks before a request leaves your machine.

use_cases.title: Restore on the way back
use_cases.detail: Put the real values into the response locally so tools still function.

use_cases.title: Keep length intact
use_cases.detail: Preserve token shape so redaction does not disturb the model's formatting.

pros: Equal-length mocks keep prompts structurally intact
Restores real values locally so agent tools still work
Runs locally as a gateway, no hosted component
cons: Requires routing all model traffic through the gateway
Mock fidelity still depends on the redaction patterns configured

name: GoRoute
description: GoRoute is a high-performance LLM gateway and multi-provider router for coding agents, with a Go core plus Rust SIMD acceleration. The project quotes 0.86ms latency and under 5MB of resident memory, alongside multi-account pooling, support for 338+ providers, autonomous cascades, prompt caching, context compression and vault sync across 35 CLI agents.
description_en: GoRoute is a high-performance LLM gateway and multi-provider router for coding agents, with a Go core plus Rust SIMD acceleration. The project quotes 0.86ms latency and under 5MB of resident memory, alongside multi-account pooling, support for 338+ providers, autonomous cascades, prompt caching, context compression and vault sync across 35 CLI agents.
best_for: Routing many coding agents through one gateway
Self-hosters who care about gateway overhead

use_cases.title: Route coding agents
use_cases.detail: Point CLI agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Aider and opencode at one gateway.

use_cases.title: Pool accounts
use_cases.detail: Spread load across multiple provider accounts with a single endpoint.

use_cases.title: Cascade on failure
use_cases.detail: Let the gateway fall through providers automatically when one fails.

pros: Very small memory and latency footprint for a gateway
338+ providers and 35 CLI agents supported
Multi-account pooling and autonomous cascades
cons: Performance figures are the project's own claims

name: Rowan

name: Argus
description: Argus is an open-source security operations platform where AI agents do the legwork and you stay in control. It watches your cloud, identity, code, endpoints, network and Kubernetes, catches attacks at machine speed, investigates them with AI agents and contains them in seconds. Local-first and self-hostable
Plugins exist for several agents and harnesses
cons: A full workspace is more to set up than a single memory file
Documentation is spread across several languages

name: MuscleMemory
description: MuscleMemory is open-source procedural memory for AI agents that learns from what worked and what failed. Coding agents relearn the same things every session, so MuscleMemory watches your agent work, and when a task really succeeds it learns how the task was done. The next time a similar task comes up it hands the agent a short note. It is local by default and Apache-2.0 licensed.
description_en: MuscleMemory is open-source procedural memory for AI agents that learns from what worked and what failed. Coding agents relearn the same things every session, so MuscleMemory watches your agent work, and when a task really succeeds it learns how the task was done. The next time a similar task comes up it hands the agent a short note. It is local by default and Apache-2.0 licensed.

use_cases.title: Learn from a passing test
use_cases.detail: When the tests pass after the last change, MuscleMemory records how the task was done.

use_cases.title: Recall it next time
use_cases.detail: A similar task later gets a short note handed to the agent.

use_cases.title: Run it locally
use_cases.detail: Local setup, Docker and PostgreSQL are all documented, with MCP and SDK integrations.

pros: Learns from real success rather than stored chatter
Local by default under Apache-2.0
MCP plus SDK integrations for different agents
cons: Only learns when a task verifiably succeeds
Needs a store such as PostgreSQL for team use

name: ReliaMesh
description: ReliaMesh is open-source reliability infrastructure for AI agents. It ingests structured outcomes, detects reliability deterioration and tracks recovery without collecting prompts, model responses or tool content, because an API returning HTTP 200 does not establish that an agent completed its task. It ships with authenticated ingestion, a Python SDK, deterministic detection and SQLite self-hosting.
description_en: ReliaMesh is open-source reliability infrastructure for AI agents. It ingests structured outcomes, detects reliability deterioration and tracks recovery without collecting prompts, model responses or tool content, because an API returning HTTP 200 does not establish that an agent completed its task. It ships with authenticated ingestion, a Python SDK, deterministic detection and SQLite self-hosting.

use_cases.title: Send outcomes, not content
use_cases.detail: The event contract rejects prompts, responses and tool arguments.

use_cases.title: Catch regressions by version
use_cases.detail: Deterministic detection flags reliability changes tied to a version.

use_cases.title: Self-host it
use_cases.detail: SQLite self-hosting needs no managed account.

pros: No prompts or responses are collected at all
Deterministic detection rather than model judgement
Apache-2.0 with a Python SDK and self-hosting
cons: Early release with evidence still being gathered
You must instrument your agent to emit the event contract

name: CommonForge
description: CommonForge is for many agents and people changing one project at once, running on Cloudflare Workers and Artifacts, so your project's understanding survives the agent. It installs through the cforge CLI published on npm and is MIT licensed.
description_en: CommonForge is for many agents and people changing one project at once, running on Cloudflare Workers and Artifacts, so your project's understanding survives the agent. It installs through the cforge CLI published on npm and is MIT licensed.

use_cases.title: Let several agents edit at once
use_cases.detail: Built for many agents and people changing one project simultaneously.

use_cases.title: Keep understanding between sessions
use_cases.detail: The project's understanding survives each individual agent run.

use_cases.title: Install from npm
use_cases.detail: The cforge CLI is the entry point.

pros: Runs on Cloudflare Workers and Artifacts
MIT licensed with an npm CLI
Aimed squarely at concurrent agent work
cons: Requires a Cloudflare stack
Early project with a narrow deployment target

name: Imagor MCP
description: Imagor MCP is an MCP server and a skill that add a template layer to imagor, the fast image processing server. An agent writes a layout, such as OG cards, product grids, quotes or testimonials, and it compiles to one imagor URL rendered by the imagor you already run.
description_en: Imagor MCP is an MCP server and a skill that add a template layer to imagor, the fast image processing server. An agent writes a layout, such as OG cards, product grids, quotes or testimonials, and it compiles to one imagor URL rendered by the imagor you already run.

use_cases.title: Describe a layout in words
use_cases.detail: The agent writes the layout and it compiles to a single URL.

use_cases.title: Render on your own server
use_cases.detail: Images are rendered by the imagor instance you already run.

use_cases.detail: A cookbook of example layouts is included.

pros: One URL per layout, no asset pipeline to manage
Works with the imagor you already run
Ships as both an MCP server and a skill
cons: You need a running imagor with unsafe mode enabled
Layouts are limited to what imagor filters can express

name: Sonia Assistant
description: Sonia is a local voice assistant that combines an LLM with speech-to-text and text-to-speech and needs no dedicated GPU, running in less than 15 GB of RAM entirely on a local computer. It is multilingual and full-duplex, so the microphone stays open while the assistant talks and you can interrupt it and it pauses, resumes or cancels accordingly. The only external piece is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
description_en: Sonia is a local voice assistant that combines an LLM with speech-to-text and text-to-speech and needs no dedicated GPU, running in less than 15 GB of RAM entirely on a local computer. It is multilingual and full-duplex, so the microphone stays open while the assistant talks and you can interrupt it and it pauses, resumes or cancels accordingly. The only external piece is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

use_cases.title: Run it without a GPU
use_cases.detail: Everything runs locally in under 15 GB of RAM.

use_cases.title: Talk over the assistant
use_cases.detail: Full-duplex audio means barge-in pauses, resumes or cancels.

use_cases.title: Point it at your own model
use_cases.detail: It talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as a running llama-server.

pros: No dedicated GPU required
Full-duplex audio with real barge-in handling
Mirrors the language you speak
cons: You must run an OpenAI-compatible endpoint yourself
English and Italian are the tested languages

name: Hatoba
description: Hatoba is an open-source desktop SSH client with an AI assistant and end-to-end encrypted sync through your own Cloudflare account. You describe the problem in a panel beside your terminal and the assistant reads the screen and runs commands. It is built with Tauri 2 and released for Windows, Linux and macOS.
description_en: Hatoba is an open-source desktop SSH client with an AI assistant and end-to-end encrypted sync through your own Cloudflare account. You describe the problem in a panel beside your terminal and the assistant reads the screen and runs commands. It is built with Tauri 2 and released for Windows, Linux and macOS.

Sync is end-to-end encrypted and under your own account
The assistant reads the terminal rather than guessing
cons: Sync depends on you having a Cloudflare account
You supply the model behind the assistant

name: Guilds
description: Guilds is an open-source alternative to Grok bots: a team of AI agents without the black box. Multi-agent workflows are easy to start but hard to trust, so it shows you the exact prompt, every tool call and every memory change, so you do not have to trust, you can verify. It runs on your machine with any model.
description_en: Guilds is an open-source alternative to Grok bots: a team of AI agents without the black box. Multi-agent workflows are easy to start but hard to trust, so it shows you the exact prompt, every tool call and every memory change, so you do not have to trust, you can verify. It runs on your machine with any model.

use_cases.title: See the exact prompt
use_cases.detail: Every prompt, tool call and memory change is shown.

use_cases.title: Run teams on your machine
use_cases.detail: Guilds runs locally with any model you choose.

use_cases.title: Start from a recipe
use_cases.detail: Recipes for coding and other work are provided.

pros: Every prompt, tool call and memory change is inspectable
Runs on your own machine with any model
Open source

Multi-agent setups are still fiddly to tune

name: Weft
description: Weft coordinates coding agents while they edit, not only when they open a pull request. Agents submit tool-call edits to a per-repository sequencer, which validates each edit against accepted changes since the agent's base and returns actionable diagnostics through the agent's native hooks. Humans see the same event stream and can approve, pause, message, undo or inspect evidence, with no file locks and no waiting for a human merge.
description_en: Weft coordinates coding agents while they edit, not only when they open a pull request. Agents submit tool-call edits to a per-repository sequencer, which validates each edit against accepted changes since the agent's base and returns actionable diagnostics through the agent's native hooks. Humans see the same event stream and can approve, pause, message, undo or inspect evidence, with no file locks and no waiting for a human merge.

use_cases.title: Sequence edits as they happen
use_cases.detail: A per-repository sequencer validates each edit against accepted changes.

use_cases.title: Get diagnostics back
use_cases.detail: Agents receive actionable diagnostics through their own native hooks.

use_cases.title: Watch the same stream
use_cases.detail: Humans see the same events and can approve, pause, undo or inspect evidence.

pros: Coordination happens during editing, not at the pull request
Harness-neutral wire protocol with Cloudflare-backed adapters
No file locks and no blocking on a human merge
cons: Status is a research and demo implementation, and WCP v0.1 is a draft
Requires adapters for your harness

name: Braus
description: Braus gives agents a desktop workspace on your Mac, so agents work in your apps while you keep using your Mac. You give a worker a task in the Braus app, or connect Claude Code or Codex through MCP to work in desktop apps, even when they expose neither an API nor an accessibility tree.
description_en: Braus gives agents a desktop workspace on your Mac, so agents work in your apps while you keep using your Mac. You give a worker a task in the Braus app, or connect Claude Code or Codex through MCP to work in desktop apps, even when they expose neither an API nor an accessibility tree.

use_cases.title: Give a worker a task
use_cases.detail: Tasks are handed over in the Braus app itself.

use_cases.title: Connect your coding agent
use_cases.detail: Claude Code or Codex can work in desktop apps over MCP.

use_cases.title: Reach apps with no API
use_cases.detail: It works even when an app exposes no API and no accessibility tree.

pros: Works with desktop apps that expose no API
MCP connection for Claude Code and Codex
Your Mac stays usable while the agent works
cons: macOS only
Giving an agent the desktop means giving it broad access

name: OpenComputerUse
description: OpenComputerUse is computer use for agents that runs in the background, as an MCP server. You start a session with an app and get back a session id, drive the app with that id, then end the session. The app works behind your other windows and your pointer, keyboard focus and frontmost app stay where they are, and sessions end when the MCP server exits.
description_en: OpenComputerUse is computer use for agents that runs in the background, as an MCP server. You start a session with an app and get back a session id, drive the app with that id, then end the session. The app works behind your other windows and your pointer, keyboard focus and frontmost app stay where they are, and sessions end when the MCP server exits.

use_cases.title: Drive an app in the background
use_cases.detail: Start a session, use the returned id, and end it when done.

use_cases.title: Keep working meanwhile
use_cases.detail: The pointer, keyboard focus and frontmost app stay yours.

use_cases.title: Install it with Homebrew
use_cases.detail: On macOS it installs as a cask from a third-party tap.

pros: Background operation leaves your pointer and focus untouched
Session ids make multi-app automation explicit
Open source and installable via Homebrew
cons: Homebrew will not load casks from a third-party tap until you trust it
macOS-first; other platforms need more work

name: TinyWebUI
description: TinyWebUI is a small, local-first chat workspace for any OpenAI-compatible model, with web search and long-term memory already connected. It keeps your chats, documents and tool output in one SQLite file on your machine, and it comes with MCP tools, installing with npx tinywebui.
description_en: TinyWebUI is a small, local-first chat workspace for any OpenAI-compatible model, with web search and long-term memory already connected. It keeps your chats, documents and tool output in one SQLite file on your machine, and it comes with MCP tools, installing with npx tinywebui.

use_cases.title: Chat with any model
use_cases.detail: It works against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

use_cases.title: Search and remember
use_cases.detail: Web research and long-term memory are switched on from the start.

use_cases.title: Keep one file
use_cases.detail: Chats, documents and tool output live in a single SQLite file.

pros: Web search and memory are bundled and already connected
Everything is stored in one SQLite file you control
Installs with a single npx command
cons: You provide the model endpoint and its cost
Two bundled MCP servers means more moving parts than a plain chat

name: Reika
description: Reika is a coding agent CLI for local and hosted models, designed around small local models first, so it is careful with context, fails more gracefully and says when it is stuck. It does not make a small model smarter; it makes working with one less frustrating. It installs with npm i -g @alexwkleung/reika.
description_en: Reika is a coding agent CLI for local and hosted models, designed around small local models first, so it is careful with context, fails more gracefully and says when it is stuck. It does not make a small model smarter; it makes working with one less frustrating. It installs with npm i -g @alexwkleung/reika.

use_cases.title: Run a local model
use_cases.detail: Designed first for the small models you can actually host.

use_cases.title: Spend less context
use_cases.detail: It is careful with how much context each step consumes.

use_cases.title: Know when it is stuck
use_cases.detail: Reika says so rather than thrashing.

pros: Built for small local models rather than frontier APIs
Fails gracefully and reports being stuck
Installs from npm in one command
cons: A small model still writes worse code than a large one
You need your own local inference setup

name: TaskHandoff
description: TaskHandoff is a self-hosted control plane for running, managing and collaborating with AI workspaces across local and remote machines, an open-source alternative to Codex Desktop's cross-device control. It runs Codex and OpenCode in one workbench for AI development, workspace management and code review, and ships an agent skill that teaches your agent to drive the control plane.
description_en: TaskHandoff is a self-hosted control plane for running, managing and collaborating with AI workspaces across local and remote machines, an open-source alternative to Codex Desktop's cross-device control. It runs Codex and OpenCode in one workbench for AI development, workspace management and code review, and ships an agent skill that teaches your agent to drive the control plane.

use_cases.title: Run agents on any machine
use_cases.detail: One control plane covers local and remote AI development.

use_cases.title: Use the tools you have

use_cases.title: Teach your agent
use_cases.detail: An installable skill tells your agent how to drive TaskHandoff.

pros: Self-hosted and Apache-2.0 licensed
Covers Codex and OpenCode in one workbench
An agent skill automates the connection
cons: Requires Docker and a server to be useful
Node.js 24 and a Vue front end to operate

name: DeepSearch
description: DeepSearch is an independent web search client for the DeepSeek API. Once you sign in it returns ranked web results with source metadata, and it is not affiliated with DeepSeek.
description_en: DeepSearch is an independent web search client for the DeepSeek API. Once you sign in it returns ranked web results with source metadata, and it is not affiliated with DeepSeek.

use_cases.title: Search the web
use_cases.detail: Type a query and get ranked results back.

use_cases.title: See where a result came from
use_cases.detail: Results come with source metadata attached.

use_cases.title: Bring your own API access
use_cases.detail: It is a client for the DeepSeek API, so you sign in to use it.

Independent client rather than a locked-in portal
Simple single-purpose interface

Pricing is not stated on the site

name: CowAgent
description: CowAgent is an open-source super AI assistant and agent harness that plans tasks, runs tools and skills, and autonomously grows with memory and knowledge. It decomposes complex tasks and executes them step by step, looping over tools and skills until the goal is reached, and uses a three-tier memory architecture with hybrid keyword and vector retrieval. It is multi-model, multi-channel and multi-agent, installs with one command, and runs 24/7 on a laptop or server.
description_en: CowAgent is an open-source super AI assistant and agent harness that plans tasks, runs tools and skills, and autonomously grows with memory and knowledge. It decomposes complex tasks and executes them step by step, looping over tools and skills until the goal is reached, and uses a three-tier memory architecture with hybrid keyword and vector retrieval. It is multi-model, multi-channel and multi-agent, installs with one command, and runs 24/7 on a laptop or server.

use_cases.title: Hand over a complex task
use_cases.detail: It decomposes the task and loops over tools and skills until it is done.

use_cases.title: Let it remember
use_cases.detail: Three-tier memory with automatic distillation and hybrid retrieval.

use_cases.title: Run it unattended
use_cases.detail: One command installs it and it runs 24/7 on your machine or server.

Multi-model, multi-channel and multi-agent
Three-tier memory with automatic distillation
