You bring your own model providers

name: ConferenceFindr
description: ConferenceFindr is a finder for business conferences, expos and trade shows, with an MCP server. You search thousands of upcoming business events across dozens of countries by industry, location, date and ticket price, including filters for free events and price ceilings.
description_en: ConferenceFindr is a finder for business conferences, expos and trade shows, with an MCP server. You search thousands of upcoming business events across dozens of countries by industry, location, date and ticket price, including filters for free events and price ceilings.

use_cases.title: Filter by price

use_cases.title: Narrow by place and time
use_cases.detail: Search by country, radius and upcoming date windows.

Price and date filters make shortlists fast
Exposes an MCP server for agent use
cons: Pricing for the service is not published on the site
Coverage will vary by industry and region

name: Lemoncode
description: Lemon Code is a free coding agent: you describe what you want, and it writes the code, runs it and shows the result, with a preview, the list of changed files and the terminal output. It also automates workflows by connecting to GitHub, Slack, Notion, Gmail, Jira, Linear and more than 1,500 other apps plus your own MCP servers, once or on a schedule.

Very large app catalogue plus custom MCP servers
Shows the diff, the terminal and the live preview

New product, so limits may apply

name: Bonbook MCP
description: BonBook Travel is an MCP connector that lets you book flights by chatting with Claude. You paste one address into Claude's custom connector settings, name it, and connect; then you ask for a flight in a new chat. Your first booking opens a secure bonbook.co checkout page, and after that you can just say which option to book.

Limited to what the travel connector supports

name: Finance Toolkit MCP
description: The Finance Toolkit MCP server takes financial calculations out of the model's hands. It exposes 500+ metrics in 22 tools plus 3 for search, and calculates numbers rather than recalling them, so the same number comes back in any model. It is MIT licensed, can be used hosted for free or run locally, and works with Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor and more.

name: LongTerMemory
description: LongTerMemory turns your own materials into an AI study plan with daily sessions and smart reviews. You import PDFs, docs, slides, web links, notes and photos, and it produces auto-generated quizzes, chat over your notes, image OCR for photographed pages, spaced repetition and mnemonics. Handles photographed pages through OCR

Quality depends on the material you import

name: MarkItDown AI
description: MarkItDown Online is a browser-based converter that turns PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON and XML into clean Markdown, preserving useful structure such as headings, lists and tables. The Basic tier runs locally in your browser with no upload, while Advanced handles scanned or complex files.
description_en: MarkItDown Online is a browser-based converter that turns PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON and XML into clean Markdown, preserving useful structure such as headings, lists and tables. use_cases.title: Convert a document
use_cases.detail: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON and XML are supported.

use_cases.title: Keep it on the device
use_cases.detail: Browser Basic processes locally with no upload.

use_cases.title: Handle the hard ones
use_cases.detail: Advanced adds OCR for scanned or complex layouts.

name: Connecting Captions
description: Connecting Captions gives you live on-device captions on a Mac, with each sentence appearing when it is ready. Use it for a presentation, a bilingual room or any conversation that needs a translation. Speech recognition and Apple Translation run on the Mac itself, so voice never leaves the machine unless you turn on a cloud speech model. There is no account and no telemetry.
description_en: Connecting Captions gives you live on-device captions on a Mac, with each sentence appearing when it is ready. Use it for a presentation, a bilingual room or any conversation that needs a translation. Speech recognition and Apple Translation run on the Mac itself, so voice never leaves the machine unless you turn on a cloud speech model. There is no account and no telemetry.

use_cases.title: Caption a presentation

use_cases.title: Run a bilingual room

25 languages with caption or translation output
Captions appear sentence by sentence as they are ready

name: Sys2txt
description: sys2txt is a command-line tool that records your system audio with ffmpeg and transcribes it locally using Whisper. It works on demand, recording until you stop and transcribing once, or in live mode, segmenting the recording every N seconds and printing each transcription as it is created. You can use faster-whisper, openai-whisper or whisper.cpp, and it auto-selects whichever is installed.
description_en: sys2txt is a command-line tool that records your system audio with ffmpeg and transcribes it locally using Whisper. It works on demand, recording until you stop and transcribing once, or in live mode, segmenting the recording every N seconds and printing each transcription as it is created. You can use faster-whisper, openai-whisper or whisper.cpp, and it auto-selects whichever is installed.

use_cases.title: Record then transcribe
use_cases.detail: On-demand mode records until you stop and transcribes once.

use_cases.title: Stream as you go
use_cases.detail: Live mode segments and prints each transcription as it is created.

use_cases.title: Pick your engine
use_cases.detail: faster-whisper, openai-whisper and whisper.cpp are all supported.

pros: Everything runs locally through Whisper
Three engines supported, auto-selected by what is installed
Both batch and streaming modes
cons: Command line only, with PulseAudio or PipeWire monitor sources on Linux
You must install an engine yourself

name: CanvoWP
description: CanvoWP is a free WordPress plugin where you describe your website in plain English and the agent builds it: it designs the pages, writes real WordPress templates and content, and checks its own work at desktop and mobile widths. Every feature is unlocked with no paid tier and no licence key, and the files stay in your own uploads folder while your existing plugins keep working.
description_en: CanvoWP is a free WordPress plugin where you describe your website in plain English and the agent builds it: it designs the pages, writes real WordPress templates and content, and checks its own work at desktop and mobile widths. Every feature is unlocked with no paid tier and no licence key, and the files stay in your own uploads folder while your existing plugins keep working.

use_cases.title: Describe the site
use_cases.detail: Tell the agent what you need in the chat and attach images.

use_cases.title: Watch it build
use_cases.detail: The agent writes pages, styles and templates, then reviews each page with screenshots.

use_cases.title: Publish when ready
use_cases.detail: Nothing reaches your visitors before you publish.

Output is plain HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PHP in your uploads folder
Existing SEO, forms, shop and search plugins carry on working

Needs WordPress 6.2+ and PHP 7.4+

name: Capsem
description: Capsem is a Rust hypervisor that sandboxes AI agents in air-gapped Linux VMs on your Mac, so you can ship fast with AI securely. It installs by download or a shell command, and works with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor through a setup prompt that walks your agent through creating an isolated environment.
description_en: Capsem is a Rust hypervisor that sandboxes AI agents in air-gapped Linux VMs on your Mac, so you can ship fast with AI securely. It installs by download or a shell command, and works with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor through a setup prompt that walks your agent through creating an isolated environment.

use_cases.title: Isolate an agent
use_cases.detail: Agents run inside air-gapped Linux VMs rather than on your desktop.

use_cases.title: Set it up with your agent
use_cases.detail: Copy the setup prompt into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.

use_cases.title: Reopen an environment
use_cases.detail: Existing environments and security settings stay intact between runs.

pros: Air-gapped Linux VMs keep agent work off your main system
Installs for macOS Apple silicon, Linux x86_64 and Linux ARM64
Setup prompt lets your own agent do the install
cons: Pricing is not published on the site
Virtual machines add setup and resource overhead

name: Checkobot
description: Checkobot is an AI image detector: you show Checko a photo and it looks for AI generation, AI edits and face swaps, then tells you what it found and why. Two detectors take a look, one studying the whole image. You get three free checks a day with no sign-up, and on free checks images are checked in memory and never stored.
description_en: Checkobot is an AI image detector: you show Checko a photo and it looks for AI generation, AI edits and face swaps, then tells you what it found and why. Two detectors take a look, one studying the whole image. You get three free checks a day with no sign-up, and on free checks images are checked in memory and never stored.
best_for: Verifying photos before you trust them

use_cases.title: Drop in an image
use_cases.detail: Upload or link a JPEG, PNG, WebP and more, up to 20 MB.

use_cases.title: Get a reason
use_cases.detail: Two detectors report what they found and why.

use_cases.title: Try it without signing up
use_cases.detail: Three free checks a day, checked in memory and never stored.

pros: Three free checks a day with no sign-up
Free checks are done in memory and never stored
Looks for AI edits and face swaps, not just generation
cons: Free usage is capped at three checks a day
No detector is right every time

name: Stof
description: Stof runs AI-generated logic safely inside your app: it is JSON with functions, so one document holds both the data and the logic that works on it, and your app runs it in a sandbox, in-process, in Rust, JavaScript or Python. Any JSON document is already valid Stof, you add types and functions where you need them, and you can export back to JSON, YAML or TOML at any time.
description_en: Stof runs AI-generated logic safely inside your app: it is JSON with functions, so one document holds both the data and the logic that works on it, and your app runs it in a sandbox, in-process, in Rust, JavaScript or Python. Any JSON document is already valid Stof, you add types and functions where you need them, and you can export back to JSON, YAML or TOML at any time.

use_cases.title: Let a model write logic
use_cases.detail: Generated logic runs sandboxed and in-process instead of as shell commands.

use_cases.title: Start from plain JSON
use_cases.detail: Every JSON document is already valid Stof, so adoption is gradual.

use_cases.title: Embed it anywhere
use_cases.detail: Rust, JavaScript and Python packages are all published.

pros: Sandboxed, in-process execution in three languages
Valid JSON is already valid Stof
Exports back to JSON, YAML or TOML
cons: A new language to learn for you and your tooling
Version 0.10 is still early

name: Tov
description: Tov is a programming language for coding agents: TypeScript's syntax that compiles to native binaries. It drops a few things, with no any, no null and no ==, separate int and f64 types, and any call that can fail marked try. After every edit you run tov check --json and apply each fix marked safe, then run and ship as a single binary.
description_en: Tov is a programming language for coding agents: TypeScript's syntax that compiles to native binaries. It drops a few things, with no any, no null and no ==, separate int and f64 types, and any call that can fail marked try. After every edit you run tov check --json and apply each fix marked safe, then run and ship as a single binary.

use_cases.title: Let your agent write it
use_cases.detail: An agent that writes TypeScript can already write Tov.

use_cases.title: Fix from the compiler
use_cases.detail: tov check --json returns edits, and the safe ones apply directly.

use_cases.title: Ship one binary
use_cases.detail: tov build produces a single native binary.

pros: Familiar TypeScript syntax for agents and people
Compiler hands back the edit that fixes the problem
Ships a single native binary
cons: Version 0.0.1 and explicitly experimental
A brand-new toolchain with no ecosystem yet

name: Droidtty
description: Droidtty puts your coding agents on your phone so you can leave the desk and keep them running. It shows what your agents are doing, notifies you only when something needs you, and lets you open a terminal only when you have to. It ships as a native Android APK powered by Ghostty.
description_en: Droidtty puts your coding agents on your phone so you can leave the desk and keep them running. It shows what your agents are doing, notifies you only when something needs you, and lets you open a terminal only when you have to. It ships as a native Android APK powered by Ghostty.

use_cases.title: See what matters now
use_cases.detail: Only the runs that need you raise a notification.

use_cases.title: Answer from the phone
use_cases.detail: Approve a command or answer a question without returning to the desk.

use_cases.title: Drop to a terminal
use_cases.detail: Open a real terminal only when the situation needs it.

pros: Notifications are filtered to what actually needs a human
Native Android build powered by Ghostty
Groups agents by space so several runs stay legible
cons: Android only
Pricing is not shown on the site

name: Muster
description: Muster is a free Mac menu bar app for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that lets you answer from the menu bar. Option-Tab brings your sessions together and Option-Return answers a supported request, and the alert unfolds to show the agent's reason for asking, the whole command, the file and size of an edit, or every option of a question. It lists every session from the last three hours with its tokens and what they would cost at API list prices.
description_en: Muster is a free Mac menu bar app for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that lets you answer from the menu bar. Option-Tab brings your sessions together and Option-Return answers a supported request, and the alert unfolds to show the agent's reason for asking, the whole command, the file and size of an edit, or every option of a question. It lists every session from the last three hours with its tokens and what they would cost at API list prices.
best_for: Answering agents from the menu bar
Tracking Claude Code and Codex sessions

use_cases.title: Answer without switching
use_cases.detail: Option-Return answers a supported request straight from the menu bar.

use_cases.title: Find the right session
use_cases.detail: Hold Option and tap Tab to see every session, the waiting one first.

use_cases.title: Watch the cost
use_cases.detail: Each session shows its tokens and what they would cost at list prices.

pros: Free, notarized and open source
Shows the command, file and size behind each request before you answer
Session list with token and cost context
cons: macOS 14 or later only
Direct answers only work with supported Claude Code and Codex requests

name: Sugabots
description: Sugabots is a place where people and agents work together: multiplayer agents on any model. A pod is a shared space for a group of people and their agents, where everyone sees the same chats, results and approvals, and agents ask before acting. It is open source.
description_en: Sugabots is a place where people and agents work together: multiplayer agents on any model. A pod is a shared space for a group of people and their agents, where everyone sees the same chats, results and approvals, and agents ask before acting. It is open source.

use_cases.title: Open a pod
use_cases.detail: A pod is a shared space for the people you get things done with.

use_cases.title: Let agents collaborate
use_cases.detail: Agents can work with each other, such as checking a trip against a budget.

use_cases.title: Approve before it acts
use_cases.detail: Actions like booking come back to the group to allow or deny.

pros: Shared context: everyone in the pod sees the same chats and results
Open source and model-agnostic
Agents ask for approval before acting
cons: Requires the whole group to adopt it
Agents in a shared space need careful permissions

name: Airlock
description: Airlock runs Claude Code or Codex in a virtual machine on your Mac so coding agents stay contained. It works on a copy of your project, so your real folder is never shared with the agent and it cannot reach anything else on your Mac. When it is done you get every changed file as a diff and choose which to apply, with build scripts, git hooks, CI config and the agent's own settings flagged.
description_en: Airlock runs Claude Code or Codex in a virtual machine on your Mac so coding agents stay contained. It works on a copy of your project, so your real folder is never shared with the agent and it cannot reach anything else on your Mac. When it is done you get every changed file as a diff and choose which to apply, with build scripts, git hooks, CI config and the agent's own settings flagged.

use_cases.title: Stop reading the fortieth prompt
use_cases.detail: Airlock turns approval prompts off and moves the agent into a VM instead.

use_cases.title: Keep your real folder
use_cases.detail: The agent works on a copy and cannot reach the rest of your Mac.

use_cases.title: Choose what lands
use_cases.detail: Every change comes back as a diff you tick, apply or undo.

pros: The agent only ever sees a copy of your project
Risky files like git hooks and CI config are flagged
Changes are applied as reviewable diffs
cons: Requires Apple silicon on macOS 26 or later
Pricing is not published on the page

name: Seodata
description: seodata.dev gives AI agents keyword data: search volume, CPC and competition for any keyword in 50+ countries, plus similar keywords. A free account gets 50 lookups a day and 500 a month, and without an account you get 20 anonymous lookups a day; the Unlimited plan is $4.99 per month.
description_en: seodata.dev gives AI agents keyword data: search volume, CPC and competition for any keyword in 50+ countries, plus similar keywords. A free account gets 50 lookups a day and 500 a month, and without an account you get 20 anonymous lookups a day; the Unlimited plan is $4.99 per month.

use_cases.title: Look up a keyword
use_cases.detail: Volume, CPC, competition and similar keywords come back together.

use_cases.title: Cover many markets
use_cases.detail: Data is available for 50+ countries.

use_cases.title: Call it from an agent
use_cases.detail: The same API key works on both plans, only the limits change.

pros: 20 free lookups a day with no account at all
Unlimited plan is $4.99 per month and cancels anytime
Agent documentation is provided
cons: Free tier is capped at 50 lookups a day with an account
Data quality depends on the upstream source

name: Phonebox
description: Phonebox gives AI agents cloud Android devices billed by the second. One API call starts an Android phone in the cloud and the CLI and SDK wait until it is ready. Your agent reads the screen as a short numbered list of what is on it, then taps by label, types, swipes and opens apps, and can also install apps, move files and change the location or language. Unused phones park themselves and cost nothing.
description_en: Phonebox gives AI agents cloud Android devices billed by the second. One API call starts an Android phone in the cloud and the CLI and SDK wait until it is ready. Your agent reads the screen as a short numbered list of what is on it, then taps by label, types, swipes and opens apps, and can also install apps, move files and change the location or language. Unused phones park themselves and cost nothing.

use_cases.title: Start a phone
use_cases.detail: One API call boots an Android device and the SDK waits for readiness.

use_cases.title: Control it by label
use_cases.detail: The agent reads a numbered list of screen elements and taps by label.

use_cases.title: Park it when idle
use_cases.detail: A parked phone costs nothing and keeps its apps and signed-in accounts.

pros: Billed by the second, and parked phones cost nothing
Screen is presented as a compact numbered list for the model
Apps and signed-in accounts persist between sessions
cons: No phone number, SMS inbox or calling: it is the device only
Costs scale with how long agents hold devices

name: Nagare
description: Nagare is a to-do app for iPhone, Mac and your agent, built around the idea that calendar events and tasks are both commitments. Both are represented by a single kind of item with an optional time, so you can put studying before the dentist appointment in one ordered list rather than keeping two separate views.
description_en: Nagare is a to-do app for iPhone, Mac and your agent, built around the idea that calendar events and tasks are both commitments. Both are represented by a single kind of item with an optional time, so you can put studying before the dentist appointment in one ordered list rather than keeping two separate views.

use_cases.title: Interleave the day
use_cases.detail: Events and tasks sit in one ordered list with optional times.

use_cases.title: Leave things untimed
use_cases.detail: An item without a time stays flexible around fixed commitments.

use_cases.title: Use it on iPhone and Mac
use_cases.detail: The app is built for both, and for your agent.

pros: One kind of item for both events and tasks
Untimed items keep the plan flexible
Designed with agents in mind
cons: Pricing and availability are not stated on the page
A single-app approach that replaces rather than syncs

name: Rinkata
description: Rinkata Hub is where your team and your AI agents share one source of truth: goals, specs, decisions and completion evidence. Structure keeps agents from inventing context, completed work is added to the knowledge base automatically, and you can upload designs and docs and extract ideas with one click. It works with Codex, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Grok and Gemini.
description_en: Rinkata Hub is where your team and your AI agents share one source of truth: goals, specs, decisions and completion evidence. Structure keeps agents from inventing context, completed work is added to the knowledge base automatically, and you can upload designs and docs and extract ideas with one click. It works with Codex, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Grok and Gemini.
best_for: Shared context for teams and agents

use_cases.title: Give the project a shared memory
use_cases.detail: Goals, specs, decisions and evidence live in one thread.

use_cases.title: Stop documenting by hand
use_cases.detail: Completed work is added to the knowledge base automatically.

use_cases.title: Bring in what you have
use_cases.detail: Upload Figma exports and documents and extract ideas from them.

pros: One intent thread from idea through goal, work, decision and evidence
Works with many agents and assistants
Completed work documents itself
cons: Freemium, so team features sit behind a plan
Requires the whole team to keep the hub current

name: ScreenCI
description: ScreenCI makes tutorial videos of your app from one prompt, recorded on your own machine. You describe a feature and paste the prompt into your coding agent, and it records a narrated walkthrough of your real app for your help center, docs, social media or the product itself. It works with any agent that runs shell commands and is free to try with no account.
description_en: ScreenCI makes tutorial videos of your app from one prompt, recorded on your own machine. You describe a feature and paste the prompt into your coding agent, and it records a narrated walkthrough of your real app for your help center, docs, social media or the product itself. It works with any agent that runs shell commands and is free to try with no account.

use_cases.title: Describe the video
use_cases.detail: Say what the video should show, optionally against a live site URL.

use_cases.title: Paste into your agent
use_cases.detail: Any coding agent that runs shell commands works.

use_cases.title: Publish it
use_cases.detail: The recording comes out ready for docs, social or in-product use.

pros: Free to try with no account needed
Works with any agent that can run shell commands
Records your real app on your own machine
cons: Recording quality depends on your app and machine
A fast, low-effort model is recommended, since the agent mostly runs commands

name: Wiyomi
description: Wiyomi is a developer agent for macOS and Windows with built-in strategies that save tokens. Smart routing and memory help it use fewer tokens on the same tasks while it codes, researches and writes, and it remembers useful context and preferences as you work. It publishes comparisons of input and output token savings against the same model.
description_en: Wiyomi is a developer agent for macOS and Windows with built-in strategies that save tokens. Smart routing and memory help it use fewer tokens on the same tasks while it codes, researches and writes, and it remembers useful context and preferences as you work. It publishes comparisons of input and output token savings against the same model.
best_for: Coding and research in one app

use_cases.title: Give it a task
use_cases.detail: Ask Wiyomi to code, research, write or solve.

use_cases.title: Save on every run
use_cases.detail: Built-in strategies and routing aim at fewer tokens per task.

use_cases.title: Build context over time
use_cases.detail: Memory keeps useful preferences between sessions.

pros: Token-saving strategies are built into the agent itself
Available for both macOS and Windows
Publishes its own savings comparisons
cons: Savings figures come from the vendor's own comparisons
Pricing is not shown on the site

name: The Last SaaS
description: The Last SaaS is a headless SaaS for agents and assistants: an experiment in reducing every SaaS app to records, files, access and background work, so Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant can build on those primitives through MCP, CLI or API. Records are validated when saved, files can be shared with temporary links, and an agent can be given its own service account, permissions and API token.
description_en: The Last SaaS is a headless SaaS for agents and assistants: an experiment in reducing every SaaS app to records, files, access and background work, so Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant can build on those primitives through MCP, CLI or API. Records are validated when saved, files can be shared with temporary links, and an agent can be given its own service account, permissions and API token.

use_cases.title: Model your data
use_cases.detail: Create collections with typed fields, references and recurring dates, validated on save.

use_cases.title: Store and share files
use_cases.detail: Upload from the CLI or a browser link and share temporary download links.

use_cases.title: Give an agent an identity
use_cases.detail: Service accounts carry their own permissions and API tokens.

pros: Open source with a free hosted version
Reachable through MCP, CLI and API at once
Agents get their own scoped service accounts
cons: Explicitly an experiment, so primitives may change
You assemble the application yourself

name: Token Barometer
description: Token Barometer tracks list prices for LLM APIs across thousands of models and hosted offerings, normalised to USD per 1M tokens, with full price history and a cloud-versus-local cost calculator. Data is refreshed daily from vendor pricing pages, official APIs and aggregators, and each row shows where the price was read from and a confidence value.
description_en: Token Barometer tracks list prices for LLM APIs across thousands of models and hosted offerings, normalised to USD per 1M tokens, with full price history and a cloud-versus-local cost calculator. Data is refreshed daily from vendor pricing pages, official APIs and aggregators, and each row shows where the price was read from and a confidence value.

use_cases.title: Compare models
use_cases.detail: Prices are normalised to USD per 1M tokens so they line up.

use_cases.title: Check the history
use_cases.detail: Full price history is kept for each offering.

use_cases.title: Weigh local against hosted
use_cases.detail: A calculator compares cloud prices with running locally.

pros: Prices are normalised and show their source and confidence
Refreshed daily from vendor pages, APIs and aggregators
Includes a cloud-versus-local calculator
cons: List prices only, not your negotiated or cached rates
Confidence varies by source

name: Bees
description: Bees is an open-source autonomous multi-agent platform that runs on your own computer. It coordinates agentic teams with loop engineering, independent reviewer loops and protected human gates, so files and execution stay private on your machines while organizational memory synchronizes centrally. Agents connect to tools and data sources through Model Context Protocol servers.
description_en: Bees is an open-source autonomous multi-agent platform that runs on your own computer. It coordinates agentic teams with loop engineering, independent reviewer loops and protected human gates, so files and execution stay private on your machines while organizational memory synchronizes centrally. Agents connect to tools and data sources through Model Context Protocol servers.
best_for: Multi-agent teams on your own hardware

use_cases.title: Run a team of agents
use_cases.detail: Bees coordinates teams with independent reviewer loops.

use_cases.title: Keep files private
use_cases.detail: Files and execution stay on your machines while memory syncs centrally.

use_cases.title: Connect your stack
use_cases.detail: Agents reach tools and data through MCP servers.

pros: Open source for macOS, Windows and Linux
Files and execution stay on your own machines
Protected human gates and independent reviewer loops
cons: Coordinating teams of agents is complex to tune
A multi-tenant cloud platform is offered alongside the local app

name: Hidden Content
description: HiddenContent.ai finds text your agent reads and you cannot see. Sign up with GitHub and the key starts with 20 free pages, after which pages are billed by the page, and the same key works from the browser extension or an API call, so your AI assistant can check documents before it reads them.
description_en: HiddenContent.ai finds text your agent reads and you cannot see. Sign up with GitHub and the key starts with 20 free pages, after which pages are billed by the page, and the same key works from the browser extension or an API call, so your AI assistant can check documents before it reads them.
best_for: Checking documents before an agent reads them

use_cases.title: Get a key in one step
use_cases.detail: Sign up with GitHub and the key is your production key right away.

use_cases.title: Check from the assistant
use_cases.detail: The extension lets your assistant check documents before reading them.

use_cases.title: Check from your code
use_cases.detail: The API does the same thing from inside your own software.

pros: The key you get on sign-up is already a production key
One key covers both the extension and the API
Starts with 20 free pages
cons: Usage is billed per page after the free allowance
Requires giving the service access to the documents you check

name: Project Arena
description: Project Arena is a vendor-neutral Kubernetes incident benchmark for testing AI investigation tools. It deploys a disposable cluster, injects faults across 21 scenarios, saves investigation records from any product, and scores them with a configurable AI judge.
description_en: Project Arena is a vendor-neutral Kubernetes incident benchmark for testing AI investigation tools. It deploys a disposable cluster, injects faults across 21 scenarios, saves investigation records from any product, and scores them with a configurable AI judge.
best_for: Benchmarking AI SRE and investigation tools

use_cases.title: Score tools on the same faults
use_cases.detail: The benchmark injects faults into a disposable Kubernetes fixture and saves each product’s investigation record for scoring.

use_cases.title: Bring your own product
use_cases.detail: Investigation records from any tool can be captured and scored, so the comparison is not limited to one vendor.

use_cases.title: Run a small suite first
use_cases.detail: A six-scenario smoke fixture runs alongside the full 21-scenario suite when you want a quicker pass.

pros: MIT licensed and vendor-neutral by design
A configurable judge rather than a fixed rubric
Runs on a local kind cluster or AWS EKS
cons: Needs Docker plus kind or an EKS cluster
Python 3.10+ and kubectl required

name: Shotstash
description: Shotstash is a self-hosted media cloud for creators and small teams. It stores project footage on your own PC, NAS or S3-compatible bucket, with resumable uploads, a portrait-aware viewer and share links per file, section or project.
description_en: Shotstash is a self-hosted media cloud for creators and small teams. It stores project footage on your own PC, NAS or S3-compatible bucket, with resumable uploads, a portrait-aware viewer and share links per file, section or project.
best_for: Delivering to clients without a subscription
Running a media library on hardware you own

use_cases.title: Keep footage on your own hardware
use_cases.detail: Storage can be a local disk, a NAS mount, or any S3-compatible bucket such as MinIO or Cloudflare R2.

use_cases.title: Uploads that survive bad Wi-Fi
use_cases.detail: Parallel parts with retries resume after a reload or a dropped connection, and every file is checksum-verified.

use_cases.title: Share a project, not a folder
use_cases.detail: Share links work per file, section or project, public or private.

pros: MIT licensed with no paid tier or locked features
Video-first viewer that respects real aspect ratios
Live demo with read-only accounts
cons: No mobile app in v1
Quick start is Linux x64 with Docker

name: AgentIntersect World
description: AgentIntersect World is a local-first 3D workspace for your repositories and your own AI coding agents. It renders a repository as a city you can walk, hosts up to four agents with their own identities, and turns conversation into workstreams with diffs and previews.
description_en: AgentIntersect World is a local-first 3D workspace for your repositories and your own AI coding agents. It renders a repository as a city you can walk, hosts up to four agents with their own identities, and turns conversation into workstreams with diffs and previews.
best_for: Running several coding agents side by side
Keeping agent work in one local workspace

use_cases.title: See your code as a place
use_cases.detail: Load a repository and navigate it as a code city instead of a file tree.

use_cases.title: Bring your own agents
use_cases.detail: Saved native connections to Claude Code, Codex, Hermes or OpenClaw, with up to four agents at once.

use_cases.title: Turn talk into work
use_cases.detail: Create a workstream, inspect source and diffs, read validation results and open an approved preview.

pros: Local-first and built for a single operator
Works with agent harnesses you already pay for
Windows and Linux builds
cons: Public preview at 0.15.0-rc.4 with rough edges
Windows builds are unsigned

name: Return Ledger
description: Return Ledger is a client-side portfolio tracker that logs contributions, withdrawals and valuation checkpoints, then computes time-weighted and money-weighted returns in the page. An AI feature reads a broker PDF and proposes the row, but nothing is added until you confirm.
description_en: Return Ledger is a client-side portfolio tracker that logs contributions, withdrawals and valuation checkpoints, then computes time-weighted and money-weighted returns in the page. An AI feature reads a broker PDF and proposes the row, but nothing is added until you confirm.
best_for: Tracking portfolio returns without an account
Keeping financial data in the browser

use_cases.title: Compute returns in the browser
use_cases.detail: TWR and XIRR are computed entirely in the page, with ledgers kept in this browser’s local storage.

use_cases.title: Import a statement with AI
use_cases.detail: Upload a buy/sell confirmation, coupon notice or position statement and a model proposes one row for review.

use_cases.title: Check before you commit
use_cases.detail: Every proposed row waits for confirmation, because the reader is alpha and tested mainly on Italian broker documents.

pros: No account, and ledgers stay in local storage
AI import adds nothing until you confirm each row
CSV import and export for moving data
cons: PDF reading is experimental and format-limited
Alpha proof of concept, and it states it is not financial advice

name: SafeBox
description: SafeBox is a local guardrail layer that sits between an AI coding agent and infrastructure tools such as Terraform and the AWS CLI. Deterministic TOML policy rules decide which commands pass, blocking destructive operations like terraform destroy before they reach the real executable.
description_en: SafeBox is a local guardrail layer that sits between an AI coding agent and infrastructure tools such as Terraform and the AWS CLI. Deterministic TOML policy rules decide which commands pass, blocking destructive operations like terraform destroy before they reach the real executable.
best_for: Guarding AI agents against destructive commands
Seeing what an agent tried to run

use_cases.title: Block destructive commands first
use_cases.detail: The default policy stops terraform destroy, kubectl delete, aws ec2 terminate-instances and similar operations.

use_cases.title: Decide with policy, not a model
use_cases.detail: Rules are explicit TOML files, so a verdict never depends on asking an AI whether a command looks safe.

use_cases.title: Proxy the real executable
use_cases.detail: SafeBox sits earlier in PATH than the real binary, so planning and read operations pass through untouched.

pros: Deterministic and fail-closed on unsupported shell syntax
MIT licensed with a packaged CLI entry point
Safe operations pass through unchanged
cons: Very early at 0.1.0
A policy file per tool to maintain

name: Pristine
description: Pristine is an agent skill that critiques, designs and polishes web UI. It captures the real page in light and dark mode, scores it out of 10 across 11 dimensions through the eyes of your personas, and can then apply the fixes it found.
description_en: Pristine is an agent skill that critiques, designs and polishes web UI. It captures the real page in light and dark mode, scores it out of 10 across 11 dimensions through the eyes of your personas, and can then apply the fixes it found.
best_for: Getting an honest UI critique from an agent
Defining a design system for a project

use_cases.title: Score a page honestly
use_cases.detail: The critique command rates a URL or screenshot out of 10 across 11 dimensions, with the exact fix for every finding.

use_cases.title: Fix what it found
use_cases.detail: The polish command keeps the look and raises every detail, with 16 named lenses such as bolder or typeset.

use_cases.title: Start from a design brief
use_cases.detail: The init command reads your code and writes DESIGN.md with product, personas, brand and design system.

pros: Works with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and any agent that reads SKILL.md
Eight published before/after pairs with full critiques
Apache-2.0 licensed
cons: Needs a browser tool such as Playwright MCP to capture pages
Scores are the agent’s judgement, not user research

name: Agent Archive
description: Agent Archive saves your Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions to your own S3 or Cloudflare R2 bucket. It hands a session’s context to another agent or machine, browses history by topic, project or branch, and tracks tokens and estimated spend.
description_en: Agent Archive saves your Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions to your own S3 or Cloudflare R2 bucket. It hands a session’s context to another agent or machine, browses history by topic, project or branch, and tracks tokens and estimated spend.
best_for: Continuing a session in a different agent

use_cases.title: Continue a session elsewhere
use_cases.detail: The handoff command picks a session and carries its conversation context into another coding agent or computer.

use_cases.title: Archive automatically
use_cases.detail: Transcripts from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor upload to your own S3 or R2 bucket.

use_cases.title: See usage and spend
use_cases.detail: The stats command breaks down session counts, tokens and estimated cost by agent, model and project.

pros: MIT licensed with release binaries for macOS and Linux
Storage stays in your own bucket
Filters by topic, project, branch or PR number
cons: Needs your own S3 or R2 bucket for automatic archiving
A CLI that lives beside your agent rather than inside it

name: Jarvis
description: Jarvis is an experimental Android voice assistant that drives other apps for you. Say the wake word and it opens apps, searches, plays music, sets reminders and can remote-control a Windows PC, with the brain running inside the app rather than on a server.
description_en: Jarvis is an experimental Android voice assistant that drives other apps for you. Say the wake word and it opens apps, searches, plays music, sets reminders and can remote-control a Windows PC, with the brain running inside the app rather than on a server.
best_for: Controlling an Android phone by voice

use_cases.title: Drive apps by voice
use_cases.detail: One command opens Spotify, searches and plays the song, using the Android accessibility service.

use_cases.title: Bring your own model keys
use_cases.detail: Vertex AI, Gemini or Groq, plus optional free OpenRouter, NVIDIA or Mistral keys, with smart routing between them.

use_cases.title: Reach the PC too
use_cases.detail: The same assistant can remote-control a Windows desktop.

pros: No server or Python needed on the phone
MIT licensed and under active development
Auto mode routes to the weakest model that can handle a request
cons: Experimental and tested on one phone
Read the security docs before giving it control of your phone

name: SelfBench
description: SelfBench builds private coding-agent benchmarks from your own repository’s merged pull requests. Each PR becomes a task with hidden tests, agents and models run against them, and accuracy is plotted against cost with the Pareto frontier drawn in.
description_en: SelfBench builds private coding-agent benchmarks from your own repository’s merged pull requests. Each PR becomes a task with hidden tests, agents and models run against them, and accuracy is plotted against cost with the Pareto frontier drawn in.
best_for: Finding the best model for your codebase
Comparing agents by accuracy and cost

use_cases.title: Turn PRs into tasks
use_cases.detail: For each merged PR the task is rebuilt from the commit before the change, with hidden tests and a reference solution.

use_cases.title: Accept only tasks that hold up
use_cases.detail: A task is accepted only if the tests fail without a solution, pass with the original, pass on rerun and survive an independent review.

use_cases.title: Read the leaderboard
use_cases.detail: Public repositories get a live leaderboard on selfbench.dev ranking models, harnesses and reasoning settings.

pros: MIT licensed with public leaderboards for open-source repos
Tasks are native Harbor format
Every accepted task passes four verification gates
cons: Batch generation takes hours
Everything happens in the hosted web app

name: LLM Usage Widget
description: LLM Usage Widget is a desktop widget that shows your Claude and Codex plan usage limits where your system tray icons live. It reuses the logins Claude Code and the Codex CLI already store, so there is nothing to configure.
description_en: LLM Usage Widget is a desktop widget that shows your Claude and Codex plan usage limits where your system tray icons live. It reuses the logins Claude Code and the Codex CLI already store, so there is nothing to configure.
best_for: Watching Claude and Codex usage limits
A tray widget instead of a browser tab

use_cases.title: See limits in the tray
use_cases.detail: The menu bar, top bar or taskbar shows Claude and Codex percentages, with a dropdown listing every limit and its reset countdown.

use_cases.title: Nothing to configure
use_cases.detail: It reuses the credentials Claude Code and the Codex CLI already store on your machine, read-only.

use_cases.title: Know when credits are what is left
use_cases.detail: Once a plan is at 100%, the widget switches to showing the remaining usage credits instead.

pros: MIT licensed across Linux, macOS and Windows
Credentials are only read and sent only to the issuing provider
Colour-coded bars marked stale when a refresh fails
cons: Claude and Codex only
A small project with three stars

name: VoxScribe
description: VoxScribe is free, open-source voice typing for Windows and Android. Hold a hotkey or tap the floating button, talk, and the text is typed into whatever app you are using, with transcription running locally on Whisper.
description_en: VoxScribe is free, open-source voice typing for Windows and Android. Hold a hotkey or tap the floating button, talk, and the text is typed into whatever app you are using, with transcription running locally on Whisper.
best_for: Private voice typing with no account

use_cases.title: Type by talking, anywhere
use_cases.detail: A system-wide hotkey types directly into the focused window rather than pasting from the clipboard.

use_cases.title: Caption a whole folder
use_cases.detail: Drop in episodes and VoxScribe writes an .srt beside each file, reporting what it saved, skipped and failed.

use_cases.title: Fix recurring mistakes
use_cases.detail: A vocabulary list covers names and jargon, and word replacements handle anything the model mishears the same way.

pros: MIT licensed with no account or subscription
100% local transcription with faster-whisper
Spoken commands for punctuation and corrections
cons: Windows and Android only
CPU-only transcription, so speed depends on your machine

name: Abyss
description: Abyss is an orchestrator that runs your AI coding agents inside containers. You configure your editor like a normal ACP agent and Abyss handles Docker, intercepting every filesystem and shell request so nothing executes on your real machine.
description_en: Abyss is an orchestrator that runs your AI coding agents inside containers. You configure your editor like a normal ACP agent and Abyss handles Docker, intercepting every filesystem and shell request so nothing executes on your real machine.
best_for: Running agents without touching the host

use_cases.title: Keep the agent in a container
use_cases.detail: Every filesystem and shell request is intercepted and executed inside the container, never on the host.

use_cases.title: Keep secrets in the dark
use_cases.detail: Nothing is visible to the agent by default until you explicitly mount or copy it in.

use_cases.title: Use any ACP client
use_cases.detail: Abyss speaks ACP, so your existing editor or client can drive the isolated agent.

pros: MIT licensed control plane rather than a general container tool bent into one
Native ACP support with middleware plugins
Startup scripts and provisioning built in
cons: Needs Docker on the host
An early project with four stars

name: agentc
description: agentc is a minimal coding agent written in freestanding C23 with no libc. It ships as a static binary under 1 MB, starts in under a millisecond, speaks MCP first, and exposes a versioned C ABI for C and Rust extensions.
description_en: agentc is a minimal coding agent written in freestanding C23 with no libc. It ships as a static binary under 1 MB, starts in under a millisecond, speaks MCP first, and exposes a versioned C ABI for C and Rust extensions.
best_for: Embedding an agent in a small footprint

use_cases.title: Run in under a megabyte
use_cases.detail: The stripped binary is about 940 KiB with roughly 0.7 MB of RSS at cold start and no runtime to install.

use_cases.title: Speak MCP first
use_cases.detail: Tools, prompts and resources come first, then a versioned C ABI in include/agentc_ext.h for extensions.

use_cases.title: Measure it yourself
use_cases.detail: A bench target reports cold-start time, peak RSS and binary size, and compares the same numbers against codex, Claude Code and pi.

pros: MIT licensed and builds for six targets from one tree
Observed rather than estimated footprint numbers
MCP first with a C ABI for extensions
cons: Freestanding C23, so expect to work without libc
A very new project with nine stars

name: Perch
description: Perch is a free beta Mac app that gives your Claude Code work one calm home. It keeps every session, PR and link in one place, stays quiet while you are in flow, and only speaks up when Claude, a reviewer or CI is waiting on you.
description_en: Perch is a free beta Mac app that gives your Claude Code work one calm home. It keeps every session, PR and link in one place, stays quiet while you are in flow, and only speaks up when Claude, a reviewer or CI is waiting on you.
best_for: Seeing which PR is waiting on you
A local-first workspace for agent work

use_cases.title: Bring your sessions with you
use_cases.detail: Pick existing Claude Code sessions and Perch resumes each one exactly where it left off.

use_cases.title: Hear only what needs you
use_cases.detail: Perch speaks up only when Claude, a reviewer or CI is waiting, and deep focus mutes everything else.

use_cases.title: Keep PRs in context
use_cases.detail: Linked PRs across repos and worktrees are detected automatically, with a one-line status Claude writes as it works.

pros: Free beta with contexts, notes and status in a local database
No account, no Perch servers and no analytics
Sessions keep running when Perch quits
cons: macOS on Apple Silicon only
Requires the Claude Code CLI, and GitHub features need your gh login

name: Kolo
description: Kolo is an open-source alpha that turns a local AI coding agent into a multiplayer session: run agents on one machine, share a link, and your team can watch, type or take over the same terminal from a browser.
description_en: Kolo is an open-source alpha that turns a local AI coding agent into a multiplayer session: run agents on one machine, share a link, and your team can watch, type or take over the same terminal from a browser.
best_for: Sharing a coding agent session with a team
Pairing on an agent run without screen sharing
Running Claude Code, Codex CLI or opencode for a group

use_cases.title: Join a session from a link
use_cases.detail: Teammates open the invitation link printed in the host terminal, choose a name and join. No install and no token to paste.

use_cases.title: Take over the same terminal
use_cases.detail: Everyone sees the same terminal, so you can type a prompt, approve a step, or pick up where a teammate left off.

use_cases.title: Keep observers read-only
use_cases.detail: The host decides who can control sessions while read-only members follow along.

pros: Built-in adapters for Claude Code, Codex CLI and opencode
Only the host installs Kolo; teammates just open a link
One Go binary runs both the hub and the host
AGPL-3.0 licensed
cons: Experimental alpha meant for trusted teams
Agents run with the host user permissions, so the isolation setup matters
Hosts support Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64, WSL2 on Windows

name: ReviewerAgent
description: ReviewerAgent is an open-source commit gate for Claude Code and Codex: a separate review agent checks each plan and commit, and the commit cannot proceed until the issues it lists are fixed.
description_en: ReviewerAgent is an open-source commit gate for Claude Code and Codex: a separate review agent checks each plan and commit, and the commit cannot proceed until the issues it lists are fixed.
best_for: Catching bugs an agent missed before it commits
Letting one model review another model work
Stopping an agent from quitting a task too early

use_cases.title: Gate every commit
use_cases.detail: A review agent you choose completes a plan or code review, and any issue it specifies must be fixed by the coding agent before the commit is allowed to proceed.

use_cases.title: Use any model as the reviewer
use_cases.detail: Codex, Pi with any model, or Claude Code itself can act as the reviewer and stop-continue agent, each in its own session.

use_cases.title: Decide when the agent may stop
use_cases.detail: Stop Continue examines the project plan, the task list and any background tasks the agent is waiting on, then either allows the stop or tells the agent what to do next.

pros: Author reports 3,877 gated commits across four months of daily use
Rejection rate scales with commit size: 23% under 50 lines, 72% over 1,000
Reviewer and stop-continue are separately controllable features
cons: Adds a review round trip to every commit
Those numbers come from the author own single-project log
MPL-2.0 licensed but a very small project

name: Token Beggar
description: Token Beggar is an open-source Claude Code plugin that checks whether a cheaper model can do a job just as well before the big model takes it, sending large tasks to one cheaper worker while design decisions stay with the model you picked.
description_en: Token Beggar is an open-source Claude Code plugin that checks whether a cheaper model can do a job just as well before the big model takes it, sending large tasks to one cheaper worker while design decisions stay with the model you picked.
best_for: Cutting Claude Code quota and API spend
Routing bug fixes in unfamiliar repos to cheaper models
Keeping the final answer with the model you chose

use_cases.title: Route each task by size
use_cases.detail: Small tasks stay in the chat. A large task, such as fixing a bug in a repository you have not read yet, goes to one cheaper worker.

use_cases.title: Verify the worker diff
use_cases.detail: The chat then checks the whole diff and runs the tests, while design, root causes and the final answer stay with the model you picked.

use_cases.title: Diagnose silent failures
use_cases.detail: token-beggar doctor lists what can quietly stop routing and exits 1 when something is broken.

pros: Author reports 1.42x less quota and money across 18 real bug fixes
Same share of hidden tests passing, 69% against 70% working alone
Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only, zero dependencies
Runs locally inside your own Claude Code session
cons: Needs Claude Code and Python 3.10 or newer
The benchmark is 18 fixes measured by the author
MIT licensed but a brand new project

name: Zilla
description: Zilla is a source-available multi-protocol gateway whose MCP Gateway gives AI agents one governed endpoint for MCP servers, HTTP APIs, OpenAPI services and Kafka, all configured in a single zilla.yaml.
description_en: Zilla is a source-available multi-protocol gateway whose MCP Gateway gives AI agents one governed endpoint for MCP servers, HTTP APIs, OpenAPI services and Kafka, all configured in a single zilla.yaml.
best_for: Giving agents one governed MCP endpoint
Exposing Kafka operations to agents over MCP
Federating several MCP servers behind one catalog

use_cases.title: Federate providers behind one endpoint
use_cases.detail: Existing MCP servers, HTTP APIs, OpenAPI-described services and Apache Kafka all connect to a single agent-facing MCP endpoint.

use_cases.title: Namespace capabilities per provider
use_cases.detail: Capabilities are namespaced as toolkit__capability, so github__create_pr, payments__refund and kafka__produce_message route without collisions.

use_cases.title: Govern identity, guardrails and telemetry
use_cases.detail: The gateway validates the agent identity, filters capability listings by authorization, applies schema guardrails and exports MCP metrics and lifecycle events.

pros: Event Gateway and MCP Gateway share one routing and security model
Large catalogs split into eager and cold tools so agents load only what they need
Docker and Helm installs with metrics on port 7190
Over 1,600 GitHub stars and an active release cadence
cons: Aklivity Community License, not OSI open source
Offering Zilla as a standalone commercial service is not permitted
Advanced OAuth grants and distributed stores need the paid Plus edition
Java stack, so Docker Compose or Helm is the normal way to run it

name: AiSniff
description: AiSniff is an open-source linter that underlines phrases in English and Chinese text matching documented AI-writing patterns, naming the rule, citing a public source and suggesting a plain rewrite, with no server and no model call.
description_en: AiSniff is an open-source linter that underlines phrases in English and Chinese text matching documented AI-writing patterns, naming the rule, citing a public source and suggesting a plain rewrite, with no server and no model call.
best_for: Editing AI-sounding phrasing out of a draft
Checking copy before you publish it
Running the same rules from a CLI or an agent skill

use_cases.title: See the rule behind every hit
use_cases.detail: Each mark names its rule, cites a public source and suggests a plain rewrite, all driven by one set of JSON rules.

use_cases.title: Run it wherever you write
use_cases.detail: The web editor, the CLI (npx github:Arthur031221/AiSniff lint draft.md) and the agent skill all read the same rule set.

use_cases.title: Read the honest evaluation
use_cases.detail: On held-out HC3 answers the English rules marked at least one phrase in 29% of chatbot answers and 2% of human ones, and the docs publish per-rule counts.

pros: No server and no model call, so it runs entirely locally
Covers English and Chinese text
Publishes its own limits, including an AUROC of 0.63 for English hit density
MIT licensed with a live demo
cons: Density alone is a weak detector, 0.59 AUROC for Chinese
71% of held-out English chatbot answers had no hit at all
It reports patterns, not authorship
A very new project

name: Boba
description: Boba is a free AI assistant you text or open on the web, built for group chats as much as for one-on-one use: it researches trips, splits costs, keeps family lists and books things once you say yes.
description_en: Boba is a free AI assistant you text or open on the web, built for group chats as much as for one-on-one use: it researches trips, splits costs, keeps family lists and books things once you say yes.
best_for: Coordinating plans inside a group chat
Trip research and splitting the cost

use_cases.title: Work inside the group chat
use_cases.detail: Drop Boba in the trip chat and it researches cabins, flights and trains, splits the cost and lays out options everyone can weigh in on.

use_cases.title: Keep the shared memory
use_cases.detail: Grocery lists, school pickups and appointments stay in the family chat, with reminders going to the right person at the right time.

use_cases.title: Let it handle email and calendar
use_cases.detail: Connect Gmail or Outlook and Boba flags what matters, drafts replies, puts plans on your calendar and books the table once you say yes.

pros: Free with no app to download and no sign-up
Works over text and on the web, one-on-one or in a group
Books restaurants and appointments once you confirm
cons: Messages you send may be used to improve Boba
The site itself notes the assistant can get things wrong
Texting it means handing over a phone number

name: Otaku AI
description: Otaku AI is a free, fan-built browser assistant for anime fans: it answers questions about currently airing shows, recommends series by mood and lets you talk to or roleplay as characters from a series you love.
description_en: Otaku AI is a free, fan-built browser assistant for anime fans: it answers questions about currently airing shows, recommends series by mood and lets you talk to or roleplay as characters from a series you love.
best_for: Chatting or roleplaying as a character
Checking what is airing right now

use_cases.title: Turn a mood into a shortlist
use_cases.detail: Ask about currently airing shows or pick a mood such as sad, hype, chill or dark, and get recommendations filtered by your own taste.

use_cases.title: Talk to a character
use_cases.detail: Character RP lets you converse with or roleplay as characters from a series as if they were really there, all through plain conversation.

use_cases.title: Use the anime tools
use_cases.detail: Anime search, a character creator, a quiz, power-scaling deep dives and a philosophy chat sit beside the recommendation tools.

pros: Free in the browser with nothing to install
Conversations stay lightweight and are not shared with anyone else
Share a chat as text or as a downloadable card image
cons: An independent fan project, not affiliated with any studio
Login is required to save chat history
Single-topic scope, useful only to anime fans

name: FrameCap
description: FrameCap is a free Chrome extension that lets AI watch a YouTube video: one click captures a timestamped transcript plus sharp frames of the screen and sends both to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity.
description_en: FrameCap is a free Chrome extension that lets AI watch a YouTube video: one click captures a timestamped transcript plus sharp frames of the screen and sends both to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity.
best_for: Asking an AI about a video tutorial
Getting the exact formula or code line from a screencast
Feeding frames to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor

use_cases.title: Capture words and visuals together
use_cases.detail: FrameCap reads the captions as a timestamped transcript and snaps a sharp frame every 1 to 15 seconds, right inside your browser.

use_cases.title: Send it straight to your AI
use_cases.detail: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity opens with a PDF of the frames and a ready prompt, and a ZIP download works for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

use_cases.title: Keep it private
use_cases.detail: Everything runs inside your browser with no account and no API key, on Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc.

pros: Free extension with no account and no API key
Frames up to 4K, sharp enough to read code on screen
One click to paste into every major AI assistant
cons: YouTube only
Frame interval is fixed when you capture, between 1 and 15 seconds
The transcript comes from the video captions, so uncaptioned videos give you frames only

name: Four-Leaf
description: Four-Leaf is an AI job search assistant with over 100,000 live openings scraped from company career pages, ghost-job checks, voice mock interviews and an MCP server that puts it inside Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT.
description_en: Four-Leaf is an AI job search assistant with over 100,000 live openings scraped from company career pages, ghost-job checks, voice mock interviews and an MCP server that puts it inside Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT.
best_for: Searching real openings without ghost jobs
Tailoring a resume to one job description

use_cases.title: Search live openings
use_cases.detail: Openings are scraped directly from company career pages with ghost-job checks built in, and search is free with no account needed.

use_cases.title: Turn a listing into an offer
use_cases.detail: Save a search for weekly matches, then run voice mock interviews, build a resume and cover letters, and prepare negotiation with a coach.

use_cases.title: Bring it into your AI
use_cases.detail: An MCP server puts Four-Leaf inside Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT, alongside hiring data, job trends and interview guides.

pros: Over 100,000 live openings with ghost-job checks
Free search with no account needed
Interview guides and question banks organised by role
cons: The seven AI assistants sit behind a paid trial; only search and the standalone tools are free
Coverage limited to employers whose career pages it can scrape
A web product, so nothing works offline

name: Radian
description: Radian is a coding agent shipped as one Rust binary. It starts with no runtime to boot and spends context on the lines a task needs, and its headless command prints every step as a JSON line and exits with a code that says how it ended.
description_en: Radian is a coding agent shipped as one Rust binary. It starts with no runtime to boot and spends context on the lines a task needs, and its headless command prints every step as a JSON line and exits with a code that says how it ended.
best_for: Running a coding agent inside a pipeline
Keeping context spend on the lines a task needs
Driving an agent headlessly from a script

use_cases.title: Run it headlessly
use_cases.detail: The headless command prints every step as a JSON line and exits with a code that says how it ended, so a task can be driven from a script or a CI job.

use_cases.title: Install one binary
use_cases.detail: Radian is one Rust binary with no runtime to boot, installed with brew install hisea/tap/radian.

use_cases.title: Work in the terminal
use_cases.detail: The terminal session shows the agent thinking, running shell commands, reading files and patching code, with timings and exit codes for each step.

pros: One Rust binary with no runtime to boot
Headless mode prints JSON lines with a meaningful exit code
Open source under MIT or Apache-2.0
cons: Source install and a Rust-centric workflow rather than a hosted product
Parts of the site and documentation are Chinese-language

name: SeekStorm
description: SeekStorm is sub-millisecond lexical, vector and hybrid search written in Rust. It embeds as an in-process library, runs as a multi-tenancy server, or gives your agents search over MCP.
description_en: SeekStorm is sub-millisecond lexical, vector and hybrid search written in Rust. It embeds as an in-process library, runs as a multi-tenancy server, or gives your agents search over MCP.
best_for: Adding hybrid search to a Rust service
Serving many tenants from one index
Giving agents a search tool over MCP

use_cases.title: Embed it
use_cases.detail: Use SeekStorm as an in-process library when you want search inside your own binary rather than a separate service.

use_cases.title: Run it as a server
use_cases.detail: Run the multi-tenancy server with its console and web UI, with a REST API documented on the project site.

use_cases.title: Wire it to agents
use_cases.detail: Expose search to AI agents through MCP so they can query indexes you own.

pros: Lexical, vector and hybrid search from one engine
Apache License 2.0, in production since 2020
Live demo and benchmarks published by the project
cons: Rust-only as a library, so other stacks go through the server or REST API
Self-managed: you run and tune the deployment yourself

name: MeetCap
description: MeetCap records any meeting you want, free, for as long as you like. It transcribes recordings on your computer and never uploads them, produces live summaries and minutes, and lets your AI agent record, search past meetings or use them as context.
description_en: MeetCap records any meeting you want, free, for as long as you like. It transcribes recordings on your computer and never uploads them, produces live summaries and minutes, and lets your AI agent record, search past meetings or use them as context.
best_for: Recording meetings without sending audio anywhere
Getting minutes ready when a call ends
Letting an agent search past meetings

use_cases.title: Record without a time limit
use_cases.detail: Record any meeting free and for as long as you like, with the recording staying on your Mac.

use_cases.title: Catch up mid-call
use_cases.detail: Live summaries catch you up and explain the terms when your mind drifts or the topic is new.

use_cases.title: Hand meetings to your agent
use_cases.detail: Your AI agent can record, search past meetings or use them as context.

pros: Transcribes on your computer and never uploads recordings
Minutes with an executive summary, recap timestamps, speakers, to-dos and transcript
Free downloads for Apple silicon and Intel Macs
cons: macOS 14.2 or later only; Windows and iPhone versions are still coming
Not open source, so transcription runs inside the app you install

name: Brod
description: Brod is the self-hosted cloud your AI agent deploys team tools to, over MCP. Your agent deploys to it directly and gets back an address that only the right people can open, with one sign-in for every app.
description_en: Brod is the self-hosted cloud your AI agent deploys team tools to, over MCP. Your agent deploys to it directly and gets back an address that only the right people can open, with one sign-in for every app.
best_for: Giving agent-built internal tools a home
Sharing one sign-in across small apps
Deploying from Claude Code or Cursor over MCP

use_cases.title: Deploy from your agent
use_cases.detail: Add Brod as an MCP server in Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor, then ask your agent to deploy an app; it answers with the app address.

use_cases.title: One sign-in for every app
use_cases.detail: People sign in with an emailed link or Google, and apps read who is signed in with their role and groups, keeping no user table of their own.

use_cases.title: Workspaces per team
use_cases.detail: One workspace per team or company, each with its own people, groups and apps.

pros: Starts with docker compose up and a one-time sign-in link from the log
AGPL-3.0-only and self-hosted on your own infrastructure
Agents deploy over MCP instead of a bespoke CLI
cons: Requires Docker with the Compose plugin and a host you run
Early project: OAuth sign-in and more clients are still in progress

name: Pasteface
description: Pasteface records, transcribes and copies speech from your terminal. It organises recordings into named transcript tabs, keeps recording while earlier chunks transcribe, and copies results to your clipboard, using whisper.cpp on your machine or the OpenAI transcription API.
description_en: Pasteface records, transcribes and copies speech from your terminal. It organises recordings into named transcript tabs, keeps recording while earlier chunks transcribe, and copies results to your clipboard, using whisper.cpp on your machine or the OpenAI transcription API.
best_for: Keeping several recordings in named tabs

use_cases.title: Record and queue
use_cases.detail: Space starts and stops recording, and stopping enqueues the chunk, so you can keep recording while earlier chunks transcribe.

use_cases.title: Copy a transcript
use_cases.detail: C copies the selected tab transcript and E exports it, so a dictation session goes straight to the clipboard.

use_cases.title: Choose the backend
use_cases.detail: Transcribe on your machine with whisper.cpp or use the OpenAI transcription API, depending on whether you want audio to leave the machine.

pros: Local whisper.cpp transcription as well as the OpenAI API
Named transcript tabs and queued recordings
Tray companion plus a terminal interface, with a tray-free build that drops the GTK dependencies
cons: Linux and macOS only; Windows is not currently supported
Source build with a Rust toolchain and FFmpeg, and macOS builds are ad-hoc signed rather than notarized

name: Ghx
description: Ghx is a caching proxy for the GitHub CLI built for AI agent workflows. Singleflight coalescing means several agents asking the same thing trigger one API call, and only allowlisted read-only commands are cached while mutations pass through.
description_en: Ghx is a caching proxy for the GitHub CLI built for AI agent workflows. Singleflight coalescing means several agents asking the same thing trigger one API call, and only allowlisted read-only commands are cached while mutations pass through.
best_for: Stopping agent fleets hitting GitHub rate limits
Caching repeated gh calls in scripts
Watching cache hit rates on a dashboard

use_cases.title: Drop it in
use_cases.detail: Use ghx instead of gh; the daemon auto-starts and needs no configuration.

use_cases.title: Collapse duplicate calls
use_cases.detail: Five agents requesting the same PR list simultaneously make only one API call, and all five get the result.

use_cases.title: Watch the cache
use_cases.detail: A real-time web dashboard shows hit rates, per-command stats and a live request log, and the same data is available as JSON.

pros: Context-aware cache keys prevent cross-repo collisions
Mutations pass through directly and invalidate related cache entries
No tokens stored; the daemon listens on a Unix socket with strict permissions
cons: Adds a daemon and a cache to reason about before trusting a stale answer
Only explicitly allowlisted read-only commands are cached

name: Fresh
description: Fresh is an agent skill that starts you clean after a merged PR. It syncs your default branch and removes branches and worktrees whose changes already landed, including squash merges, and shows you the cleanup plan first.
description_en: Fresh is an agent skill that starts you clean after a merged PR. It syncs your default branch and removes branches and worktrees whose changes already landed, including squash merges, and shows you the cleanup plan first.
best_for: Cleaning up branches after a squash merge
Removing stale worktrees left by agents
Running cleanup from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor

use_cases.title: Run it in your agent
use_cases.detail: Install the skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok or OpenCode, then ask the agent to use fresh once your PR merges.

use_cases.title: See the plan first
use_cases.detail: Fresh previews the cleanup before running it, stops on uncommitted changes, and keeps branches with unmerged work.

use_cases.title: Use it from the shell
use_cases.detail: The same cleanup runs as camp fresh in your terminal.

pros: Handles squash merges, which naive branch cleanup misses
Preview before run, with uncommitted changes halting the run
Works across several coding agents plus a CLI
cons: Requires macOS or Linux, Bash and Python 3, with WSL2 on Windows
Installs Festival on first use to provide the camp command

name: Mixdog
description: Mixdog is an open-source desktop coding agent where a lead model plans and cheaper models handle search, edits and review. It reports 63% fewer tokens than Codex CLI on the same model at the same success rate, with auto reasoning effort judged by a small model that runs locally on the CPU.
description_en: Mixdog is an open-source desktop coding agent where a lead model plans and cheaper models handle search, edits and review. It reports 63% fewer tokens than Codex CLI on the same model at the same success rate, with auto reasoning effort judged by a small model that runs locally on the CPU.
best_for: Cutting token spend on routine agent steps
Running a desktop coding agent on Windows, macOS or Linux
Keeping a lead model for planning only

use_cases.title: Split the work by cost
use_cases.detail: A lead model plans while cheaper models handle search, edits and review.

use_cases.title: Let it pick the effort
use_cases.detail: Auto reasoning effort gives each message and tool step the effort it needs, judged in about 0.1 s by a 150 MB model that runs locally on the CPU.

use_cases.title: Install a desktop build
use_cases.detail: Downloadable builds are published for Windows, macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, and Linux.

pros: Apache-2.0 licensed with published terminal-bench benchmarks
A desktop app rather than a terminal-only agent
Auto reasoning effort is on by default
cons: The token saving is the project own benchmark claim against Codex CLI
Early desktop release, so expect rough edges

name: Graft
description: Graft is source control for agent-scale monorepos, an open-source implementation of the design in Anthropic Redesigning source control post. History, blame, diffs and merges happen server-side, commits are changesets, landing is lock-free, and working copies are optional and sparse.
description_en: Graft is source control for agent-scale monorepos, an open-source implementation of the design in Anthropic Redesigning source control post. History, blame, diffs and merges happen server-side, commits are changesets, landing is lock-free, and working copies are optional and sparse.
best_for: Serving many agent or CI clients from one repo
Landing changes without a merge queue

use_cases.title: Do the work server-side
use_cases.detail: History, blame, diffs, merge bases, search, commits, rebases and merges all happen server-side, each as an HTTP API, so many jobs never need a local repository.

use_cases.title: Land without contention
use_cases.detail: gft land rebases server-side and moves the ref with a compare-and-swap on one row: no global lock, no merge queue.

use_cases.title: Mount what you need
use_cases.detail: gft mount gives a writable virtual checkout that fetches files on first read, commits only what you changed, and switches revisions instantly.

pros: Want-only tiered fetch with no packfiles and no negotiation
Repository and directory-level access control plus review gates
Prebuilt binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows, or go install
cons: An independent implementation, not Anthropic own tool
Requires running and operating a server rather than just a local clone

name: Kryzz AI
description: Kryzz AI is a private, local-first Android AI workspace with chat, voice and autonomous agents running on your own API keys. It ships as a Kotlin and Jetpack Compose app with no account, no subscription and no telemetry, so conversations stay on the phone.
description_en: Kryzz AI is a private, local-first Android AI workspace with chat, voice and autonomous agents running on your own API keys. It ships as a Kotlin and Jetpack Compose app with no account, no subscription and no telemetry, so conversations stay on the phone.
best_for: Running agents on Android with your own keys

use_cases.title: Bring your own key
use_cases.detail: Paste an OpenRouter key, test it in the onboarding screen and start talking; no bundled keys.

use_cases.title: Pick a workflow
use_cases.detail: The workflow picker offers Auto, Deep search, Wide search, Document, Spreadsheet, Database and Code.

use_cases.title: Talk instead of type
use_cases.detail: A voice session overlay shows the listening state while the agent works.

pros: MIT licensed, with no telemetry and no analytics
About a 19 MB APK, Android 9 and later
Chat, autonomous agents and voice in one app
cons: Android only; there is no desktop or iOS build
You supply and pay for the model API keys yourself

name: pg_vectorsearch
description: pg_vectorsearch is a PostgreSQL extension for high-performance approximate nearest neighbor search. It adds a PRISM index built for 100M+ vectors with hierarchical routing, RaBitQ quantization with theoretical error bounds, and SIMD-optimized distance computation, and it can index existing pgvector columns as-is.
description_en: pg_vectorsearch is a PostgreSQL extension for high-performance approximate nearest neighbor search. It adds a PRISM index built for 100M+ vectors with hierarchical routing, RaBitQ quantization with theoretical error bounds, and SIMD-optimized distance computation, and it can index existing pgvector columns as-is.
best_for: Keeping inserts, updates and deletes working

use_cases.title: Index at scale
use_cases.detail: The PRISM index is IVF-style with hierarchical routing and is built for 100M+ vectors.

use_cases.title: Reuse pgvector tables
use_cases.detail: Index existing vector and halfvec columns as-is instead of migrating data.
