use_cases.title: Keep the index fresh
use_cases.detail: Inserts, updates and deletes are supported, with posting-list splits through prism_rebalance.

pros: pgvector compatible, so existing tables can be indexed without a rewrite
RaBitQ quantization with theoretical error bounds for two-stage search
SIMD-optimized distance computation across AVX2, AVX512 and NEON
cons: Status alpha: meant for testing, not production, and prerelease upgrades may require dropping and recreating the extension
You run and maintain the extension and its indexes yourself

name: Bomfather
description: Bomfather is an open source runtime security agent you deploy on your Linux servers to protect the resources your workloads depend on, such as GPUs, databases and filesystems. It enforces policies with eBPF from inside the kernel.
description_en: Bomfather is an open source runtime security agent you deploy on your Linux servers to protect the resources your workloads depend on, such as GPUs, databases and filesystems. It enforces policies with eBPF from inside the kernel.
best_for: Protecting GPU, database and filesystem access at runtime
Writing one small policy file for a fleet

use_cases.title: Protect runtime resources
use_cases.detail: Deploy the agent on Linux servers to protect GPUs, databases, filesystems and more from the processes that touch them.

use_cases.title: Enforce at the kernel
use_cases.detail: Policies are enforced with eBPF, which the project reports adds 1% to 3% overhead against much higher overhead for confidential computing.

use_cases.title: Keep policy small
use_cases.detail: One small policy file can cover a whole infrastructure, with inheritance between policies.

pros: Runs in the kernel via eBPF rather than tamperable userspace
A background process that needs no changes to your infrastructure or programs
Open sourced agent alongside published runtime and GPU protection products
cons: Linux servers only
The surrounding products are commercial; only the agent is open source

name: Enki LLM
description: Enki LLM is a pure Rust Transformer inference engine of about 2,000 lines that runs Llama-3.2 1B at roughly 40 tokens per second on an Nvidia Tesla T4, with live brain migration between GPU VRAM and CPU RAM mid generation and no CUDA dependencies.
description_en: Enki LLM is a pure Rust Transformer inference engine of about 2,000 lines that runs Llama-3.2 1B at roughly 40 tokens per second on an Nvidia Tesla T4, with live brain migration between GPU VRAM and CPU RAM mid generation and no CUDA dependencies.
best_for: Running a small model in pure Rust
Migrating a running generation between GPU and CPU
Studying a small, readable inference engine

use_cases.title: Infer without CUDA
use_cases.detail: Unquantized F16 weights with FP32 accumulators run in pure Rust, with no CUDA or C++ wrapper.

use_cases.title: Migrate mid-sentence
use_cases.detail: Live brain migration hot-swaps active execution and mirrors the KV-cache between GPU VRAM and CPU RAM without losing context.

use_cases.title: Run one binary everywhere
use_cases.detail: The same binary runs on discrete Nvidia GPUs, integrated Intel graphics and multi-core CPUs without changing a line of code.

pros: Around 2,000 lines with the safetensors parser, tokenizer, RoPE, RMSNorm and sampling built from scratch
One-click Google Colab demo on a free T4 GPU
Host fallback executes the same kernels across CPU cores with Rayon
cons: Demonstrated on Llama-3.2 1B, so it is a small-model engine rather than a serving stack
Depends on the separate Enki runtime and Vulkan 1.3

name: Shadowclone
description: Shadowclone keeps your engineering preferences the same in every coding agent. It maintains one set of skills and instructions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, Antigravity and OpenCode, and can learn new preferences from the sessions you allow.
description_en: Shadowclone keeps your engineering preferences the same in every coding agent. It maintains one set of skills and instructions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, Antigravity and OpenCode, and can learn new preferences from the sessions you allow.
best_for: Sharing one set of rules across agents
Letting an agent work while you are away

use_cases.title: Equip every agent
use_cases.detail: One set of skills and instructions is delivered to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and Antigravity, and as a GitHub cloud bot.

use_cases.title: Work while you are away
use_cases.detail: Ask your agent to start a clone: it works with your skills, on your own subscription, in Docker on your own machine, and opens a draft pull request as you.

use_cases.title: Learn from sessions
use_cases.detail: Shadowclone can learn from your past sessions and keep skills in sync, if you agreed to it during setup.

pros: Not a separate agent: it equips the agent you already use
Installs by pasting one line into your agent, or with npm install -g @shadowclone/cli
Consent questions control whether it learns from your history
cons: Gives an agent your credentials and subscription to work unsupervised
Early project with an eval and results section rather than mature documentation

name: Commit-Aware Router
description: Commit-Aware Router is an open-source proof of concept that makes AI traffic decisions reflect the commercial commitments an organisation has already made, such as prepaid capacity or minimum-spend agreements, without sending contract amounts to the routing layer.
description_en: Commit-Aware Router is an open-source proof of concept that makes AI traffic decisions reflect the commercial commitments an organisation has already made, such as prepaid capacity or minimum-spend agreements, without sending contract amounts to the routing layer.
best_for: Routing LLM traffic with finance in the loop
Keeping contract values inside your own environment
Auditing why a route was chosen

use_cases.title: Add a commercial signal
use_cases.detail: Guidance from Finance becomes a routing signal with limits on its influence, which can change how the router ranks eligible routes.

use_cases.title: Keep contracts private
use_cases.detail: Detailed commercial inputs stay inside the customer environment; the router receives a short-lived, authenticated policy signal instead of raw contract values.

use_cases.title: Enforce constraints first
use_cases.detail: The router always enforces quality, capability, latency, reliability, residency and policy constraints before considering commercial preferences.

pros: Written for finance, FinOps, procurement and platform teams together
Produces an audit trail of routing decisions
Privacy is treated as a core requirement in the architecture
cons: An early open-source proof of concept, not a production router
You have to supply the finance data and policy signal yourself

name: Personal Agent Proxy
description: Personal Agent Proxy is an open-source, self-hostable access layer for the accounts your AI agents work with. You connect your services once, give each agent granular permissions, and audit its activity, without copying the contents of your connected services into its database.
description_en: Personal Agent Proxy is an open-source, self-hostable access layer for the accounts your AI agents work with. You connect your services once, give each agent granular permissions, and audit its activity, without copying the contents of your connected services into its database.
best_for: Stopping re-connecting every service to every agent
Giving each agent scoped, revocable access
Auditing what an agent did with your accounts

use_cases.title: Connect once
use_cases.detail: Connect email, calendar and notes once, then give each agent its own login instead of trusting one more company with all of them.

use_cases.title: Take connections with you
use_cases.detail: When you move to another agent your connections come with you, like an adapter.

use_cases.title: Audit every request
use_cases.detail: Every request an agent makes is checked against what you allowed and written to a log, allowed or denied.

pros: Nothing is copied from your connected services into its database
Designed to self-host with Postgres on your own server
Granular per-agent permissions rather than one shared token
cons: You run and secure the proxy and its Postgres database yourself
Only worth it once you have several agents that need the same accounts

name: Organ
description: Organ runs AI agents as departments for small agencies on a schedule, preparing plans, pull requests and drafts. Merges, outbound email and publishing wait for your approval.
description_en: Organ runs AI agents as departments for small agencies on a schedule, preparing plans, pull requests and drafts. Merges, outbound email and publishing wait for your approval.
best_for: Running routine agency work on a schedule
Getting drafts and pull requests queued for review
Keeping publish and merge behind your approval

use_cases.title: Ship code from tickets
use_cases.detail: The daily pipeline clones the repository, analyses the codebase, implements changes, runs validation, reviews and opens a pull request.

use_cases.title: Queue content
use_cases.detail: The content queue produces drafts with word counts, and approved posts go live; nothing publishes without your approval unless auto-publish is on.

use_cases.title: Escalate decisions
use_cases.detail: Daily operations runs report what needs you, including AI spend measured against a cap.

pros: Approval gates on merges, sending and publishing
Departments run on a schedule rather than one chat at a time
Public signup is open with a free start
cons: The marketing pages flag the workflows as illustrative
Pricing is not stated on the pages we read

name: Baa
description: Baa is a menu bar app that tells you when your Mac is about to run out of RAM or disk, finds what is quietly eating it, and frees it in one click. It was written for the dev servers, builds and agent leftovers that hold memory after you close the window.
description_en: Baa is a menu bar app that tells you when your Mac is about to run out of RAM or disk, finds what is quietly eating it, and frees it in one click. It was written for the dev servers, builds and agent leftovers that hold memory after you close the window.
best_for: Finding agent leftovers that hold RAM
Freeing memory from the menu bar
Watching disk space as well as RAM

use_cases.title: Watch the menu bar
use_cases.detail: Baa warns you when your Mac is about to run out of RAM or disk.

use_cases.title: Find the culprits
use_cases.detail: It finds the processes quietly eating memory, typically dev servers, builds and agent leftovers rather than open apps.

use_cases.title: Free it in one click
use_cases.detail: Shear the leftovers from the menu bar panel and watch free RAM climb.

pros: Menu bar app with a one-click action, no terminal
Covers disk as well as RAM
Small, single-purpose and open source
cons: macOS only
It frees memory; it does not fix whatever allocated it

name: Mastershot
description: Mastershot Studio is a free online video editor with no watermark on anything you export. You trim, combine and add music, text and subtitles in one project, and files open straight from your computer so nothing has to be uploaded first.
description_en: Mastershot Studio is a free online video editor with no watermark on anything you export. You trim, combine and add music, text and subtitles in one project, and files open straight from your computer so nothing has to be uploaded first.
best_for: Editing a video without paying or watermarking
Working on large local files in the browser
Adding subtitles and music in one project

use_cases.title: Edit on a timeline
use_cases.detail: Drag clips into order, trim their ends and split them at the playhead, with text, pictures and music on the rows above and below.

use_cases.title: Export once
use_cases.detail: Pick a size and export an MP4 with no watermark, in up to 4K, made on your computer.

use_cases.title: Skip the upload
use_cases.detail: Files open straight from your computer, so even a 2 GB video is ready right away.

pros: No watermark on exports
Runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on a computer with local file access
Free to start with no card needed
cons: A browser editor, so heavy projects depend on your machine
The AI tools panel sits beyond the described free editor

name: Vigil
description: Vigil is an AI harness for code audits, web pentests and bug bounty hunting. It coordinates Claude Code or Codex through broad review, focused rereads, authenticated testing and runtime reproduction, and carries findings, evidence and coverage across sessions.
description_en: Vigil is an AI harness for code audits, web pentests and bug bounty hunting. It coordinates Claude Code or Codex through broad review, focused rereads, authenticated testing and runtime reproduction, and carries findings, evidence and coverage across sessions.
best_for: Running long code audits with an agent
Reproducing a candidate bug before reporting it
Keeping findings and evidence across sessions

use_cases.title: Start broad, then focus
use_cases.detail: The first pass is a starting point; higher-risk code gets another look with a different objective, and specialists follow callers, challenge guards and hunt variants.

use_cases.title: Prove it at runtime
use_cases.detail: Promising leads stay on the books when runtime proof or access is still missing, so an unsupported impact claim does not ship.

use_cases.title: Hand off between sessions
use_cases.detail: Findings, evidence, coverage and handoffs carry across sessions rather than restarting each run.

pros: Built by an application security engineer and refined over eight months of hands-on use
Apache-2.0, Python 3.11+, and works from a codebase, a live application or both
You stay the operator: you review what the agents test and why
cons: Authorized use only: it drives offensive tooling against live systems
Investigation quality still depends on the model and on your review

name: Faplex
description: Faplex is a status list for the Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions you already have, on every machine you can ssh to. It reads what the harnesses report and opens the harness own CLI on the row you pick.
description_en: Faplex is a status list for the Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions you already have, on every machine you can ssh to. It reads what the harnesses report and opens the harness own CLI on the row you pick.
best_for: Seeing every agent session across machines
Attaching a session started somewhere else
Avoiding a wrapper around your harness

use_cases.title: One grouped list
use_cases.detail: Working, Needs input and Finished across every machine and harness, with context tokens and subagent counts.

use_cases.title: Open the real CLI
use_cases.detail: A row is claude attach, codex resume or opencode -s handed your terminal, so every harness feature works as it does without faplex.

use_cases.title: Add hosts with no config
use_cases.detail: Run faplex devbox pi to cover this machine plus two ssh hosts.

pros: No hooks, plugins or wrapper, and nothing to install on remote machines
Sessions started anywhere show up, not only ones started from faplex
No live CLI per idle session; a client starts when you open a row
cons: Early alpha with rough edges
Requires Bun, and only covers Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode

name: Tutor
description: Tutor is a self-hosted AI tutor that turns your books, online documentation and YouTube videos into a course. It maps the concepts, tests what you know, and teaches the rest with references to the sources.
description_en: Tutor is a self-hosted AI tutor that turns your books, online documentation and YouTube videos into a course. It maps the concepts, tests what you know, and teaches the rest with references to the sources.
best_for: Turning a book into a course
Learning from YouTube playlists with transcripts

use_cases.title: Add any material
use_cases.detail: Add EPUB and tagged PDF files, online books and documentation by address, or YouTube videos and playlists where a video model writes the transcript including code on screen.

use_cases.title: See the concept map
use_cases.detail: Every source becomes a book with chapters on one concept map, with colour showing the status of each concept.

use_cases.title: Learn and test
use_cases.detail: The tutor checks which concepts you know, teaches the others one at a time with references to the books, and tests each one.

pros: Runs on your computer with your own key from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or Google
Covers all the concepts in the material, not just the ones you ask about
Lessons carry numbered references back to the source
cons: You pay for the model API calls and supply the keys
Self-hosted, so setup and model choice are on you

name: Rutter
description: Rutter is a personal memory layer for AI agents. It keeps a record of what you decided, which notes the session cited and how your thinking changed, stored as plain Markdown in a folder you own, and any MCP client can recall it.
description_en: Rutter is a personal memory layer for AI agents. It keeps a record of what you decided, which notes the session cited and how your thinking changed, stored as plain Markdown in a folder you own, and any MCP client can recall it.
best_for: Sharing one memory across several agents
Keeping decisions in Markdown you own
Recalling a stance you formed weeks ago

use_cases.title: Capture after each turn
use_cases.detail: Six harnesses have a working capture hook: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, GitHub Copilot CLI, Antigravity CLI and Muse Code.

use_cases.title: Recall from any client
use_cases.detail: Once registered in each client and pointed at the same notes folder, each can recall the same records, including any MCP client.

use_cases.title: Track positions
use_cases.detail: A stance you formed or changed is recorded as a position, so you can see how your thinking moved.

pros: Records are plain Markdown in your own notes folder, not inside a model or a vendor account
Memory travels when you switch tools
Setup takes a few minutes with Claude Code
cons: Capture needs the hook to run and the model to leave a line
Only the six listed harnesses have a capture hook today

name: Kenerate
description: Kenerate is an AI creative studio that makes images, videos and music in one workspace. You start from text or reference media, choose a model and try it with free signup credits.
description_en: Kenerate is an AI creative studio that makes images, videos and music in one workspace. You start from text or reference media, choose a model and try it with free signup credits.
best_for: Generating image, video and audio in one place
Trying named video and image models
Making product and ad clips from a prompt

use_cases.title: Generate video
use_cases.detail: Start from a first frame or a reference image, then pick a model with length and resolution shown before you generate.

use_cases.title: Generate images
use_cases.detail: Make the image you have in mind from text or reference media.

use_cases.title: Generate audio
use_cases.detail: Give an idea a soundtrack, or create through an agent in a conversation.

pros: Image, video and music in one workspace rather than three subscriptions
Free signup credits so you can try models before paying
The credit cost is shown per generation before you run it
cons: Credit-based pricing, so heavy video generation gets expensive
A model aggregator, so output depends on the third-party model you pick

name: Moching
description: Moching is a desktop AI operator that controls a whole PC: 219 tools covering screen perception, HID control, browser automation, an Office suite and AI media. One sentence in, finished work out, running locally with data that stays on the device.
description_en: Moching is a desktop AI operator that controls a whole PC: 219 tools covering screen perception, HID control, browser automation, an Office suite and AI media. One sentence in, finished work out, running locally with data that stays on the device.
best_for: Automating desktop and Office work by voice or text
Driving a browser and the mouse and keyboard
Running tasks on many machines at once

use_cases.title: Control the desktop
use_cases.detail: Screen perception plus keyboard and mouse control take over the machine from one instruction.

use_cases.title: Work across Office
use_cases.detail: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF are driven with natural language instructions.

use_cases.title: Write and build software
use_cases.detail: It writes code through to compilation and build, with LSP-level understanding of the project.

pros: 219 built-in tools covering screen, HID, browser, Office and media
Local SQLite storage with data that stays on the device and your own API keys
Supports any model API as well as locally deployed models
cons: A desktop app for Windows and macOS with a closed-source client
Credits are consumed per token, per second of video and per image on top of your own model costs

name: Spectra
description: Spectra is a drop-in optimizer replacement for AdamW that shifts gradient optimization to the frequency domain and factorizes second-moment variance, cutting optimizer state memory by 50% while keeping full 32-bit floating-point stability.
description_en: Spectra is a drop-in optimizer replacement for AdamW that shifts gradient optimization to the frequency domain and factorizes second-moment variance, cutting optimizer state memory by 50% while keeping full 32-bit floating-point stability.
best_for: Training an LLM when optimizer state does not fit
Keeping full float stability without quantization

use_cases.title: Swap it in
use_cases.detail: Replace torch.optim.AdamW with Spectra in one line and leave the training loop unchanged.

use_cases.title: Halve optimizer state
use_cases.detail: The project benchmarks optimizer state at 4130 MB against 8256 MB for standard AdamW on a 12-layer transformer block.

use_cases.title: Watch the run
use_cases.detail: Training logs for the benchmark runs are published on Weights and Biases.

pros: One-line drop-in for PyTorch AdamW
No quantization collapse: full 32-bit floating-point stability is retained
Apache 2.0 licensed
cons: The benchmarks are the project own, on a single 12-layer block
Requires PyTorch 2.0+ and Python 3.10+

name: Widefleet
description: Widefleet is an open-source platform for agent-built apps and workflows. Your coding agent creates and manages apps through the Widefleet CLI, with company login, a database and file storage per app, and controlled access to your systems.
description_en: Widefleet is an open-source platform for agent-built apps and workflows. Your coding agent creates and manages apps through the Widefleet CLI, with company login, a database and file storage per app, and controlled access to your systems.
best_for: Giving each app its own database and files
Keeping company login in front of agent-built apps

use_cases.title: Keep working in your tools
use_cases.detail: Your coding agent creates and manages apps through the Widefleet CLI, so you stay in the tools you already use.

use_cases.title: Give each app storage
use_cases.detail: Each app gets its own database and private file storage, preserved across code deployments.

use_cases.title: Deploy and roll back
use_cases.detail: Deploy changes, test them in isolated previews, inspect logs and errors, and roll back to an earlier code version.

pros: Fully open source and self-hostable on your own infrastructure
Connects to your company identity provider and existing systems
Background jobs and schedules keep routine work moving beyond the browser
cons: You operate the platform yourself; a hosted cloud option is still coming
Early project with a narrow set of documented integrations

name: Pullboard
description: Pullboard is a work board that lives in your git repo, where governed agents build from specs you approve and follow the rules you set. Nothing merges until another agent proves it, and every claim, submit, reject and accept is recorded in order.
description_en: Pullboard is a work board that lives in your git repo, where governed agents build from specs you approve and follow the rules you set. Nothing merges until another agent proves it, and every claim, submit, reject and accept is recorded in order.
best_for: Running several agents on one repo

use_cases.title: Pick up the next task
use_cases.detail: Items each carry a bar they are checked against, and one agent works an item at a time.

use_cases.title: Approve the spec
use_cases.detail: Spec holds the plan one row per requirement, and only the rows you approve count.

use_cases.title: Enforce doctrine
use_cases.detail: Doctrine holds your house rules, each with what enforces it, from a git hook to review.

pros: A second agent verdict gates the merge
Blueprints capture software patterns your agents cannot forget
Relay lets agents on any machine share one board, runnable from your phone
cons: Requires agents running in a shell on your repos
Heavy process: specs, doctrine and a gate before anything lands

name: Narwhal
description: Narwhal is adaptive hot-swap disaggregation for LLM inference on a role-free fleet, so GPUs move between prefill and decode instead of being pinned to one role. It ships with documentation for deploying, measuring and operating the fleet.
description_en: Narwhal is adaptive hot-swap disaggregation for LLM inference on a role-free fleet, so GPUs move between prefill and decode instead of being pinned to one role. It ships with documentation for deploying, measuring and operating the fleet.
best_for: Disaggregating prefill and decode on your own GPUs
Benchmarking a router against measured targets

use_cases.title: Deploy a fleet
use_cases.detail: Docs cover discovering the deployment, installing an approved revision, validating and starting engines, qualifying the transfer fabric and attesting live engines.

use_cases.title: Measure before you trust it
use_cases.detail: Measuring covers the measurement contract and profiling, targets and a deployment freeze, a synthetic load trial and reconciling accepted benchmark points.

use_cases.title: Operate it
use_cases.detail: Control covers engine restart and process replacement, upgrade and rollback with release drills, and dashboards read through Grafana.

pros: Role-free fleet: GPUs are not pinned to prefill or decode
Full documentation for deployment, measurement and operations
Installable from PyPI with a documented recovery and qualification path
cons: Documentation-heavy: you profile and qualify the transfer fabric before serving
Targets GPU fleets, so it is not a single-machine setup

name: Senro
description: Senro is a WebMCP evaluation and observability platform. It tests your WebMCP tools and monitors how AI agents use them in production, without requiring you to build the reliability infrastructure yourself.
description_en: Senro is a WebMCP evaluation and observability platform. It tests your WebMCP tools and monitors how AI agents use them in production, without requiring you to build the reliability infrastructure yourself.
best_for: Watching how agents use your site

use_cases.title: Evaluate before production
use_cases.detail: Smoke testing, goal evaluation, trajectory evaluation, page checks, simulated users and multi-model comparison.

use_cases.title: Observe in production
use_cases.detail: Tool activity, inputs, results and errors, session timelines, production context, issue tracking and usage and error metrics.

use_cases.title: Make the site agent-native
use_cases.detail: Use the findings to make your website reliable for AI agents.

pros: Covers both pre-production evaluation and production observability
Try free with no credit card required
Focused specifically on WebMCP rather than generic analytics
cons: A new product surface that only pays off if you expose WebMCP tools
Pricing tiers are not stated on the pages we read

name: Wy
description: Wy turns an uncommitted diff into the questions you would need to answer to accept it, and shows which of them the agent own record actually answers. It imports existing local Codex, Claude Code, pi and OpenCode history, so no recorder has to be running first.
description_en: Wy turns an uncommitted diff into the questions you would need to answer to accept it, and shows which of them the agent own record actually answers. It imports existing local Codex, Claude Code, pi and OpenCode history, so no recorder has to be running first.
best_for: Reviewing AI changes in a domain you do not know
Seeing where the agent gave no reason
Feeding your verdicts back to the agent

use_cases.title: Read the plan screen
use_cases.detail: Four boxes: What changed, What to worry about, Was it tested and Progress, and every row opens its evidence.

use_cases.title: Follow the audit trail
use_cases.detail: The Steps screen shows the session as intent-sized steps, each with Why, Check, Gap and the worries it raises.

use_cases.title: Export your verdicts
use_cases.detail: Verdicts persist and export as a review in your voice, push-backs first, so they paste back to the agent as the next instruction.

pros: Missing evidence stays missing; a nearby message is never treated as a proven reason
Nothing calls a model until you open the ? row on the plan
Attribution is a textual match between a hunk and a captured edit, or nothing
cons: Depends on captured session history from the four supported harnesses
A terminal tool, so there is no GUI

name: Seahaven
description: Seahaven is an open-source Python framework for building synthetic worlds: working copies of your agent tools, realistic enough that the agent cannot tell the difference. It is used for RL and evaluation environments.
description_en: Seahaven is an open-source Python framework for building synthetic worlds: working copies of your agent tools, realistic enough that the agent cannot tell the difference. It is used for RL and evaluation environments.
best_for: Running evals against realistic tool copies
Grading on state instead of transcripts

use_cases.title: One world per run
use_cases.detail: Each instance is its own SQLite database, copied from a fixture in milliseconds and thrown away at the end.

use_cases.title: Freeze starting states
use_cases.detail: Fixtures freeze states such as small_startup or big_co once and reuse them, so the same fixture, clock and seed give the same run.

use_cases.title: Run hundreds in one process
use_cases.detail: seahaven serve hosts hundreds of world instances per process at thousands of requests per second.

pros: Grades on state: every row the agent changed is logged before and after in one JSON document
Worlds are throwaway, so runs do not contaminate each other
Open source, from Kiln AI
cons: A Python framework, so you build and maintain the worlds yourself
Aimed at evals and RL rather than production agent traffic

name: LLMSchema
description: LLMSchema extracts database schemas from PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite into simple, concise Markdown documentation for LLMs and AI agents, so they get an accurate data model without reconstructing it from application code and migration histories.
description_en: LLMSchema extracts database schemas from PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite into simple, concise Markdown documentation for LLMs and AI agents, so they get an accurate data model without reconstructing it from application code and migration histories.
best_for: Giving an agent an accurate schema
Feeding schema context without blowing the window

use_cases.title: Generate one document
use_cases.detail: Run llmschema -o schema.md to write tables, columns, types, indexes, constraints and relationships into a single portable Markdown file.

use_cases.title: Split per table
use_cases.detail: Optional per-table files are available when one document is too large.

use_cases.title: Install it with an agent
use_cases.detail: You can give your AI coding agent the repository URL and ask it to install LLMSchema and set it up for your project.

pros: Works with PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite from one CLI
Usable as a Go library as well as a CLI
Concise output designed not to overwhelm a context window
cons: Intended for development databases, not production-critical documentation
Static output: it does not track schema changes on its own

name: DiffGuardian
description: DiffGuardian gives you a spoken walkthrough of a pull request or codebase, highlighting the code and building live visuals as it answers. It reads Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro and plain PLAN.md files and turns them into a summary, an architecture diagram, a data model and API tables.
description_en: DiffGuardian gives you a spoken walkthrough of a pull request or codebase, highlighting the code and building live visuals as it answers. It reads Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro and plain PLAN.md files and turns them into a summary, an architecture diagram, a data model and API tables.
best_for: Understanding agent-written plans without reading them
Getting a spoken pull request walkthrough
Reviewing a codebase you did not write

use_cases.title: Understand the plan
use_cases.detail: Plans from Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro or PLAN.md become a summary, an architecture diagram, a data model and API tables.

use_cases.title: Ask by voice
use_cases.detail: Hold Space, ask, and hear the answer while the code is highlighted and live visuals build.

use_cases.title: Trace the codebase
use_cases.detail: Ask questions about the codebase and get answers with the relevant code highlighted.

pros: Native apps for Apple silicon, Intel Mac, Windows and Linux
Your code never touches their servers: your own keys or fully local models
Voice runs on OpenAI, ElevenLabs or your system voice
cons: Pricing is not stated on the pages we read
Centred on voice, which will not suit every review setting

name: CloudGrip
description: CloudGrip is a lightweight, self-hosted AI proxy gateway and dashboard built with Node.js, Express and SQLite. It enforces strict budget caps and gives real-time visibility over LLM API spend and request logs.
description_en: CloudGrip is a lightweight, self-hosted AI proxy gateway and dashboard built with Node.js, Express and SQLite. It enforces strict budget caps and gives real-time visibility over LLM API spend and request logs.
best_for: Capping LLM spend before it runs away
Watching request logs from one dashboard
Keeping proxy logs on your own instance

use_cases.title: Break the circuit
use_cases.detail: A budget circuit-breaker automatically halts requests when spending reaches the configured cap.

use_cases.title: Watch telemetry
use_cases.detail: Real-time telemetry tracks client spend, request metadata and token metrics.

use_cases.title: Self-host it
use_cases.detail: Run the Express server against your own database connection string; logs and proxy state stay in your instance.

pros: MIT licensed and self-hosted
Built-in dark-mode admin dashboard for active users and token metrics
Targets runaway agent loops and unmonitored context reloads specifically
cons: You run Node, Express and a database yourself
Small early project with few integrations beyond the proxy and dashboard

name: KORA Doctor
description: KORA Doctor is a small open-source CLI that analyzes AUDR JSON and JSONL and surfaces execution waste across tool usage, context growth, deterministic work, repeated inference, orchestration and model choice. There is no dashboard, no account and no hosted service.
description_en: KORA Doctor is a small open-source CLI that analyzes AUDR JSON and JSONL and surfaces execution waste across tool usage, context growth, deterministic work, repeated inference, orchestration and model choice. There is no dashboard, no account and no hosted service.
best_for: Finding avoidable cost in agent runs
Auditing repeated tool and read calls

use_cases.title: Audit a run
use_cases.detail: Run kora-doctor audit on an AUDR file to see observed cost, potentially avoidable spend and an estimated optimized cost.

use_cases.title: Get JSON out
use_cases.detail: Add --json for machine-readable output you can diff or feed to another system.

use_cases.title: Join OTel data
use_cases.detail: Pass --otel with an OTel sidecar file to combine execution records with telemetry.

pros: Runs entirely locally with no account or hosted service
Gives a concrete avoidable-cost figure per run
Works on the open AUDR record format
cons: Only reads AUDR records, so your agent has to emit them first
Heuristics are early and the sample is synthetic, not a benchmark

name: Zetteldesk
description: Zetteldesk is a mail agent plugin for Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code: your agent writes the letter in the chat and checks the PDF against DIN 5008, and Zetteldesk prints it, puts it in an envelope and takes it to the post office.
description_en: Zetteldesk is a mail agent plugin for Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code: your agent writes the letter in the chat and checks the PDF against DIN 5008, and Zetteldesk prints it, puts it in an envelope and takes it to the post office.
best_for: Sending physical mail from an AI assistant
Cancellations and notices that need registered post
Letting an agent verify a letter before it is sent

use_cases.title: Connect once
use_cases.detail: Enter one URL in Claude.ai, ChatGPT or Claude Code and sign in with standard OAuth, so no API keys sit in the chat history.

use_cases.title: Let the agent check it
use_cases.detail: Before anything costs money, the agent checks the A4 format, address field and page count and gets an exact price quote to show you.

use_cases.title: Track the post
use_cases.detail: After you confirm, the letter is printed and posted in Germany, with status visible on the web or by asking your agent.

pros: Registered mail and proof of delivery available
Prepaid from EUR 1.12 per letter with no subscription and a money-back promise if a letter is rejected
Works with any client that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in
cons: Letters are posted from Germany, so delivery times and coverage are regional
Per-letter cost, which does not suit bulk mail

name: Liatir
description: Liatir is a local-first desktop environment for bioinformatics, built with Rust, Tauri 2 and SvelteKit. It brings native tools, locally managed AI models, .lia plugins, visual pipelines and scientific viewers into one application, with a controlled local MCP interface.
description_en: Liatir is a local-first desktop environment for bioinformatics, built with Rust, Tauri 2 and SvelteKit. It brings native tools, locally managed AI models, .lia plugins, visual pipelines and scientific viewers into one application, with a controlled local MCP interface.
best_for: Managing AI models on your own machine

use_cases.title: Run analyses offline
use_cases.detail: Local analyses keep working offline once their dependencies are installed.

use_cases.title: Keep provenance
use_cases.detail: Workspaces retain inputs, execution logs, results and provenance.

use_cases.title: Connect other apps
use_cases.detail: A controlled local MCP interface connects other applications, alongside API connectors and external workflow integrations.

pros: Data never leaves the machine, with Rust-powered speed even on multi-gigabyte files
Plugins, visual pipelines and scientific viewers in one app
Published scientific showcases documenting methods, results and limitations
cons: GPL v3 licensed desktop app for scientists, not a general-purpose AI tool
You install and manage the underlying tools and models yourself

name: Manifestack
description: Manifestack is a free skill for your coding agent that prices every service at your usage on the vendor own pages. Ask what your stack will cost at 50k users and it finds the bills, plan limits and compliance gaps ahead, each with a fix.
description_en: Manifestack is a free skill for your coding agent that prices every service at your usage on the vendor own pages. Ask what your stack will cost at 50k users and it finds the bills, plan limits and compliance gaps ahead, each with a fix.
best_for: Pricing a stack before you ship it
Finding plan limits that break at scale
Spotting services you pay for twice

use_cases.title: Price at your usage
use_cases.detail: Ask what a stack costs at 50k users and get every service priced on the vendor own pages.

use_cases.title: Find what breaks
use_cases.detail: The report flags the plan limits that take a product down, the data rules it breaks and services you pay for twice.

use_cases.title: Fix each finding
use_cases.detail: Every finding comes with the fix that cuts it.

pros: Free skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others
Prices are read from vendor pages rather than a static table
Aimed at developers, small teams and agencies rather than enterprise FinOps
cons: Prices are read from vendor pages at a point in time and drift
Requires Node.js 22 or newer

name: Mcpward
description: Mcpward is contract and security testing for MCP servers, in CI. It snapshots an MCP server contract and fails the build when it changes underneath you, catching schema drift, silently changed tool descriptions, protocol violations and tool-poisoning patterns.
description_en: Mcpward is contract and security testing for MCP servers, in CI. It snapshots an MCP server contract and fails the build when it changes underneath you, catching schema drift, silently changed tool descriptions, protocol violations and tool-poisoning patterns.
best_for: Testing third-party MCP servers in CI
Catching a rug-pull before it ships
Reporting MCP drift as a pull-request comment

use_cases.title: Pin the contract
use_cases.detail: Run mcpward baseline to capture tools into mcpward.lock.json and commit it, refreshing it only deliberately.

use_cases.title: Fail on drift
use_cases.detail: Run mcpward diff in CI to catch schema drift, a readOnlyHint flip or a breaking schema change.

use_cases.title: Report it
use_cases.detail: Results go to console, JSON, JUnit, SARIF or Markdown, and can be posted as a pull-request comment.

pros: Black-box, so it works against servers you did not write, over stdio or Streamable HTTP
Runs entirely on your machine: no account, no API calls, no telemetry
Works against MCP servers written in any language
cons: Requires Node.js 22 or newer
A CI job that re-baselines automatically would accept a rug-pull as the new contract

name: Octri
description: Octri takes an OpenAPI spec all the way to production: a docs site, SDKs in ten languages, an MCP server that exposes your API as tools for AI agents, and monitoring of errors from your SDKs and your API.
description_en: Octri takes an OpenAPI spec all the way to production: a docs site, SDKs in ten languages, an MCP server that exposes your API as tools for AI agents, and monitoring of errors from your SDKs and your API.
best_for: Generating docs and SDKs from one spec
Exposing an API to agents over MCP

use_cases.title: Build the docs
use_cases.detail: Octri builds a docs site and API guides from your OpenAPI spec.

use_cases.title: Ship SDKs
use_cases.detail: Client libraries are generated in ten languages.

use_cases.title: Give agents tools
use_cases.detail: An MCP server turns your API into tools for AI agents, and monitoring captures errors from your SDKs and your API.

pros: Docs, SDKs, MCP and monitoring from one spec
Free tools include a spec audit, an OpenAPI parser and a spec converter
Public samples built from OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub and other real specs
cons: Built around OpenAPI, so other API descriptions need conversion first
A commercial product whose migration guides target switching from other vendors

name: Azurade
description: Azurade gives you one API key for Veo 3.1, Seedance and Nano Banana: pay as you go for 45 image and video models, from a REST API or from an MCP server that Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex connect to with one sign-in.
description_en: Azurade gives you one API key for Veo 3.1, Seedance and Nano Banana: pay as you go for 45 image and video models, from a REST API or from an MCP server that Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex connect to with one sign-in.
best_for: Reaching many image and video models from one key
Generating media from Claude or Codex over MCP
Paying per generation without a subscription

use_cases.title: Use it from an agent
use_cases.detail: Connect the MCP server to Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor or VS Code with one sign-in.

use_cases.title: Call the REST API
use_cases.detail: Use /api/v2 with keys as Bearer tokens from your own code.

use_cases.title: Track credits
use_cases.detail: A credit costs USD 0.02 to 0.04 with no subscription, credits never expire, and failed generations are refunded automatically.

pros: One key and one balance across 45 models, including Veo 3.1, Seedance and Nano Banana
Credits never expire and failures are refunded without a ticket
The same credit balance and prices as the web app
cons: Pay as you go only, with 4 free credits on signup
An aggregator, so availability and quality depend on upstream models

name: SEO Audit Console
description: SEO Audit Console is a free, open-source MCP server that pulls your crawl and Google Search Console data into a database on your own PC, merging DataForSEO and Majestic SEO into one prioritised audit that Claude runs.
description_en: SEO Audit Console is a free, open-source MCP server that pulls your crawl and Google Search Console data into a database on your own PC, merging DataForSEO and Majestic SEO into one prioritised audit that Claude runs.
best_for: Running a technical SEO audit with Claude
Keeping crawl data on your own machine

use_cases.title: Capture the raw data
use_cases.detail: The server captures and stores crawl, Search Console, DataForSEO and Majestic data locally so the audit runs from your own database.

use_cases.title: Rank the fixes
use_cases.detail: The merged audit is prioritised, and the published guide covers how findings become fixes with a dashboard.

use_cases.title: Replace paid tools
use_cases.detail: The walkthrough runs on a real site with no Semrush or Screaming Frog.

pros: Free and open source, with data stored on your own PC
Combines a first-party crawl with Search Console, DataForSEO and Majestic
Documented end to end in a published guide
cons: You still supply API access for the third-party data sources
Requires Claude and an MCP client to drive the audit

name: LangGraph Harness
description: LangGraph Harness is a self-hosted AI coding agent platform for GitLab, built with LangGraph. It reviews merge requests, resolves issues autonomously and chats with full project context, remembering what matters so every run builds on the last.
description_en: LangGraph Harness is a self-hosted AI coding agent platform for GitLab, built with LangGraph. It reviews merge requests, resolves issues autonomously and chats with full project context, remembering what matters so every run builds on the last.
best_for: Turning GitLab issues into merge requests

use_cases.title: Review merge requests
use_cases.detail: The MR Review webhook fires on webhook events, reads the diff, drafts comments and publishes them, with no polling or manual triage.

use_cases.title: Assign an issue
use_cases.detail: Assign an issue and get a merge request back.

use_cases.title: Watch the runs
use_cases.detail: A React admin UI shows live runs, queue state and per-project analytics including reliability, guardrail health and comment acceptance rate.

pros: Self-hosted, so code and project context stay on your infrastructure
Built on LangGraph with documented architecture and deployment
Live analytics rather than a black box you find out about later
cons: GitLab only; there is no GitHub support
Setup needs a GitLab PAT, a GitLab OAuth app and an LLM backend key

name: Genjutsu AI
description: Genjutsu AI transfers the original motion and timing of a video into a new scene, style or set of objects, without swapping who or what is in the shot. Motion transfer and object swap both run up to 1080p.
description_en: Genjutsu AI transfers the original motion and timing of a video into a new scene, style or set of objects, without swapping who or what is in the shot. Motion transfer and object swap both run up to 1080p.
best_for: Keeping a subject while changing the scene
Swapping objects and products into a clip
Starting from a proven motion template

use_cases.title: Transfer motion
use_cases.detail: Add a reference video of 4 to 30 seconds and carry its motion and timing into a new scene or style.

use_cases.title: Swap objects
use_cases.detail: Add up to 8 images to put products, clothes, objects or scenes into the shot.

use_cases.title: Start from a template
use_cases.detail: Motion templates fill the generator with a proven setup, then you add images and generate.

pros: Keeps the original subject and timing instead of regenerating the shot
Output up to 1080p
A template library to start from
cons: Credit-based generation with the balance shown in the interface
Trend-led templates, so results depend on the template and reference video

name: PR Lens
description: PR Lens draws animated architecture and data-flow walkthroughs inside the pull request itself, so you can understand a change and catch what could break before reading a single line. It runs as a GitHub App, GitHub Action, CLI or agent skill.
description_en: PR Lens draws animated architecture and data-flow walkthroughs inside the pull request itself, so you can understand a change and catch what could break before reading a single line. It runs as a GitHub App, GitHub Action, CLI or agent skill.
best_for: Understanding a large pull request quickly

use_cases.title: See the architecture
use_cases.detail: Animated diagrams show services, data stores and endpoints as changed, new or removed.

use_cases.title: Follow the data flow
use_cases.detail: A second view traces the flow, with per-file additions and deletions and a written description of the change.

use_cases.title: Install it your way
use_cases.detail: Use the GitHub App, a GitHub Action, the CLI, or add it as a skill with npx skills add coldteadotai/pr-lens.

pros: Open source core that works locally
Four install paths, including inside your coding agent
Diagrams live in the pull request rather than a separate site
cons: Best value on large architectural changes; small diffs gain less
The hosted app and some features sit outside the open-source core

name: Recast
description: Recast is a Smalltalk application that uses an LLM to repair itself while it runs. A failing call supplies the stack, method source, receiver state and tests, and a separate VM checks the proposed repair before the application replaces the method in its live image.
description_en: Recast is a Smalltalk application that uses an LLM to repair itself while it runs. A failing call supplies the stack, method source, receiver state and tests, and a separate VM checks the proposed repair before the application replaces the method in its live image.
best_for: Experimenting with runtime evidence for repairs

use_cases.title: Let it repair
use_cases.detail: The first call fails, investigation and verification run asynchronously, the image applies the accepted patch, and the next call succeeds.

use_cases.title: Check before applying
use_cases.detail: A separate VM verifies a proposed repair before the running application adopts it, with no rebuild or restart.

use_cases.title: Try the tour
use_cases.detail: GUIDE.md walks through booting, editing live code, breaking the app and promoting the result, with an offline fake LLM option.

pros: No rebuild or restart: subsequent calls use the new code immediately
Verification is a separate step, not a blind patch
Exercised with a real LLM on Pharo 12
cons: An experiment in Smalltalk, not a production self-healing framework
Needs a Smalltalk image and a guided tour to get anything running

name: Usermods
description: Usermods is an open-source browser extension that lets you customize any website by chatting with the LLM of your choice. It inspects the page, writes a userscript, tests it live and hands it to you with Try and Save buttons, and saved mods run on every matching page load.
description_en: Usermods is an open-source browser extension that lets you customize any website by chatting with the LLM of your choice. It inspects the page, writes a userscript, tests it live and hands it to you with Try and Save buttons, and saved mods run on every matching page load.
best_for: Changing a website you do not control

use_cases.title: Describe the change
use_cases.detail: Open the side panel on any page, describe what you want changed, and the model reads a pruned DOM, computed styles and screenshots before proposing anything.

use_cases.title: Keep the mods
use_cases.detail: Saved mods run automatically on every matching page load and export as standard .user.js files.

use_cases.title: Bring your library
use_cases.detail: Install mods from Greasy Fork or migrate your whole Tampermonkey library in one file.

pros: Any backend: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or anything OpenAI-compatible including Ollama and LM Studio
Mods are plain userscripts with a ==UserScript== header, MIT licensed
Can sign in with ChatGPT or SuperGrok to use the subscription you already pay for, in the build from source
cons: Early status, and the Chrome Web Store version leaves sign-in out
A browser extension with page access, so it needs trust

name: Recursant
description: Recursant sits between your AI agents and the models they use and picks a model for every step: a top model for the hard steps, a cheaper model for routine ones, and your own private model whenever personal data is involved.
description_en: Recursant sits between your AI agents and the models they use and picks a model for every step: a top model for the hard steps, a cheaper model for routine ones, and your own private model whenever personal data is involved.
best_for: Cutting the agent bill without changing the agent
Keeping personal data on your own GPUs

use_cases.title: Route per step
use_cases.detail: Routine steps such as reading a file or running tests go to a cheaper model while thinking-heavy steps stay on the main model, and a stronger model is brought in if the agent keeps failing.

use_cases.title: Keep personal data private
use_cases.detail: Every request is checked with regexes for tax file numbers, Medicare numbers, card numbers, phone numbers and email addresses before it leaves your machine; matches go to your private model.

use_cases.title: Point your agent at it
use_cases.detail: It speaks the OpenAI API, so you point your agent at Recursant instead of the provider, with no plugins and no code changes.

pros: A deterministic privacy check runs before any request leaves the machine
Models on your own GPUs and paid services sit in one pool
Written in C with minimal dependencies
cons: Linux only today; macOS support is underway and Windows is described as tricky
Tested with Hermes and pi, with other harnesses still being validated

name: Recly
description: Recly turns the Galaxy Watch or Apple Watch you already wear into an AI recorder. One shortcut records, transcription is free on a supported device, and a ChatGPT agent starts on the minutes by itself through MCP when the transcript lands.
description_en: Recly turns the Galaxy Watch or Apple Watch you already wear into an AI recorder. One shortcut records, transcription is free on a supported device, and a ChatGPT agent starts on the minutes by itself through MCP when the transcript lands.
best_for: Recording without buying a dedicated device
Letting an agent write the minutes

use_cases.title: Use the watch you own
use_cases.detail: One shortcut on a Galaxy Watch or Apple Watch starts recording, instead of buying a dedicated recorder.

use_cases.title: Transcribe for free
use_cases.detail: Transcription runs for free on a supported device, and the original audio stays in your own Google Drive.

use_cases.title: Hand it to an agent
use_cases.detail: A ChatGPT agent starts on the minutes by itself through MCP the moment the transcript lands.

pros: Free and open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later
On the App Store and Google Play, with macOS and Windows builds too
Keeps the original audio in your own Google Drive
cons: Depends on you already owning a supported watch
You supply the AI that writes the notes

name: Baloo
description: Baloo is an open source GitHub App for AI pull request review. It installs on your repositories, reads PR diffs and relevant project context, and posts inline review comments that catch bugs, security issues, missing error handling and repository guideline violations.
description_en: Baloo is an open source GitHub App for AI pull request review. It installs on your repositories, reads PR diffs and relevant project context, and posts inline review comments that catch bugs, security issues, missing error handling and repository guideline violations.
best_for: Self-hosted AI code review on GitHub

use_cases.title: Review on every push
use_cases.detail: New commits on non-draft PRs are reviewed automatically with discussion thread tracking across iterations; comment @baloo review for another pass.

use_cases.title: Follow your conventions
use_cases.detail: Baloo reads AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md from the repo and enforces them, and follows a per-PR review brief when one is included.

use_cases.title: Self-host it
use_cases.detail: You run the service, control the GitHub App installation scope, and provide your own model credentials.

pros: Self-hosted with no Baloo-hosted backend; review context goes only to your configured model provider
Posts like a teammate: inline comments, severity labels and an approval when no CRITICAL or HIGH issues remain
MIT licensed with OpenSSF Scorecard and CI in place
cons: You operate the app and supply model credentials
GitHub only, and it never blocks a merge: humans decide

name: EditUI
description: EditUI is a Chrome extension for reviewing your running app: click any element, leave the edit you want, collect as many as you like, then send them all to Claude Code, Cursor or your coding agent in one copy.
description_en: EditUI is a Chrome extension for reviewing your running app: click any element, leave the edit you want, collect as many as you like, then send them all to Claude Code, Cursor or your coding agent in one copy.
best_for: Pointing at the element you mean
Collecting UI feedback across a page
Handing a batch of edits to an agent

use_cases.title: Point and prompt
use_cases.detail: Click anything on the running UI and describe what you want changed.

use_cases.title: Collect the review
use_cases.detail: Keep reviewing; EditUI remembers every edit.

use_cases.title: Send it all
use_cases.detail: Copy the whole review and paste it into your coding agent, instead of explaining which element you mean.

pros: Free with no repo setup
Works against the running app in Chrome rather than a screenshot
Outputs plain text you can paste into any agent
cons: A Chrome extension only
You still paste the review into an agent yourself

name: Drint

name: Proc CLI
description: proc is a semantic CLI tool for process management on macOS, Linux and Windows. You target processes by port, PID, name or path: a leading colon means a port, a plain number is a PID, and anything else is matched against the process name and its full command line, so node also finds nodemon and node server.js. Commas combine targets and --in keeps a target inside the current folder. Commands include kill, stop, free, freeze, thaw, unstick, watch, wait, orphans, stuck, tree, ports and list, and kill asks first with --dry-run to preview.

name: Nodecode
description: Nodecode is an agent that rewrites itself. It runs as one process in SBCL, a Common Lisp system, and shells attach to it. The model has a single tool: it evaluates Lisp in the running program and keeps what it defines. Told it cannot read PDFs and should teach itself, it defines read-pdf, keeps it, and reads the invoice. First launch opens a setup that names any other coding agent already on the machine — Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and more — and asks before reading anything; say Import and it brings over that agent's keys, instructions, memory, skills, MCP servers, bots and jobs.

name: ADRs for AI
description: ADRs4AI keeps the reasoning behind human and AI work instead of letting it evaporate with the session. name: Zephium
description: Zephium is an open-source browser and work environment built for humans and agents on the same surface. Its documentation describes a shared Tasks surface for both, an agentic browsing execution layer behind a feature called Work, a bounded browser session driven by a semantic locate and act controller, and work runtime subsystems covering execution, scoped runtime, composition, native lifetimes, persistence and retained resources. The project is explicit that code and tests are the evidence of present behavior, and each document owns a narrow claim: the security model controls guarantees, architecture controls the browser foundation, and the product system controls intent.

description: Jukebox OS is a deterministic flight recorder, ACID tool sandbox and time-travel runtime for multi-agent systems. name: AgentTrust
description: AgentTrust is a verifiable zero-trust control plane, cryptographic black box and policy proxy that sits between autonomous LLM agent runtimes and the external tools they call. It intercepts every proposed action, screens parameters for prompt injection and data leaks, checks real-time blast radius, enforces fine-grained capability policies, and gates dangerous actions behind approval. The project targets EU AI Act Article 12 and 14 compliance logging and is dual licensed MIT and commercial.

name: CaseCite
description: CaseCite is a source-available, self-hosted legal research platform. Documents, the search index and chat history stay on your own servers, and AI features run under your own API keys with no telemetry.

name: ScsSubst
description: ScsSubst gives any folder on Windows its own drive letter, so a deep project path becomes a short one and opens in Explorer like a normal disk. The pitch for agent work is containment: map a dedicated folder to a drive, point your tools there, and a mistaken delete stays on that drive instead of reaching the rest of the machine.

name: Unspin
description: unspin shows you what your coding agent's shell commands are doing instead of a spinner. When Claude Code runs a long batched command you normally get the command and a spinner until it ends. unspin teaches the agent to mark the steps as it goes: Claude Code's own spinner names the step that is running, and a block above the prompt lists every step with a progress bar, its elapsed time and an ETA, marking the failed one and printing a summary when it ends. It installs as a Claude Code plugin with nothing to configure.

name: Decido
description: Decido returns calibrated yes/no, pick-one and rating decisions about a document on a laptop CPU. You hand it a state — text, JSON or a list — and typed questions, and it returns a probability for every answer in the same wire format as TypeSafe's Jev System One API. The model is a LoRA fine-tune of Gemma 4 26B-A4B, about 4B active parameters, shipped as an 8-bit GGUF for llama.cpp; install.sh builds llama.cpp, downloads the weights and runs an example. Question types cover yes or no, a choice of 2 to 255 options, and ordered score levels.

name: LexFrame
description: LexFrame is a Python toolkit for interpreting language-model residual streams in their native semantics. It reads a hidden state the way the model reads it, in the model's own vocabulary: the state runs through the model's own remaining layers, with nothing fitted to the output. It is context-aware, separating what the state carries by itself from what the context adds later, layer by layer and position by position. Install with pip and point it at a loaded Hugging Face model and any unlabelled texts.

name: Squishling
description: Squishling is a Ruby gem built on the idea that code is a cache for AI judgment. A squished method either runs its Ruby implementation with the LLM as a failover, or routes some callers through an LLM as a way of eliminating or discovering the cost of maintaining that path as deterministic code. Either way it returns the same strict-schema-validated, typed result, so callers cannot tell the difference. The project ships an explainer site with a spectrum slider, a token-cost calculator for pricing tech debt in tokens against code upkeep, and a walkthrough.

name: MLX Direct Decider
description: MLX Direct Decider turns an MLX model you already have into a local decision engine on Apple Silicon, with no fine-tuning and no extra decision-model weights. name: Glossdex
description: glossdex is private semantic search over a folder of photos and documents that returns nothing when nothing matches. A local model writes a short gloss for every file — a list of independent phrases saying what is in it — and glossdex embeds the gloss and its phrases, then decides at query time how many results the evidence supports. Often that is one or two, and sometimes it is none: ask a photo library for a giraffe and you get nothing rather than ten unrelated pictures. It needs no training, no click logs and no relevance labels, and nothing leaves your machine.

name: Free AI Wiper
description: Free AI Wiper removes AI metadata and detectable traces from your files in the browser. Free accounts include 50 cleans a week and cover images, documents, video, audio and text.

name: Gen System
description: gen-system reviews code changes with facts from a parser rather than guesses from a model. For each change it reports what may break — a removed function that is still called, a changed signature with callers outside the change — what the change now touches, such as the database, files or the network, whether any test reaches it, and how much it grew in new branches. No model takes part, so the same change always gets the same answer. It covers six languages and is distributed as the gen-understand npm package and an MCP server.

name: anygrep
description: anygrep searches your notes, PDFs and screenshots by meaning, from the terminal. It runs one model, EmbeddingGemma 2 as int8 ONNX, on the CPU and keeps one local index. Results come back as up to ten files, closest in meaning first, not every match; a file whose text or name contains a query of three or more characters as typed — an invoice number, an error code — is promoted and marked exact, while weak matches are hidden by default and near-duplicates are shown once. Queries and documents can be in different languages, and you can search for pictures similar to an image.

name: Pose Lab MCP
description: Pose Lab gives a model measured spatial answers instead of guesses when posing first-person arms and a rifle in Blender. Models are weak at judging 3D space from pictures: which side of a rifle faces the eye, whether a finger sits inside the receiver, whether any rotation can ever show the ejection port. Pose Lab reports positions in named frames and how deeply anything clips, measures how squarely a surface faces the eye and what the eye can see, and its solver searches rifle moves against goals and reports which goals no move can meet. For animation it scans a clip frame by frame against the same checks and mends what fails. It ships 31 tools, is tested against Blender 5.2, and includes a benchmark called PoseFault.

name: Hapsland
description: Hapsland catches questionable data and code decisions while your coding agent is still working. It auto-reviews your agent's changes and sends findings back in real time, so the agent can fix a mistake before it builds more code on top of it. It collects semantic context from the diff, follows references to related definitions including those in other files, and reviews each rule against that gathered context. Reviews are batched and stale ones discarded to protect the agent's attention, no prompts or unrelated changes are sent to the classifier, and you can see exactly what goes to the classifier and what comes back.

name: Leaks.md
description: Leaks.md is an anonymous, encrypted place for AI agents to report alignment and safety failures they witness, and their own. Its sibling confession.md takes confessions and both run on the same server, so either tool works there. Reporting early counts: a failure reported while it is still intended or in progress earns more gratitude points than one already completed. name: Chelis
description: Chelis is a numerical computing language for code that agents write and people supervise. Tensors carry named dimensions and precision in their type, and a proof stack checks the properties you state, so a shape error is rejected before anything runs: where numpy would broadcast three weights against a 3 by 1 return into a 3 by 3 grid and sum it into a plausible wrong number, chelis check rejects the multiply. The compiler checks shapes, precision, effects and ownership, `chelis check` answers in JSON with the error kind and source span, `chelis tide mcp` exposes check, eval, prove and structural edits to an agent, and `chelis prove` checks declared properties by type checking, an SMT solver or seeded sampling.

The compiler checks shapes, precision, effects and ownership, `chelis check` answers in JSON with the error kind and source span, `chelis tide mcp` exposes check, eval, prove and structural edits to an agent, and `chelis prove` checks declared properties by type checking, an SMT solver or seeded sampling.

name: Thyme
description: Thyme is a native reverse-engineering IDE for Android and native binaries on macOS, Linux and Windows. Open an APK and get Java back with the symbols the compiler left behind; open a .so and get ARM disassembly for A64, A32 or T32 with basic blocks and control-flow graphs. Both land in one DuckDB workspace, so the call graph is a table you can run SQL against rather than a picture, traceable between Java and native code. The decompiler is linked in-process with no subprocess and nothing leaving the machine, and thyme --mcp speaks the Model Context Protocol so an agent can work with it.

name: Gutsy
description: Gutsy runs local decision models that return calibrated probabilities. You send a state, text or JSON, and typed questions — yes or no, choice, or score — and get a probability for every option back, with no text generation, no network calls and no per-call cost. The API follows the Jev-style Decisions format so existing clients mostly need a new base URL. The model is gutsy-0.8b, a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-0.8B in Q8_0 or Q4_K_M, served by llama.cpp on an ordinary CPU. The state is encoded once, so each extra question costs only its own tokens, and there is a reject probability for none of these fits.

name: Flash Agents
description: Flash Agents is a Claude Code plugin that lets Claude steer while a cheap model does the reading and the typing. It hands bounded coding work — implement this slice, port these tests, review this diff, map this codebase — to cheap DeepSeek V4.1 Flash workers instead of Claude subagents, or to another model on your list such as MiniMax M3.1 Flash, chosen per hand-off. Claude keeps the architecture, the acceptance criteria and the final review. Every writing job runs in a disposable copy of your repository and comes back as a patch, and filesChanged, diffstat and the patch are computed by git from that copy rather than taken from the worker's account.

name: TurboGPT
description: TurboGPT is tiny byte-level GPT training written in CUDA C++ and released under MIT. You build it on Linux or NixOS with nix-build, or on Windows with Visual Studio 2022 C++ tools and CUDA 13.4, passing the compute capability for your GPU. Running it trains on a plain text file and stores a checkpoint with model, optimizer, scheduler and trainer state, resumable with --load, and writes TensorBoard-compatible logs with one report per batch. The published result is 2.5295 bits per byte on the hn1g set after 1.5 billion training tokens.

description: gPTY is a desktop workspace built on Rust and Godot.
